Every \(f\in E\) preserves each graded \(S_T\). To see this, expand its full cofree formula on the pullback along the cut shuffle. The two outer coactions of an element of \(S_T\) remain in the image of those coalgebra embeddings. Its middle Taylor value can be any element of the full central block \(sN\),so the reconstructed output is again in \(S_T\). Consequently restriction to \(U\) is an algebra homomorphism,and its kernel \(K\) is a two-sided graded ideal. It is \(\partial_b\)-stable,since \(d_bU\subset U\).

Let \(F^rE\) consist of endomorphisms whose central Taylor values are zero on every input of rank less than \(r\). Equivalently their full cofree formulas consume rank at least \(r\). A term of \(fg\) first consumes the piece used by \(g\),then the piece used by \(f\) in the remaining outside words. The ranks of these removed pieces add: IC letter counts add under cuts,and heights telescope along their actual endpoints. Therefore \[ F^rE\,F^sE\subset F^{r+s}E. \] This argument uses the entire signed cofree composition;its evaluation sign does not alter which outside pieces are consumed. In particular the graded commutator has the same filtration bound.

On Taylor maps \(\partial_{b,0}\) preserves rank,and \(\partial_b-\partial_{b,0}\) raises filtration by at least one. Indeed a remaining source pure operation reduces original IC count before Taylor evaluation. A target pure operation cannot contribute to the central projection from a nonempty outside output,because it is normalized. These account for all nonleading baseline terms.

The leading restriction kernel has the normalized contraction \(H_0\) proved in C.56.4.1. That proof uses the common cut decomposition of the two outside index runs,the acyclic nonretained summands,and the signed Hom contraction on the quotient. It applies here with the same central complex on source and target. It preserves rank and \(K\);hence on every homogeneous rank component of \(K\) we have \[ \partial_{b,0}H_0+H_0\partial_{b,0}=1. \]

The cut decomposition glues the prescribed central action values. Extend them on the remaining graded summands and reconstruct a full bicomodule map \(\mu^{(0)}\). Choose its bare central value zero. Thus \(\mu^{(0)}\in F^1E^1\),and its restrictions are exactly the prescribed maps. For any such extension set \[ F(\mu)=\partial_b\mu+\mu^2. \] Its restriction to \(U\) vanishes by the prescribed square-zero equations. Thus its curvature belongs to \(K^2\cap F^1E\).

Here is the full obstruction correction. Direct use of the graded Leibniz rule gives the Bianchi identity \[ \partial_b F(\mu)+\mu F(\mu)-F(\mu)\mu=0. \] In fact \(\partial_b(\mu^2)=(\partial_b\mu)\mu- \mu\partial_b\mu\);the two displayed commutator terms cancel these,and the two cubic terms cancel each other. No division or unproved deformation principle is used.

Suppose the current curvature has filtration at least \(r\ge1\). Write \(F_r\) for its exact rank-\(r\) Taylor component, extended by zero at other ranks and then by the cofree formula. Rank preservation of the cut projectors shows \(F_r\in K\). The commutator in the Bianchi identity has filtration at least \(r+1\), as does the nonleading part of \(\partial_bF\). Hence \(\partial_{b,0}F_r=0\). Put \[ \nu_r=-H_0F_r,\qquad \mu_{\rm new}=\mu+\nu_r. \] Then \(\nu_r\in K^1\cap F^rE\) and \(\partial_{b,0}\nu_r=-F_r\). Expanding the new curvature gives \[ \begin{aligned} F(\mu+\nu_r)&=F(\mu)+\partial_b\nu_r\\ &\quad+\mu\nu_r+\nu_r\mu+\nu_r^2. \end{aligned} \] The last three terms have filtration at least \(r+1\),as does \((\partial_b-\partial_{b,0})\nu_r\). Its exact rank-\(r\) part is therefore zero. The new curvature has filtration at least \(r+1\),and the prescribed action values are unchanged because \(\nu_r\) vanishes on \(U\).

Start with \(r=1\) and repeat. On a fixed original rank-\(R\) input no correction with \(r>R\) contributes. The cofree reconstruction at that input has finitely many outside cuts,so it too stabilizes. These stabilized values define a genuine global bicomodule map \(\mu\). Its curvature is zero on every original input,since the corresponding finite stage has already killed all ranks up to that input. Hence \((d_b+\mu)^2=0\). All corrections were in \(K\) and had positive consumption. The selected product actions,pure core differentials and bare central unary differential are therefore retained exactly. This proves the theorem. \(\square\)

C.57.2. Ordered root products can be constructed simultaneously

Fix a finite ordered list of root factors. Root \(i\) has input arity \(n_i\ge0\),one output core,and a finite directed parameter category \(I_i\). Its given one-cross module has the fixed pure cores and central space \(N_i\). For a nonempty consecutive block \(B\),use the literal tensor IC cores,the parameter category \(I_B=\prod_{i\in B}I_i\),and the central graded tensor \(N_B=\bigotimes_{i\in B}N_i\),with its tensor unary differential. The one-cross suspension is applied once after forming this ordinary tensor,as in C.41.2.1. Prescribe the singleton modules.

Theorem C.57.2.1 (ordered output-root induction on product domains). There exist full one-cross module structures for all nonempty consecutive blocks with these bare central and pure-core data,whose restriction to every ordered cut shuffle is exactly the ordered product of the corresponding block structures. This construction includes genuine zero-input root factors. It asserts product compatibility on the specified product parameter categories;it does not identify a general native grafting category with such a product.

Proof. Induct on the number of roots in a block. A singleton uses its prescribed structure. Suppose all shorter blocks have been done. For each proper cut of the current block,prescribe the product of its two shorter modules. Remove their individual cross shifts,tensor with the ordinary graded tensor rule,and restore one total cross shift. C.41.2.1 and C.52.3.1 prove that this gives a full cofree module along the actual outside shuffle coalgebra embeddings. Its differential squares to zero because the graded tensor differential does;the baseline restriction is the stated pure and central unary differential.

On the intersection of two cut images,the commuting-cut theorem gives the refined product domain. Restricting either prescribed two-block structure there invokes only previously constructed structures on shorter blocks. By the induction hypothesis they restrict to the same flat product on the refined blocks. This equality includes the full module actions:ordinary graded tensor regrouping has the same sign for either parenthesization,its pure cores regroup literally,and the one total cross shift is performed after that regrouping. Iterating the same argument proves compatibility on every finite refined cut.

Apply Theorem C.57.1.1 to these compatible positive-consumption action maps. It supplies the structure on the entire current block with all of its two-block restrictions fixed. Any finer cut factors through one of those cuts;the already imposed shorter-block restrictions identify it with the prescribed flat product too. This proves the inductive step and hence the assertion for all blocks in the finite list.

The source arity never enters the obstruction contraction or its rank decrease. A root with \(n_i=0\) has source IC tensor power \(C^{\otimes0}\),but still retains its index bar,output core and actual central mapping factor \(N_i\). It is not removed from the ordered list. This is exactly the zero-input convention of C.52.3.1. A genuinely empty output list is separate coefficient-unit data,not a missing zero-input root. \(\square\)

C.57.3. What comparison retains the native whole graph

Theorem C.57.3.1 (relative comparison and whole-path transport). Suppose an old full module structure on the same \(Z\) has the same pure cores and bare central differential as a newly constructed structure. Suppose on the finest product-shuffle domain there is an actual closed full comparison from the old restricted module to the new restricted module,with identity leading central term and identity pure cores. Then it extends to a global bicomodule chain isomorphism. For a whole directed path coalgebra,such isomorphisms on its one-cross sectors give a graded whole-path coalgebra isomorphism. Conjugating the whole differential retains every several-cross operation and its enhanced interpretation. This alone does not assert strict external grafting covariance in the new coordinates.

Proof. First every old module differential restricts to the graded finest shuffle pullback. Its pure coderivations retain that subcoalgebra; its nonunary module part is a bicomodule map over identity cores and preserves the pullback by Theorem C.57.1.1's cofree argument. The same is true of the new differential. Thus the given comparison has an actual chain domain and target.

Extend its central Taylor values graded-linearly and reconstruct a full map \(F_0\). The full comparison differential has the signed form \(\partial F=d_{\rm new}F-(-1)^{|F|}F d_{\rm old}\). Its restriction kernel is contracted exactly as in C.56.4.1:the leading quotient by the finest shuffle is acyclic at fixed outside rank;every omitted source or target module action consumes positive outside rank. That proof does not use equality of the old restricted nonunary action with a flat product action;it uses the chain property of that restriction and the strict rank decrease. Both were just checked. The corresponding full contraction \(H\) therefore corrects the closed degree-one defect by \(F=F_0-H\partial F_0\). This is a global chain comparison with the prescribed finest restriction.

The bare central block lies in the finest domain,so the correction has zero bare value. Consequently the leading central term remains the identity. Every other term of \(F-1\) consumes positive outside rank. The usual geometric inverse \(\sum_{j\ge0}(-1)^j(F-1)^j\) is finite on each original input and is a bicomodule inverse by the full cofree composition formula. The chain equation makes the inverse a chain map too.

For a path of several cross sectors,take the cotensor of these graded bicomodule isomorphisms over the common pure cores. Its inverse is the cotensor of their inverses. A path cut is either an outside core coaction or a cut between cross sectors. Bicomodule compatibility retains the former,and the literal cotensor factors retain the latter. Thus these maps,over the identity on pure sectors,form a graded whole-path coalgebra isomorphism \(G\),including all several-cross path sectors. Define \(D_{\rm new}=G D_{\rm old}G^{-1}\). Its square is zero and its coderivation identity follows by applying the coalgebra equations for \(G,G^{-1}\) to that for \(D_{\rm old}\). On a one-cross sector it is the prescribed new differential by the chain equation for \(F\);on a pure sector it is unchanged. No several-cross Taylor component has been discarded:all are transported by the displayed conjugation. The original interpretation transports through this actual coalgebra isomorphism.

External marks must also be transported on their actual domains. Their transported higher components need not be the strict external product formula even when their one-cross restrictions are products. Hence the full higher grafting equations still require proof before the marked-point descent can be applied. \(\square\)

C.57.4. Root components,including unit outputs

Fix an actual joint arrow \(f=(K,J')\) of C.47.2.1,with original source state \((t,J)\). Put \(I=\pi_K^{-1}(J')\). Write \(n=m_J\) for its source frontier length and \(m=m_I\) for its target frontier length before the canonical contraction relabelling. Retain the selected contraction labels throughout. At each root output of the actual partial forest \(F^t_{I,J}\),take its component between the two frontiers. Include a surviving old frontier edge as an identity component. Denote the ordered components by \(F_1,\ldots,F_m\),and their source block lengths by \(n_1,\ldots,n_m\).

Theorem C.57.4.1 (native rootwise central tensor). Each source frontier variable occurs in exactly one component,with its original order. Thus \(n_i\ge0\),\(\sum_i n_i=n\),and the blocks are consecutive, allowing empty blocks. After the canonical frontier relabelling,the actual native functor is the ordered external product of these root functors. For selected IC tuples \(x,y\),its represented mapping cohomology consequently has the actual identification \[ \begin{aligned} N_f(y,x) &:=H^\bullet\operatorname{RHom} (F^t_{I,J}x,y)\\ &\cong\bigotimes_{i=1}^m H^\bullet\operatorname{RHom} (F_i x_{B_i},y_i). \end{aligned} \] It is nonnegative,even and degreewise finite on the finite forward corners. These are the same central graded tensor spaces used by the output-root induction. A zero-input component retains its full output mapping space;an identity component retains its full mapping space too.

Proof. Traverse the original planar tree,stopping at the frontier of \(I\). Below one such stopped output,traverse only until the frontier of \(J\). Since \(J\subseteq I\) are descendant-closed ideals,all operations between those frontiers belong to that one component. A frontier edge of \(J\) has exactly one first ancestor in the stopped \(I\)-frontier,or is itself the surviving stopped edge. It therefore belongs to exactly one component. Planar traversal makes each such set consecutive in the source list and preserves the order of the components. A newly executed nullary subtree can have no old frontier input;it still has its stopped output. This proves all the block assertions,including empty blocks and identity strands.

The native partial functor of C.44.3.1 is defined by evaluating these components independently and taking their ordered external product. Its enhanced geometric interpretation is the common expanded-chain construction in that proof,with the actual unit object at a nullary input and the actual identity correspondence at an identity strand. C.47.2.1 supplies the canonical output frontier bijection for the selected contraction \(K\). This bijection retains all tuple factors and their order. Composing with it gives the stated product functor for \(f\). This retains the original contraction label even if a different label gives an isomorphic underlying forest. No parallel arrows have been identified.

Choose the external-product strict enhancement of this fixed forest functor. Its target tensor category has by definition the ordinary graded tensor of its mapping complexes. If a root image is a finite additive IC sum,use its actual finite multiplicity matrix. Distributing those finite sums identifies the full represented complex with \[ \bigotimes_i\operatorname{RHom}(F_i x_{B_i},y_i). \] The original enhanced forest comparison transports this represented complex to that of \(f\),rather than asserting equality merely from matching dimensions.

For completeness,the tensor cohomology identification is the split complex calculation used in C.33.1.1. Split each factor over the field as its cohomology representatives plus a contractible complex. The finite tensor expands into the all-cohomology summand and summands with at least one contractible factor. Contract the first such factor with the ordinary tensor degree sign;the differentials on later factors cancel in the contraction identity. Each of those summands is contractible. Inclusion of the representatives therefore gives precisely the displayed Künneth isomorphism. The isomorphism on cohomology is the tensor of the actual represented comparison,so it has the required geometric provenance.

Every \(F_i x_{B_i}\) is a finite additive IC sum by C.47.2.1's forward-corner construction. C.33.1.1 proves nonnegative,even and degreewise finite mapping cohomology for those generators. Finite sums and finite tensors preserve those assertions;in a fixed degree only finitely many tuples of nonnegative factor degrees contribute.

If \(n_i=0\),the input is the coefficient object,but its output is the actual nullary forest value,canonically identified with \(IC_0\) by C.44.3.1. The corresponding factor is \(H^\bullet\operatorname{RHom}(IC_0,y_i)\),which need not be the coefficient field. If the component is an identity strand,the factor is \(H^\bullet\operatorname{RHom}(x_i,y_i)\),also retained in full. Hence neither case permits deletion of an output mapping factor. Finally the source pure core regroups as \(C^{\otimes n}=\bigotimes_iC^{\otimes n_i}\),and the target as \(C^{\otimes m}=\bigotimes_iC\). The ordinary central tensor therefore has exactly the graded root data required by the preceding output-root induction. \(\square\)

If the output frontier is empty,no operation has an executed output. Thus both ideals are empty and both frontier lengths are zero. The underlying partial functor is the coefficient identity,with empty central tensor equal to the coefficient field;its contraction-arrow label is still retained.

C.57.5. Two solved root/action examples

Exercise C.57.5.1 (nonlinear curvature; advanced). Let \(V\) have basis \(x\) in degree minus one,\(y,u\) in degree zero,and \(v\) in degree one. Put \(d_0x=y,d_0u=v\). The normalized contraction is \(h_0y=x,h_0v=u\),zero otherwise. In the formal filtration \(t^r\operatorname{End}(V)[[t]]\), fix \(kv\) with its zero differential. Let \[ \begin{aligned} \delta_1(x)&=u,&\delta_1(y)&=-v,\\ \delta_1(u)&=v,&\delta_1(v)&=0. \end{aligned} \] Verify that the initial action is closed,compute its curvature,and apply the relative obstruction correction to determine the full formal differential. Use the normalized endomorphism contraction specified below.

Solution. This degree-one map is \(\partial_0\)-closed,but \(\delta_1^2(x)=v\ne0\). Thus its linear chain equation is insufficient for a module differential. On maps vanishing on \(v\), postcomposition \(H_0(f)=h_0f\) is a normalized contraction of the endomorphism differential. Indeed the two source-composition terms in \(\partial_0H_0+H_0\partial_0\) cancel,and the remainder is \((d_0h_0+h_0d_0)f=f\). It preserves that relative kernel.

Start with \(\mu=t\delta_1\). Its curvature is the nonzero term \(t^2(x\mapsto v)\). The first correction is \(-t^2(x\mapsto u)\). At the next order the curvature is \(-t^3(x\mapsto v)\),so the next correction is \(+t^3(x\mapsto u)\). Inductively at every order \(r\ge2\) the correction on \(x\) is \((-1)^{r-1}t^ru\), zero on the other basis vectors. Therefore the resulting formal differential has the exact formula \[ \begin{aligned} Dx&=y+\frac{t}{1+t}u,&Dy&=-tv,\\ Du&=(1+t)v,&Dv&=0. \end{aligned} \] Its square on \(x\) is \(-tv+\frac{t}{1+t}(1+t)v=0\);its square is zero on the other basis vectors too. Each finite \(t\)-adic window uses only finitely many of the displayed corrections. This is a formal filtered algebra diagnostic of the nonlinear induction,not a claim that the finite complex is a native IC module or an original-word rank window.

Exercise C.57.5.2 (unit,convolution and identity roots; intermediate). Take an unexecuted ternary parent with three ordered branches:a nullary operation \(u\),a binary operation \(b\) with external inputs \(x_1,x_2\),and an external input \(x_3\). Execute \(u,b\) and leave the parent unexecuted. Determine the two frontiers,the ordered root input lengths,the represented central cohomology and the one-cross degree. Explain which mapping factors remain.

Solution. The initial frontier is \((x_1,x_2,x_3)\),and the new frontier is \((IC_0,x_1*x_2,x_3)\). Its ordered root input lengths are \((0,2,1)\). On a target tuple \((y_1,y_2,y_3)\),the central cohomology is \[ \begin{aligned} &H^\bullet\operatorname{RHom}(IC_0,y_1)\\ &\quad\otimes H^\bullet\operatorname{RHom}(x_1*x_2,y_2)\\ &\quad\otimes H^\bullet\operatorname{RHom}(x_3,y_3). \end{aligned} \] The first and third factors remain present. For homogeneous central degrees \(d_1,d_2,d_3\),the corresponding one-cross degree is \(d_1+d_2+d_3-1\). Indeed C.41.2.1 removes the three individual cross shifts before tensoring and then restores one shift. Tensoring three suspended central letters directly would incorrectly give \(d_1+d_2+d_3-3\).

For a genuinely rootwise product parameter family,the same calculation applies at every original endpoint tuple,with all parallel arrow labels retained. It supplies the graded central identifications there. It does not prove that an independently transferred differential restricts to the desired product differential. The actual closed comparison on the finest shuffle domain and compatibility across complete native grafting domains remain the next required checks.

Theorems C.57.1.1–C.57.3.1 construct relative module actions,ordered products and conditional whole-path transport. Theorem C.57.4.1 identifies the actual native graded central tensor. Exercises C.57.5.1–C.57.5.2 compute the curvature correction and the zero-input/identity root factors. Editable SVG source.

C.58. The actual finest product comparison

The whole native product family and its independent root models project to one common dg target. The projection square with the finest shuffle commutes on the actual cobar generators. Full represented evaluation of the supplied native comparison,combined with the fixed projection contractions,gives a module comparison with its precise leading calibration. Both actions and all higher source components remain in the construction. The product domains here retain their stated scope; compatibility across general native overlaps and higher grafting equations remains to be established.

C.58.1. The strict common projection square

Put \(U=\Omega C\). For root factors \(i=1,\ldots,m\),let \(n_i\ge0\),\(I=\prod_iI_i\),and \(n=\sum_i n_i\). Write \[ \begin{aligned} A_i&=C^{\otimes n_i}\otimes D_{I_i},\\ B_i&=C\otimes D_{I_i},\\ A_\otimes&=\bigotimes_iA_i,\\ B_\otimes&=\bigotimes_iB_i,\\ A_I&=C^{\otimes n}\otimes D_I,\\ B_I&=C^{\otimes m}\otimes D_I. \end{aligned} \] The actual coalgebra embeddings \(j_A:A_\otimes\to A_I\),\(j_B:B_\otimes\to B_I\) first regroup the IC and index factors with the Koszul sign,then shuffle the index bars. Let \(\kappa_A,\kappa_B\) be the C41 cobar projections onto the tensor of the factor cobars. The C52 maps \(\rho_{r,J}\) have target \(U^{\otimes r}\otimes kJ\). Use the canonical ordered identification \(\bigotimes_i(U\otimes kI_i)=U^{\otimes m}\otimes kI\).

Lemma C.58.1.1 (exact projection and shuffle compatibility). We have the literal dg functor identities \[ \begin{aligned} &\rho_{n,I}\Omega j_A\\ &\quad=\left(\bigotimes_i\rho_{n_i,I_i}\right)\kappa_A,\\ &\rho_{m,I}\Omega j_B\\ &\quad=\left(\bigotimes_i\rho_{1,I_i}\right)\kappa_B. \end{aligned} \] All objects and parallel index arrows are retained. Each side is a graded-surjective mapping quasi-isomorphism. The identities also commute with the prescribed common core powers of \(g\).

Proof. The cobars are free on their reduced coalgebra generators, so it suffices to compare their actual generator images. Recall the C52 formula \(\rho=\epsilon\Omega\operatorname{sh} (\bigotimes\eta_C\otimes1)\). Its twisting projection has a nonzero value only in the following two cases. One IC factor is reduced and every other factor,including the index bar,is coaugmented;its value is the same generator of that \(\Omega C\) factor. Or all IC factors are coaugmented and the index bar is one actual arrow; its value is that arrow with the scalar IC identities. An index word of length at least two has zero value. A generator with both an IC input and a nonempty index input has zero value,as does one with two reduced IC factors:the shuffled target bar then has at least two letters,which the counit twisting projection kills. These statements include a reduced IC coalgebra element of any primitive length;its one-letter bar-unit component is the corresponding cobar generator.

On the right,\(\kappa\) kills a generator with two noncoaugmented root factors. On a generator supported in one root factor it retains exactly that factor and then applies its \(\rho\). On the left, two reduced IC factors are killed as just described. A reduced IC factor together with any nonempty index factor is killed too. If only index factors are nonempty,their shuffle has total index length equal to the sum of those lengths;two or more such letters are killed. If just one root factor is noncoaugmented,the only surviving possibilities are precisely that factor's single IC generator or its single actual index arrow. Both sides have the same value there. The factor regrouping sign is one on these surviving single-factor inputs;all other signed terms map to zero. This proves both exact identities.

The coaugmentations give the same object identities on both sides. The one-arrow case retains its actual parallel-arrow label and embeds it with identities in the other index coordinates. At \(n_i=0\) there is simply no reduced IC generator in that source factor;its index-arrow case remains unchanged. Thus the proof includes zero-input roots and all empty outside words.

C.52.2.1 proves that each \(\rho\) is graded-surjective and a mapping quasi-isomorphism. C.52.3.1 proves the same for \(\kappa\). Finite tensors over the field preserve surjectivity and quasi-isomorphism, by the split tensor calculation. Their displayed composites therefore have the asserted property. In particular,\(\Omega j\) is itself a mapping quasi-isomorphism by two out of three,since the global \(\rho\) is one too. All these object maps are the same tuple maps.

For a normalized common core map \(g\),C.52.2.1 gives strict naturality of \(\rho\),C.41.1.1 gives strict naturality of \(\kappa\),and the index shuffle is the identity on IC factors. The resulting two composites on each generator coincide. Hence the identities commute with the literal prescribed powers of \(g\), not with independently chosen maps at different arities. \(\square\)

C.58.2. An actual full represented comparison on the finest domain

Fix a native rootwise product family from C44/C47 on these independent parameter categories,with its actual enhanced external-product comparison on all parameter cells. Take the strict native representatives of C.52.3.1,including their comparison through the canonical common-cobar units and target projections: \[ \begin{aligned} F&:\Omega A_I\to\operatorname{Add}(\Omega B_I),\\ F_i&:\Omega A_i\to\operatorname{Add}(\Omega B_i). \end{aligned} \] Here \(F\) represents that entire native product family,not an unrelated functor with the same cohomology. Retain these representing comparisons as part of the data supplied by the lift. Set \[ \begin{aligned} T&=\bigotimes_i(U\otimes kI_i),\\ P&=(\bigotimes_iF_i)\kappa_A,\\ p_B&=(\bigotimes_i\rho_{1,I_i})\kappa_B,\\ f_0&=\rho_{m,I}F\Omega j_A,\\ f_1&=(\bigotimes_i\rho_{1,I_i})P. \end{aligned} \] The two functors \(f_0,f_1\) have the same strict source \(\Omega A_\otimes\) and target \(\operatorname{Add}(T)\).

Theorem C.58.2.1 (native finest comparison with its actual source and target). The supplied whole native external-product comparison gives a closed full bicomodule comparison between the old minimal module restricted along \(j_A,j_B\) and the finest product of the singleton minimal modules. Under C.57.4.1's actual rootwise cohomology identification, its bare central component is the identity. It is over identity pure cores and has its finite bicomodule inverse. Thus it supplies C.57.3.1's finest-domain hypothesis for this specified native product family.

Proof. We first specify the actual full natural transformation used in the construction. The original native family has the enhanced external-product comparison of C.44.3.1/C.47.2.1. The chosen native lifts come with their representing comparisons through the canonical bar-cobar units and counits,as in C.52.3.1. Transport that original comparison through these particular equivalences. Orient it as \(\beta:f_1\Rightarrow f_0\). More explicitly,if \(c_i\) denotes the representing equivalence from the interpretation of \(f_i\) to its native family,and \(\alpha\) is the original comparison from the product family to the whole family,then its full enhanced expression is \(c_0^{-1}\alpha c_1\). The inverses and their coherent unit maps are those of the actual representing equivalences;the canonical bar-cobar equivalences and their homotopies were proved in C39 and retained by C52. This defines all its higher components,not only an objectwise isomorphism.

Apply the normalized source bar construction of C.33.2.1 to that whole diagram. On every source bar word it records the corresponding full component of \(c_0^{-1}\alpha c_1\),with its consecutive-block composition. Its differential is zero by the full transformation identity. Thus \(\beta\) is an actual closed full transformation in the common-source model;no assumption that natural-transformation spaces are contractible is being used. Its inverse and its two composition homotopies are recorded from the same supplied native diagram. All parameter components of the original comparison remain present in this construction.

Use three full represented raw modules over the identical outside cores \(B_\otimes,A_\otimes\). Their central complexes are \[ \begin{aligned} &M_0(y,x)\\ &\quad=\operatorname{Hom}_{\Omega B_I}(F\Omega j_Ax,\Omega j_By),\\ &M_\Pi(y,x)\\ &\quad=\operatorname{Hom}_{\otimes_i\Omega B_i}(Px,\kappa_By),\\ &Q_a(y,x)\\ &\quad=\operatorname{Hom}_{T}(f_ax,p_By),\quad a=0,1. \end{aligned} \] Write \(Y_0,Y_\Pi,Y_{Q_0},Y_{Q_1}\) for their common-core one-cross modules,with one total cross suspension. Naturality of the canonical coalgebra unit identifies \(Y_0\) with the actual \((j_B,j_A)\)-pullback of the original raw global module. It is not a separately selected module on the same graded ranks.

Postcomposition by \(\rho_{m,I}\) and by \(\bigotimes_i\rho_{1,I_i}\) gives respectively \[ \phi_0:Y_0\to Y_{Q_0},\qquad \phi_\Pi:Y_\Pi\to Y_{Q_1}. \] These are full chain bicomodule maps over identity cores. For the left action the exact square is \(\rho_{m,I}\Omega j_B=p_B\),proved in Lemma C.58.1.1;for the right action it is precisely the displayed definitions of \(f_0,f_1\). Multiplicativity of the target dg projections then proves both full represented action equations. The cofree formulas retain their higher terms. Their central maps are graded-surjective quasi-isomorphisms by Lemma C.58.1.1 and C52;finite additive images cause only finite mapping matrices.

C.45.2.1 therefore gives a full fixed-projection chain section \(\sigma_\Pi:Y_{Q_1}\to Y_\Pi\),including its complete normalized kernel homotopy. C.53.1.1 evaluates the full degree-zero \(\beta:f_1\Rightarrow f_0\) in the contravariant direction: \[ R_\beta:Y_{Q_0}\longrightarrow Y_{Q_1}. \] At bare central level it is \(m\mapsto m\beta\). On each source word it uses the full transformation component and reconstructs the outside coactions. That lemma proves its complete chain and bicomodule identities. Degree zero introduces neither an opposite composition sign nor a cross-shift sign. In particular,this map is not obtained by ignoring the source or target action differential.

Let \(I_0\) be the old minimal module's actual inclusion into \(Y_0\). It is obtained by restricting the chosen global minimal contraction along \(j_A,j_B\). This restriction retains the full contraction identities:the maps are bicomodule maps over identity cores,and the finest pullback contains their full central spaces,so their cofree formulas preserve it,as proved in C.57.1.1. Let \(P_\Pi:Y_\Pi\to Z_\Pi\) be the tensor product of the actual singleton minimal projections,with the C41 regrouping and one total cross suspension. It is a full chain bicomodule map by C.41.2.1.

The required comparison is the now fully typed composite \[ F_{\rm fine}=P_\Pi\sigma_\Pi R_\beta\phi_0 I_0. \] Every arrow is a full chain bicomodule map over the same identity cores,so this composite is one too. On cohomology,\(I_0,P_\Pi\) are the chosen identity-calibrated minimal maps,\(\phi_0\) is the actual common target projection,and \(\sigma_\Pi\) induces the inverse of \(\phi_\Pi\). The remaining map is the original rootwise represented comparison \(R_\beta\). These are precisely the represented comparison and tensor Künneth maps used in C.57.4.1's native central identification. Hence the bare central component of \(F_{\rm fine}\),between those minimal cohomology spaces,is the identity,not merely an unspecified isomorphism of equal dimensions.

Its remaining cofree Taylor terms consume positive outside rank,so the triangular inverse is finite on each original input by the indexed finite inverse proof in C.57.3.1. It is a chain inverse by the original chain equation. This constructs the actual finest-domain comparison required by C.57.3.1 for the specified product family. That theorem extends it to a global module isomorphism and transports the whole path differential. It still does not impose strict higher external grafting equations,identify an unsafe clipped product domain,or supply the full marked descent point. \(\square\)

C.58.3. Two solved comparison examples

Exercise C.58.3.1 (mixed generator and retained arrow; intermediate). Take \(I_1=I_2=[1]\) and no IC inputs. Let \(a,b\) be their actual index arrows. In \(\Omega(D_{I_1}\otimes D_{I_2})\), consider the mixed generator \(t(sa\otimes sb)\). Compute both routes of Lemma C.58.1.1 on it. Then compute the images of the two composable single-factor cobar words around the square. Explain why killing the mixed generator does not discard the mixed index arrow.

Solution. All suspended index arrows are odd. In target-to-source order the shuffle is \[ \begin{aligned} j(sa\otimes sb)&=sA_{\rm top}\mid sB_{\rm left}\\ &\quad-sB_{\rm right}\mid sA_{\rm bottom}. \end{aligned} \] Both terms have bar length two,so the global counit twisting projection kills their cobar generators. The other route first applies \(\kappa\), which kills a generator supported in two noncoaugmented factors. Both routes therefore give zero. Its degree is minus one,as each suspension has degree minus one and the cobar generator raises degree by one.

The individual cobar generators \(t(sA),t(sB)\) have degree zero. Both composable words \[ \begin{gathered} t(sA_{\rm top})t(sB_{\rm left}),\\ t(sB_{\rm right})t(sA_{\rm bottom}) \end{gathered} \] map to the same actual arrow \(00\to11\),whose tensor-coordinate value is \(a\otimes b\). The two coordinate compositions agree in the ordinary product category,with no extra sign since these cobar generators have degree zero. Thus the negative-degree mixed generator has zero projection while the genuine mixed endpoint arrow remains the nonzero product of the two retained single-factor arrows.

Exercise C.58.3.2 (full bimodule comparison; advanced). Work with the ordinary unsuspended cofree module,restoring the single cross shift afterwards as in C41. Let the left algebra be \(k[z]/z^2\),acting on its own coefficient factor,and the right algebra \(k[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2\). Let the remaining central complex have \(e,y\) in degree zero and \(f\) in degree minus one,with \(df=y\). In the old module the right \(\epsilon\) action is zero;in the new one it is \(T(e)=y,T(f)=T(y)=0\). Put \(K(e)=f,K(f)=K(y)=0\). Then \(T=dK+Kd\),\(T^2=K^2=TK=KT=0\),and every map is linear over the left coefficient algebra.

Denote a basis word by \((p,r,v,q)\),where \(p\) is its left \(sz\)-word length,\(r=0,1\) is its central coefficient power of \(z\),\(v=e,f,y\),and \(q\) is its right \(s\epsilon\)-word length. The full differential has the central term \((-1)^p(p,r,dv,q)\),the left action term \((-1)^p(p-1,r+1,v,q)\) when \(p>0,r=0\),and the new right term \((-1)^{p+|v|}(p,r,Tv,q-1)\) when \(q>0\). Terms with zero displayed central value are omitted. The pure bar differentials vanish since \(z^2=\epsilon^2=0\).

Verify the square-zero equations and construct an invertible full comparison over the identity outside cores. Check both actions and coactions,and show explicitly where its higher Taylor component is necessary. This algebraic example is separate from the positive IC cores in the native theorem.

Solution. These differentials square to zero. The central and left terms cancel in pairs because the left action commutes with \(d\) and reducing \(p\) reverses the central differential sign. The central and right terms cancel because \(T\) is a chain map and \(d\) changes \(|v|\) by one. The left and right terms cancel by their respective coefficients \((-1)^{|v|-1}\) and \((-1)^{|v|}\),since \(zT=Tz\). The repeated left and repeated right terms vanish by \(z^2=T^2=0\). These exhaust the terms of the square.

The degree-zero full comparison is \[ \begin{aligned} F(p,r,v,q)&=(p,r,v,q)\\ &\quad+(-1)^{|v|+1}(p,r,Kv,q-1) \end{aligned} \] when \(q>0\),with only its first term when \(q=0\). The extra term is a genuine Taylor component. In its chain equation, the one-letter coefficient is \((-1)^{p+|v|}(T-dK-Kd)v=0\);the two-letter coefficient is zero by \(TK=0\). Its left action equation holds because \(K\) commutes with that action. The inverse changes the sign of the extra term,since \(K^2=0\). The two outside coactions cut the left and right words. On the right,a term consuming one letter can be followed by exactly the cuts leaving that letter in the module piece;on the left all cuts remain available. Thus its full coaction equations hold too.

For instance,\(F(e\mid s\epsilon)=e\mid s\epsilon-f\), and the new differential of this word is \(y-df=0\),matching the old differential before applying \(F\). The bare identity alone would instead give \(y\ne0\).

Lemma C.58.1.1 proves the exact common projection square. Theorem C.58.2.1 constructs the actual finest comparison on the stated native rootwise product families. Exercises C.58.3.1–C.58.3.2 retain the genuine mixed endpoint arrow and the nonzero higher full module comparison. Editable SVG source.

C.59. Full projection homotopies and simultaneous cut normalization

The comparison through represented projections has four homotopy terms. The source and target projection squares and the original monoidal cell each contribute,and the fixed kernel homotopy contributes as well. After the actual minimal contractions,the resulting finest primitive extends to compatible comparisons on all ordered cuts. The formulas retain every action term and prescribed pure core map. Their global native use requires the displayed full cells on their complete domains.

C.59.1. The four-term homotopy between represented projection roofs

Use full chain bicomodule maps of degree zero with these types: \[ \begin{aligned} a&:Z\to Q_0,&a'&:Z'\to Q_0',\\ b&:W\to Q_1,&b'&:W'\to Q_1',\\ s&:Q_1\to W,&s'&:Q_1'\to W',\\ B&:Q_0\to Q_1,&B'&:Q_0'\to Q_1',\\ t&:Z\to Z',&u&:W\to W',\\ t_0&:Q_0\to Q_0',&t_1&:Q_1\to Q_1'. \end{aligned} \] Here \(b s=1,b's'=1\),and the actual fixed-projection target homotopy satisfies \(\partial H'=1-s'b'\). Assume the actual specified degree-minus-one homotopies have the types and equations \[ \begin{aligned} A_0 &:Z\to Q_0',&\partial A_0&=a't-t_0a,\\ A_1 &:W\to Q_1',&\partial A_1&=b'u-t_1b,\\ C &:Q_0\to Q_1',&\partial C&=B't_0-t_1B. \end{aligned} \] All composites use the same prescribed source-to-target core powers; the projections,sections and homotopies within a side are over identity cores. Set \(\phi=sBa\) and \(\phi'=s'B'a'\).

Theorem C.59.1.1 (the complete projection-roof square homotopy). An actual full homotopy \(\partial R=\phi't-u\phi\) is \[ \begin{aligned} R&=s'Ca+s'B'A_0\\ &\quad-H'u sBa-s'A_1sBa. \end{aligned} \] It retains all stated face restrictions. In general none of its four terms can be omitted,even if every leading cohomology map is the identity.

Proof. The Hom differential is a graded derivation,and all factors other than \(C,A_0,H',A_1\) are closed of degree zero. In particular \[ \begin{aligned} \partial(H'us)&=(1-s'b')us\\ &=us-s't_1-s'(\partial A_1)s, \end{aligned} \] using \(b'u=t_1b+\partial A_1\) and \(bs=1\). Consequently \(us-s't_1=\partial(H'us+s'A_1s)\). Also \[ \begin{aligned} \phi't &=s'B't_0a+\partial(s'B'A_0),\\ s'(B't_0-t_1B)a&=\partial(s'Ca). \end{aligned} \] Subtract \(u\phi=usBa\) from the first equality,insert the second equality,and replace \(us-s't_1\) by the primitive just computed. This gives exactly the displayed four-term formula,including the minus sign on its \(A_1\) term. It is an equation in the full mapping complex,so every composed map retains both bicomodule coaction equations and all its source and target actions.

Restriction to any parameter face commutes with these same composites. Thus compatible specified input data give that identical restricted homotopy. No homotopy inverse has been substituted without its kernel homotopy. The example below has four independent nonzero boundaries, proving the non-omission assertion. \(\square\)

C.59.2. The primitive on the normalized finest models

Use the actual full contractions \[ \begin{aligned} (i,p,h)&:Z\rightleftarrows N,\\ (i',p',h')&:Z'\rightleftarrows N',\\ (j,q,k)&:W\rightleftarrows P,\\ (j',q',k')&:W'\rightleftarrows P'. \end{aligned} \] Put \(T=p'ti,U=q'uj,J=q\phi i,J'=q'\phi'i'\),and assume \(J,J'\) are closed and invertible. In the native application these are the actual identity-leading isomorphisms of C58. The normalized global comparison restricted to the finest domain is \(T_*=J'TJ^{-1}:P\to P'\).

Corollary C.59.2.1 (a finest primitive with every contraction term). For the actual roof homotopy \(R\) of Theorem C.59.1.1,set \[ \begin{aligned} L&=q'Ri-q'\phi'h'ti\\ &\quad+q'uk\phi i,\\ K_*&=-LJ^{-1}. \end{aligned} \] Then \(\partial K_*=U-T_*\). In particular a fully recorded raw monoidal square gives the finest primitive needed for simultaneous ordered-cut normalization,without discarding any projection or minimal contraction term.

Proof. C.51.1.1's full calculation gives \(\partial L=J'T-UJ\). Its hypotheses are precisely the four contractions above and \(\partial R=\phi't-u\phi\),proved in Theorem C.59.1.1. Since \(J^{-1}\) is a closed degree-zero full map, \[ \begin{aligned} \partial(-LJ^{-1})&=-(J'T-UJ)J^{-1}\\ &=U-J'TJ^{-1}. \end{aligned} \] This is the stated sign and type. The inverse is the actual indexed cofree inverse of C.57.3.1/C.58.2.1. Its restriction to a face is the inverse of the restricted map by the two inverse identities,so every compatible face in the given data is retained. \(\square\)

C.59.3. One finest primitive suffices for all ordered cuts

Let \(Z,Z'\) be the product-normalized common-core module models of C57,with minimal nonnegative even central spaces. Let \(T:Z\to Z'\) be an actual full chain isomorphism over the prescribed invertible core powers. On a nonempty finite family of ordered cut domains \(S_c\), prescribe closed full comparisons \(F_c\),with the same bare identity and core powers. Suppose these agree on all refined intersections. Their common restriction to the finest product domain is \(F_*\). Let an actual full homotopy \(K_*\) be given there with \(\partial K_*=F_*-T|_*\). This is exactly the primitive produced by Corollary C.59.2.1 when its raw diagrams are the supplied native ones.

Theorem C.59.3.1 (simultaneous normalization from the finest domain). There is an actual full degree-minus-one bicomodule map \(K:Z\to Z'\) such that \(T^{\rm new}=T+\partial K\) restricts to every \(F_c\). It is an identity-leading chain isomorphism over the same pure core powers. One can retain the specified \(K_*\) while gluing. For compatible complete whole-graph sector data,C.51.3.1 implements this change in the whole graph without dropping several-cross components.

Proof. Within one \(S_c\),the closed difference \(L_c=F_c-T|_{S_c}\) has primitive \(K_*\) on its finest shuffle domain. The relative full Taylor-kernel contraction of C.56.4.1 applies inside \(S_c\),with its refined factor bars. The original cut embedding and its finest refinement are actual chain submodels of the product-normalized module;the omitted action terms consume positive outside rank. Thus C.56.5.1 extends \(K_*\) to a full primitive \(K_c\) of \(L_c\) on \(S_c\).

The prescribed differences \(L_c\) agree on their intersections, since all \(F_c\) do. C.56.6.1 therefore adjusts the \(K_c\) by closed full maps to make them agree on the whole finite cut union. Here the specified finest primitive can also be kept. Indeed,when the next domain meets the previously assigned union,the closed difference of its two homotopies vanishes on the finest domain:both were equal to \(K_*\) there. Closed-map extension from that intersection retains its zero finest value,because the finest domain is already contained in the prescribed intersection. Thus adding this correction does not alter \(K_*\). Induction glues all the homotopies while keeping the earlier domains and that finest value fixed.

Their common central Taylor map on the actual sum extends graded-linearly to \(Z\),using the common cut decomposition of C.56.1.1. Apply the full cofree formula along the prescribed outside core powers to obtain \(K\). It retains every assigned \(K_c\). No equation \(\partial K=L\) outside the union is required:define \(T^{\rm new}=T+\partial K\). It is closed because \(\partial T=0\) and \(\partial^2=0\),and on each cut its restriction is \(T|_{S_c}+L_c=F_c\). This construction uses the full differential and the actual sum,not a termwise extension across independently selected shuffle words.

The bare central value is the prescribed identity,as every cut contains that block. The usual cofree inverse is finite on each original input. Furthermore \(K\)'s bare central value is zero by even central parity: a degree-minus-one map cannot take a bare even unsuspended mapping degree to another such degree. Therefore the genuine whole-graph gauge theorem C.51.3.1 applies whenever these sector homotopies are compatible on the complete assigned face/string overlaps. It retains all higher-cross terms. Compatibility across additional native overlaps and external grafting marks is still a separate obligation, not a conclusion from this single module statement. \(\square\)

When \(F_c\) are products of already normalized smaller-root comparisons,their refined-intersection compatibility follows from that ordered root induction and the single final cross-shift rule of C41. The new theorem reduces all coarse-cut primitive choices to the one actual finest primitive. Applying it to the full native diagram still requires recording \(A_0,A_1,C\) from its entire projection and monoidal cells,with the fixed core powers and complete domains. These data must not be replaced by equality of first cohomology maps.

C.59.4. Two solved homotopy examples

Exercise C.59.4.1 (four necessary terms; advanced). Let \(V\) have the cycle \(e\) in degree zero and three acyclic pairs \(f_i\) in degree minus one,\(y_i\) in degree zero, with \(df_i=y_i\). Take \(Z=Z'=Q_0=Q_0'=Q_1=Q_1'=V\). Let \(W=W'=V\oplus K\),where \(K=(kg\to kz)\), \(|g|=-1,|z|=0,dg=z\). Let \(a,a',B,B'\) be identities, \(b,b'\) the projection onto \(V\),and \(s,s'\) its standard inclusion. Set \(H'(z)=g\),zero on all other basis vectors.

Define \(C(e)=f_1,A_0(e)=f_2\),zero elsewhere,and let \(A_1:W\to V\) send \(e\) to \(f_3\),zero elsewhere. Put \(t_1=1,t_0=1+\partial C,t=t_0+\partial A_0\). Let \(u\) act as the identity except that \(u(e)=e+y_3+z\). Check all three projection-square homotopy equations and compute the four terms of the full roof homotopy. Show that omitting any one gives an incorrect homotopy,even though all cohomology comparisons are identities. Retain the full two-sided module interpretation.

Solution. The first and third homotopy equations follow from the definitions of \(t\) and \(t_0\). For the second,both sides send \(e\) to \(y_3\) and vanish on all other basis vectors. These are degree-zero chain maps,with the stated projection homotopy equations;for example \((b'u-t_1b)(e)=y_3=(\partial A_1)(e)\). All induced cohomology maps are the identity.

The four terms of Theorem C.59.1.1,on \(e\),are respectively \[ f_1,\qquad f_2,\qquad -g,\qquad -f_3. \] Their differential is \(y_1+y_2-z-y_3\),which is exactly \((\phi't-u\phi)(e)\). These four target boundaries are linearly independent. Omitting any one term gives a nonzero defect. Tensor everything with \(k[r]/r^2\),using regular left and right multiplication on the coefficient factor. All maps and homotopies are bimodule-linear,so the construction extends to their full cofree two-sided bar modules with both nonzero coefficient actions. The same equations hold there by the cofree formula. This is an algebraic diagnostic of the homotopy terms,not an identification with the native IC mapping complexes.

Exercise C.59.4.2 (inverse placement and sign; intermediate). Work at the level of ordinary complexes. Let \(V=ke\oplus kf\oplus ky\), where \(|e|=|y|=0,|f|=-1,df=y\). Put \(h(y)=f\),zero on the other basis vectors,and \(S=dh+hd\). In Corollary C.59.2.1's contraction diagram take all four complexes to be \(V\),with identity contractions. Let \(t=u=\phi'=1\) and \(\phi=J=1+S\),so \(J'=1\). Determine \(R,L,K_*\) and verify the finest homotopy equation. Explain the errors produced by omitting \(J^{-1}\) or reversing the sign.

Solution. The map \(S\) is zero on \(e\) and the identity on the acyclic pair \(f,y\). It is a closed projector. Thus \(J\) is identity on \(e\) and multiplication by two on that pair;its inverse is \(1-\tfrac12S\). Both maps induce identity on cohomology. The raw square has defect \(\phi't-u\phi=-S\),so take \(R=-h\). The identity contractions have zero homotopies,hence \(L=R=-h\) and \[ K_*=-LJ^{-1}=h(1-\tfrac12S)=\tfrac12h. \] Its differential is \(\tfrac12S\). On the other hand \[ U-T_*=1-J^{-1}=\tfrac12S, \] so the stated equation holds on all three basis vectors. Omitting the inverse would give \(h\),whose differential is \(S\),twice the required value on both \(f\) and \(y\). Reversing the minus sign in \(-LJ^{-1}\) gives differential \(-\tfrac12S\). The example checks the algebraic homotopy formula; it does not identify this nonminimal complex with the minimal native central spaces. The full cofree version uses the actual identity-leading maps and contractions stipulated in the preceding theorems.

Theorem C.59.1.1 retains all four terms of the full projection homotopy. Corollary C.59.2.1 gives the correctly typed finest primitive;Theorem C.59.3.1 extends its normalization to the prescribed ordered cuts. Exercises C.59.4.1–C.59.4.2 compute the necessary terms,inverse and sign. Editable SVG source.

C.60. Reverse path projection and coherent square transport

The second projection of the module path category has an explicit normalized mapping-kernel contraction. It lifts a supplied entire coherent family to larger module models with projection-compatible edges. A coherent square with the exact compressed edge values then returns to the original comparisons through the full kernel homotopies. The results apply to the complete module differentials;identifying the prescribed native edges remains necessary in the geometric application.

C.60.1. The other path projection has a normalized kernel contraction

Let \(p_i:X_i\to Q_i\) be normalized full module SDR projections, with sections \(i_i\) and homotopies \(h_i\). Thus \(p_ii_i=1,\partial h_i=1-i_ip_i\),and \(h_i^2=p_ih_i=h_ii_i=0\). For the object paths \(p_i\), use C.53.4's path category. A degree-\(r\) morphism is \((f,g,a)\),with \[ \begin{aligned} f&:X_i\to X_j,\qquad g:Q_i\to Q_j,\\ a&:X_i\to Q_j,\qquad |a|=r-1. \end{aligned} \] Its differential is \(D(f,g,a)=(\partial f,\partial g,-\partial a+p_jf-gp_i)\). Let \(\pi_1\) retain \(g\),the second component.

Lemma C.60.1.1 (reverse path-projection kernel). The projection \(\pi_1\) is graded-surjective on each mapping block and its kernel has the normalized contraction \[ k_1(f,a)=(h_jf+i_ja,0). \] The kernel differential is \(d_K(f,a)=(\partial f,-\partial a+p_jf)\). This is a contraction in the full mapping complex,including all module actions and fixed core maps.

Proof. The triple \((0,g,0)\) is a graded preimage of every \(g\). In its kernel the displayed differential is immediate from the path formula. Since \(|h_j|=-1\) and \(i_j\) is closed, \[ \begin{aligned} \partial(h_jf+i_ja) &=(1-i_jp_j)f-h_j\partial f+i_j\partial a,\\ p_j(h_jf+i_ja)&=a. \end{aligned} \] Consequently the first component of \(d_Kk_1+k_1d_K\) is \((1-i_jp_j)f-h_j\partial f+i_j\partial a +h_j\partial f-i_j\partial a+i_jp_jf=f\). Its second component is \(a\). Also \(h_j(h_jf+i_ja)=0\),so \(k_1^2=0\). Every operation is postcomposition with an actual full module map. It therefore retains the two coactions and the stated core maps. This proves the contraction without omitting any source differential term. \(\square\)

C.60.2. Lift the entire smaller family with exactly prescribed edges

Let \(I\) be a finite directed parameter category,and let \(G:\Omega B(kI)\to\mathcal E\) be the supplied entire unital coherent family with objects \(Q_i\). Use the projections \(p_i:X_i\to Q_i\) above. The free source generator for an original strict-arrow string of length \(q\) has degree \(1-q\). Its differential uses merges or products of shorter generators.

Theorem C.60.2.1 (reverse coherent model transport). There is a unital dg functor \(\mathscr H:\Omega B(kI)\to\operatorname{Path}(\mathcal E)\) with object paths \(p_i\),second projection exactly \(G\),and one-arrow values \[ \mathscr H(\alpha) =(i_jG(\alpha)p_i,G(\alpha),0). \] Its first projection is a whole coherent family \(F\) on the larger models,whose arrows commute exactly with the specified projections. The construction retains every higher parameter generator and is finite. Compatible previously assigned free-generator face data can be kept.

Proof. For an original arrow,\(G(\alpha)\) is closed. The first component is closed too,and \(p_ji_jG(\alpha)p_i=G(\alpha)p_i\). The path differential is therefore zero. Assign the identity triple to an identity arrow. This defines the lift on the length-one generators and their products.

Suppose all shorter generator values are assigned. For a degree-\(1-q\) generator \(x\),choose \(v=(0,G(x),0)\) and set \[ o=Dv-\mathscr H(dx),\qquad \mathscr H(x)=v-k_1o. \] The second projection of the defect is zero because \(G\) is a dg functor. Applying \(D\) to the defect gives zero:the chain equations already hold on every shorter product in \(dx\),and \(d^2x=0\). Lemma C.60.1.1 thus gives \(Dk_1o=o\). The corrected value has precisely the required differential and its second projection remains \(G(x)\). Extend freely and multiplicatively; the dg Leibniz identity gives the equation on all new products.

Induction constructs the entire dg functor. Finite directed height bounds the length of every strict-arrow string,so this is a finite generator construction. A full parameter face consists of the free generators whose original vertices lie in that face. Merging removes vertices and splitting uses their subsets. Thus a union of already assigned face generators is differential-stable;use its agreeing values and perform the correction only on the remaining generators. The same induction retains compatible earlier finite corners.

The first projection is a dg functor by the path-category identities. Its projection-compatible edge formula is the one assigned initially, and its higher values are the just-constructed coherent values,not separately chosen fillers. The object paths are homotopy equivalences, so the path family is an actual enhanced equivalence of the two whole families. \(\square\)

C.60.3. A coherent small square and the corresponding actual raw square

Use the C59 raw objects \(Z,Z',W,W'\) and projections \(a,a',b,b'\),with sections \(i,i',s,s'\) and normalized homotopies \(h,h',k,k'\),respectively. Let the actual closed raw comparisons be \(t:Z\to Z'\),\(u:W\to W'\). Set their exact compressed comparisons to be \[ t_0=a'ti,\qquad t_1=b'us. \] Suppose a supplied entire coherent square on the four smaller objects has horizontal edges \(B:Q_0\to Q_1\),\(B':Q_0'\to Q_1'\) and these vertical edges \(t_0,t_1\). For the square poset its two length-two generators have images \(H_0,H_1\) satisfying \[ \partial H_0=B't_0-c,\qquad \partial H_1=t_1B-c, \] where \(c\) is the same original diagonal arrow image. Put \(C=H_0-H_1\),\(\phi=sBa,\phi'=s'B'a'\).

Theorem C.60.3.1 (return from projection-compatible edges). The full projection homotopies and monoidal homotopy can be chosen as \[ \begin{aligned} A_0&=a'th,\qquad A_1=b'uk,\\ C&=H_0-H_1. \end{aligned} \] They have exactly C59's types and differentials. The raw roof square then has the full primitive \[ R=s'Ca+s'B'a'th-k'usBa. \] This is the corresponding specialization of the four-term formula: its fourth term is zero by the normalized equation \(ks=0\). Every higher component of the supplied smaller square can be retained via Theorem C.60.2.1. No zero homotopy is asserted for a general unnormalized projection square.

Proof. Closedness of the other factors gives \[ \begin{aligned} \partial A_0&=a't(1-ia)=a't-t_0a,\\ \partial A_1&=b'u(1-sb)=b'u-t_1b,\\ \partial C&=B't_0-t_1B. \end{aligned} \] These are the required full mapping-complex identities. C.59.1.1 now applies. Its last term is \(-s'A_1sBa=-s'b'uk sBa=0\),and its target kernel homotopy is \(k'\). The remaining terms give the displayed primitive.

There is also a direct whole-family interpretation. Theorem C.60.2.1 lifts the supplied small square to the projection-compatible arrows \(t_c=i't_0a\),\(u_c=s't_1b\),\(\phi,\phi'\). The small primitive has the raw lift \(s'Ca\),since \(a'i'=1,bs=1\). The actual comparisons are connected to those canonical ones by the explicit full homotopies \[ \begin{aligned} D_t&=-h't-i'a'th,\\ D_u&=-k'u-s'b'uk. \end{aligned} \] Differentiating gives \(\partial D_t=t_c-t\) and \(\partial D_u=u_c-u\),by cancelling the two intermediate \(i'a't\) or \(s'b'u\) terms. Therefore \[ s'Ca-\phi'D_t+D_u\phi \] has differential \(\phi't-u\phi\). Its normalization identities \(a'h'=0,ks=0\) simplify it to exactly the displayed \(R\). This proves the return formula without replacing either actual raw comparison by an unrelated edge.

All restrictions use these same maps and original generators. Thus every compatible assigned face is retained. Applying the actual contractions of C.59.2.1 to this \(R\) gives its finest primitive, and C.59.3.1 then normalizes the prescribed compatible ordered cuts. The supplied square,its compressed vertical maps,and its horizontal represented maps must have the stated exact values before those applications are made. \(\square\)

C.60.4. Two solved reverse-transport examples

Exercise C.60.4.1 (the kernel correction; intermediate). Let \(Q=ke\oplus k\eta\),with \(|e|=0,|\eta|=-1\) and zero differential. Put \(X=Q\oplus(kg\xrightarrow{d}kz)\),with \(|g|=-1,|z|=0,dg=z\). Let \(p\) be projection,\(i\) inclusion,and \(h(z)=g\),zero otherwise. In Lemma C.60.1.1's reverse mapping kernel take the degree-zero pair \((f,a)\),where \(f(e)=z,a(e)=\eta\),zero elsewhere. Compute both parts of \(d_Kk_1+k_1d_K\),retaining the source differential term,and verify the square-zero normalization.

Solution. The pair has the stated degree because \(a\) has degree minus one. We have \(hf(e)=g,ia(e)=\eta\),so \(k_1(f,a)=(v,0)\),where \(v(e)=g+\eta\),zero elsewhere. The Hom differential of \(v\) is \(dv+vd\),which sends \(e\) to \(z\) and vanishes on the other basis vectors. Its second kernel component is \(pv=a\). Hence \(d_Kk_1(f,a)=(f,a)\). Directly \(\partial f=0\), \(\partial a=d_Qa+ad=0\),and \(pf=0\),so \(d_K(f,a)=0\). The second composite is therefore zero. Finally \(hv=0\),since \(v\) lands in \(kg\oplus k\eta\),where \(h\) vanishes. Thus \(k_1^2(f,a)=0\). Both summands \(hf\) and \(ia\) occur in this single correction.

Exercise C.60.4.2 (return to the actual comparisons; advanced). Let \(V\) have basis \(e,f_1,y_1,f_2,y_2,f_3,y_3\),with \(|e|=|y_i|=0,|f_i|=-1,df_i=y_i\). Put \(X=V\oplus(kg\xrightarrow{d}kz)\),where \(dg=z\), \(|g|=-1,|z|=0\). Let all four larger objects be \(X\),all smaller objects be \(V\),all projections be \(p:X\to V\), all sections be \(i\),and all normalized homotopies be \(h(z)=g\). Take \(B=B'=1\). Define degree-zero chain maps \(t,u:X\to X\) by the identity except for \[ \begin{aligned} t(e)&=e+y_3+z,&u(e)&=e+z,\\ t(g)&=g+f_1,&u(g)&=g+f_2,\\ t(z)&=z+y_1,&u(z)&=z+y_2. \end{aligned} \] Find the compressed square,its two projection homotopies and the full return primitive. Explain precisely why its fourth roof term vanishes.

Solution. The chain equations hold on \(g\) because its images differentiate to the stated images of \(z\);they hold on the other basis vectors directly. The compressed maps are \(t_0=pti\),which sends \(e\) to \(e+y_3\),and \(t_1=pui=1\). Take \(C(e)=f_3\),zero otherwise. Then \(\partial C=t_0-t_1\). A coherent small square can use the diagonal \(c=t_1\),with \(H_0=C,H_1=0\);its two triangle equations have exactly the required boundaries.

The actual projection homotopies are \(A_0=pth,A_1=puh\). They send \(z\) to \(f_1,f_2\),respectively,and vanish on the remaining basis vectors. They are both nonzero. In the reverse homotopy equation their differentials also act on \(g\):the Hom source term gives \(A_0(dg)=f_1\) or \(A_1(dg)=f_2\). These are precisely the corresponding values of \(pt-t_0p\) and \(pu-t_1p\).

The three terms of the return primitive \(R\) are \[ iCp,\qquad ipth,\qquad -huip. \] Their nonzero values are, respectively,\(e\mapsto f_3\), \(z\mapsto f_1\),and \(e\mapsto-g\). Their boundaries send \(e\) to \(y_3\),send \(z,g\) to \(y_1,f_1\), and send \(e\) to \(-z\),respectively. These are independent directions and sum exactly to \(\phi't-u\phi\),where \(\phi=\phi'=ip\). The fourth C59 term is \(-iA_1i p=0\),because \(hi=0\) in \(A_1=puh\). It vanishes by this proved normalization,even though \(A_1\ne0\). There is no general rule allowing its omission in an arbitrary roof.

Tensoring with \(k[r]/r^2\),using regular left and right multiplication on that coefficient,retains these equations as bimodule equations. Their full cofree extensions therefore retain both nonzero actions and both outside coactions. This is an algebraic example of the return formula;the native application additionally requires its exact supplied coherent square and edge identifications.

Lemma C.60.1.1 contracts the reverse path-projection kernel. Theorems C.60.2.1–C.60.3.1 lift entire coherent module families and return their exact compressed square to the raw comparisons. Exercises C.60.4.1–C.60.4.2 retain the source differential and the normalized nonzero correction terms. Editable SVG source.

C.61. Full mapping restriction and the fixed native square

The actual bar-unit embedding retains the whole bicomodule mapping complex. Its restriction kernel contracts at fixed original rank, and a finite perturbation retains both module actions. Thus full transformation classes and their null-homotopies can be recorded on the common bars. The actual represented native equivalences identify the four edges of one specified product square in that full complex. The relative version retains genuine full faces when the required relative transformation class is given.

C.61.1. The common-bar mapping complex is the correct full complex

Let \(K=C^{\otimes n}\otimes D_I\),including \(n=0\),and let \(L=C^{\otimes m}\otimes D_J\). Use the actual minimal IC bar and finite directed index bars of C52. Write \(\widehat K=B\Omega K,\widehat L=B\Omega L\),and use their actual natural unit embeddings \(\eta_K,\eta_L\). Take two full cofree modules \(\widehat X,\widehat Y\) over \(\widehat L,\widehat K\),with central complexes \(M,N\). They have normalized module actions. Let \(X,Y\) be their genuine pullbacks over \(L,K\),retaining the same central complexes.

Count original IC primitive letters plus index height jumps in an element of \(K\) or \(L\),and add these counts in an original word of \(B\Omega K\) or \(B\Omega L\). Denote the sum on the two outside runs by \(R\). Every reduced original input has positive count,and cuts preserve its sum. Assume the given module actions consume positive count whenever they are not central unary terms. This holds for the raw normalized represented modules used in C58:an action removes a nonempty original outside word,including its index height when the corresponding arrow acts by a scalar.

Theorem C.61.1.1 (full mapping restriction is a surjective quasi-isomorphism). Restriction along \(\eta_L,\eta_K\) gives a graded-surjective chain map \[ \begin{aligned} r:\operatorname{Hom}_{\widehat L,\widehat K} (\widehat X,\widehat Y)\\ \longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{L,K}(X,Y). \end{aligned} \] Its kernel has a normalized contraction finite on every original outside input. Here both Hom complexes consist of full cofree bicomodule maps over identity pure cores,with their complete source and target action differential. Restriction preserves composition and identities on the whole dg category of these pullbacks. Thus it is fully faithful on full transformation cohomology,not only on bare central values.

Proof. Each unit is a coalgebra map by C.39.4.1. It is graded injective:its one-bar-letter,one-cobar-generator component is exactly \(c\mapsto s(tc)\),an injective map on the reduced original coalgebra. Coaugmentations are retained too. Consequently the tensor embedding of the two outside runs is injective. A homogeneous full map is determined by its central Taylor map. Restrict that map to the two unit images;any prescribed homogeneous Taylor map on their tensor extends linearly. The cofree reconstruction proves graded surjectivity of \(r\).

The pulled-back modules are chain modules because the unit embeddings are dg coalgebra maps. Their coactions on any retained word stay in the unit images. Hence restriction commutes with the entire mapping differential,including its source and target actions. The cofree composition formula cuts the original words using those same coactions. Restricting before or after that formula gives identical cuts and signs,so it preserves composition and the identity. This also shows directly that the restriction kernel is a subcomplex.

We now contract that kernel without an infinite-length assertion. First discard only the nonunary IC operations and the nonunary module actions. Keep the central unary differential,all index-bar unary differentials,and the complete bar-cobar cut and splitting differentials. Call the resulting mapping differential \(\partial_0\). It preserves \(R\). The unit for these leading pure differentials also preserves \(R\),and is the same explicit unit formula as C.39.16. It contains all iterated coproduct terms;none is removed.

At each fixed original rank the unit is a quasi-isomorphism. Here is the finite argument needed for that stronger assertion. In \(B\Omega K\),filter by the number \(r_0\) of original noncoaugmented \(K\)-elements before dividing them into cobar blocks. Every such element has positive original rank,so \(r_0\le R\). The cobar splitting increases \(r_0\);the original unary differential and bar merging preserve it. At a fixed \(r_0\ge2\) associated quotient,C.39.4.1's explicit cut homotopy inserts the first missing cut with coefficient \((-1)^{|c_1|}\). It contracts that full quotient,including the original unary differential. It preserves the total original rank,each endpoint and every original letter label. At \(r_0=1\) the unit has identity leading value. Finite cone elimination through \(1\le r_0\le R\) proves that the unit has acyclic comparison cone in that exact rank block. The argument applies to \(L\) as well. Tensoring over the field therefore makes \(\eta_L\otimes\eta_K\) a quasi-isomorphism in every fixed total rank,by splitting each acyclic tensor factor as in C30.

It is an injective chain map. Thus its quotient complex on the two outside runs is acyclic in every rank and endpoint block. Choose a normalized splitting contraction there by C.30.1.1. Tensor it with the unchanged central complex \(M\),using the Koszul sign when the outside homotopy crosses a central factor. This gives a normalized quotient-input contraction \(h_Q\). The leading kernel of \(r\) is precisely the Taylor Hom complex from that quotient input to \(N\). For a degree-\(d\) map \(f\),the operator \(H_0(f)=(-1)^d f h_Q\) has \(\partial_0H_0+H_0\partial_0=1,H_0^2=0\),by the full signed Hom calculation in C.56.3.1. It preserves original rank.

Write the entire mapping differential as \(\partial_0+\delta\). The omitted source pure IC terms reduce original primitive count. Every omitted source action consumes a positive-rank outside piece. For a target action,expand the full cofree formula:the central Taylor map is evaluated on the middle input left after those outside pieces have been removed. It has smaller original rank too. Normalization rules out a pure operation creating a scalar from nonempty original IC inputs;index-scalar action cases still consume positive height. These are all the omitted terms. Thus \(\delta f\) on a rank-\(R\) input uses \(f\) only on smaller ranks.

The restriction kernel is stable under both differentials,so the finite perturbation formula of C.35.1 gives its actual contraction \[ H=H_0(1+\delta H_0)^{-1}. \] At most \(R\) perturbation factors contribute on that original input. It satisfies \(\partial H+H\partial=1,H^2=0\) in the full restriction kernel. The kernel is therefore contractible, and the already proved graded-surjective chain map is a quasi-isomorphism. No bound on arbitrary natural-transformation spaces or on infinitely many input lengths was used. \(\square\)

C.61.2. A fully faithful recording transfers prescribed whole edge classes

Let \(P:\mathcal D\to\mathcal E\) be a dg functor,with fixed chosen object labels,whose maps on all retained Hom complexes are surjective quasi-isomorphisms. In the application \(P\) is the actual restriction \(r\) of Theorem C.61.1.1 on a finite set of raw module objects. Let \(I\) be a finite directed parameter category and \(F:\Omega B(kI)\to\mathcal D\) a supplied entire family. For each original arrow \(\alpha\),suppose a closed map \(e_\alpha\) in \(\mathcal E\) is prescribed and its full cohomology class equals \([PF(\alpha)]\).

Theorem C.61.2.1 (exact-edge coherent recording). There is a whole coherent family \(G:\Omega B(kI)\to\mathcal E\) whose edges are exactly \(e_\alpha\),with an actual resolved path equivalence to \(PF\). Each entire native null-homotopy is retained through the path construction. The result uses equality in the full mapping complex,not equality only of leading cohomology components.

More explicitly,if \(z\in\mathcal D^0(X,Y)\) is closed and \(Pz=\partial c\),the kernel contraction produces a full primitive of \(z\). It can be chosen to have exact image \(c\).

Proof. Equality of the stated full classes means precisely that there is a degree-minus-one map \(k_\alpha\) with \(\partial k_\alpha=e_\alpha-PF(\alpha)\). These maps belong to the actual full Hom complexes. Apply C.54.4.1 to the entire \(PF\) and these actual edge homotopies. Its explicit identity-path recursion retains all higher generators and gives the exact prescribed edges. This proves the coherent assertion,including the actual path to the original entire family. For example,on a triangle its new higher image is \(H+k_ba+b'k_a-k_c\),with every term and sign retained.

Here is a constructive primitive lift,which also proves the stated faithfulness without appealing only to the phrase quasi-isomorphism. Choose a graded preimage \(c_0\) of \(c\). Then \(z-\partial c_0\) is a closed degree-zero element of the mapping kernel. With its actual contraction \(H\),put \[ c_{\mathcal D}=c_0+H(z-\partial c_0). \] Its differential is \(z\) and its image is exactly \(c\). All its values are full maps. For the restriction in Theorem C.61.1.1, the correction is finite on each original input. Thus a primitive on the common bars lifts without discarding a higher source or target component. The construction also shows that two native full edge representatives with the same restricted full class are homotopic upstairs. This does not assert that edges with equal bare components have the same restricted full class. \(\square\)

C.61.3. The exact four edges of one specified native product square

Fix one of C58's specified rootwise product families,with all its original parameter cells. Work over the extension field \(E\) and use the actual calibrated whole enhanced comparison of C.48.1.1. Retain its actual whole-prism representative from C50/C54. Denote its raw global and product restrictions by \(t:Z\to Z'\) and \(u:W\to W'\). Use C58's four common-target projections \(a,a',b,b'\) and their actual fixed-projection sections \(i,i',s,s'\). Let \(B,B'\) be exactly the represented evaluations of the native external-product transformations constructed in C.58.2.1.

Theorem C.61.3.1 (record one fixed native square with its prescribed edges). For this fixed product family,there is an entire coherent square in the full module category whose horizontal edges are exactly \(B,B'\) and whose vertical edges are exactly \(t_0=a'ti,t_1=b'us\). Its two triangle images supply an actual full \(C\) with \(\partial C=B't_0-t_1B\). Consequently C.60.3.1 supplies the actual projection-roof homotopy,and C59 supplies its finest primitive and simultaneous normalization of the compatible ordered cuts. The assertion retains this whole parameter family;it does not yet assert that choices made on different native families agree on every overlapping parameter or grafting domain.

Proof. First remove the varying-core type issue. C.48.1.1's actual coalgebra isomorphism \(g\) identifies the two pure core systems. Pull the target system back by its literal tensor powers and the index identities. C.52.2.1 makes every common-target projection commute strictly with that pullback. All four module objects and all the maps now belong to one dg category over the same fixed cores. This uses the actual \(g\);it is not an attempt to linearize an unfixed coalgebra coordinate.

Each raw represented module of C58 is the pullback along \(\eta_L,\eta_K\) of its ordinary normalized bar module over \(\Omega L,\Omega K\). This follows directly from the canonical unit formula and the consecutive-block represented construction in C.33.2.1. The small common-target modules have the same property,using their target projection to the common dg tensor category. That projection is a quasi-equivalence on the pertinent finite envelopes by C.52.2.1/C.52.3.1. Thus they are actual represented objects on those envelopes too,with the specified represented comparisons. No module has been selected by its graded dimension alone.

The entire native strong monoidal comparison of C48 supplies its original square,including its two triangles and their original diagonal,on these functor envelopes. Apply the full represented evaluation of C.33.2.1/C.53.1.1 before any compression. It records that complete square as full normalized module transformations. The full Yoneda mapping equivalence of C.33.2.1 retains the transformation mapping complexes,including every source-word component. The actual unit and counit equivalences of the chosen representing objects therefore transport this whole square to the four retained bar-module models. Restrict it by Theorem C.61.1.1. It is now an entire coherent square on the common bars,possibly with different edge representatives from the four prescribed ones.

We check equality of those four full edge classes. In the homotopy category of full module maps,a normalized SDR gives \([i]=[a]^{-1}\),\([s]=[b]^{-1}\),and the corresponding primed equalities,because its two inverse equations have the specified actual full homotopies. Hence the transported vertical classes on the common-target objects are precisely \[ [a'][t][a]^{-1}=[a'ti],\qquad [b'][u][b]^{-1}=[b'us]. \] Here \([t],[u]\) are the classes of the supplied whole native comparison,not inferred comparison classes. C.50.2.1 identifies its entire prism bimodule with that comparison by the actual represented evaluation maps. Its inverse and units are the full action-transfer equivalences of C.50.1.1;C.54.2.1 keeps the prescribed complete pure-state actions in this recovery. Restricting these actual equivalences to the present product family is exactly the raw \(t,u\) stipulated above. Thus the two displayed classes use their full comparison provenance.

For a horizontal edge,C.58.2.1 defines its transformation \(\beta\) by \(c_0^{-1}\alpha c_1\),where \(\alpha\) is the original native external-product comparison and \(c_0,c_1\) are these particular representing equivalences. Full represented evaluation gives exactly \(B=R_\beta\),and likewise \(B'\). The degree-zero contravariant direction is the one proved in C.53.1.1. Consequently these are exactly the horizontal classes of the transported native square. This argument identifies the entire transformations through their representing equivalences; it uses no assertion about their bare cohomology maps.

Theorem C.61.1.1 ensures that passage to the common bars has retained these full mapping classes faithfully. In particular any two edge representatives just compared differ by an actual full degree-minus-one boundary. Choose those edge homotopies and apply the identity-path replacement of C.54.4.1 to the entire restricted square. Equivalently use Theorem C.61.2.1's exact-edge recording. The resulting coherent square has exactly \(B,B',a'ti,b'us\),with its actual two triangle components \(H_0,H_1\) and the same recorded diagonal. Their difference \(C=H_0-H_1\) therefore satisfies the required full equation.

All constructions were on the supplied entire parameter family, so its higher parameter components remain present. C.60.3.1 now gives \(A_0=a'th,A_1=b'uk\) and its normalized return homotopy;C.59.2.1 transfers that actual homotopy to the finest models,and C.59.3.1 retains its value while normalizing all prescribed compatible ordered cuts. Restore the same literal \(g\) powers afterwards. This proves the fixed-family assertion. The choice of full edge primitives on two different ambient families has not been compared here. Compatible assignments on all such overlaps,all whole-graph sectors and all external higher grafting marks still require their own relative construction. \(\square\)

C.61.4. Relative restriction on genuine parameter faces

Fix a finite collection of full parameter faces in the original root factors,and,if needed,a finite collection of full IC label corners. On a bar-cobar word retain a face when every one of its original parameter vertices and IC labels belongs to that face. The leading quotients in Theorem C.61.1.1 use these actual subcomplexes; they do not identify a nonrectangular joint domain with a rectangle.

Theorem C.61.4.1 (relative full-face mapping restriction). The kernel contraction in Theorem C.61.1.1 can be chosen to preserve maps vanishing on the assigned union of such faces. Restriction remains a surjective quasi-isomorphism on those relative full mapping complexes. Thus a relative full null-homotopy on the common bars lifts while retaining its assigned native face values. Compatible increasing full corners can retain earlier choices. A relative null-homotopy class is required; absolute null-homotopy alone does not assert a relative one.

Proof. At the leading differential work separately in each fixed original rank and endpoint block. The unit is injective with leading term \(s(tc)\). Choose an original basis of \(K\) and \(L\) consisting of the actual IC/index word tensors.
