In each \(B\Omega K\) basis,the unit image of such a basis element is its one-bar-letter,one-cobar-generator word plus terms with at least two original coalgebra elements. All terms use only its original parameter vertices and labels. The analogous assertion holds for the two outside runs together by taking their tensor.

Eliminate each leading canonical unit-image basis vector using that unit relation. The quotient has the remaining bar-cobar word basis. A full face retains exactly its subset of this quotient basis: when a canonical vector belongs to the face,all terms of the unit relation used to eliminate it also belong to the face. Conversely the leading canonical component detects membership in the original face. Thus the quotient-face subspaces have the distributive original-word support lattice,and their intersections are the quotient subspaces for the actual common faces. The same basis argument works for a union of the retained faces.

Theorem C.61.1.1's finite rank/cut proof applies to every full face and every finite intersection. Their leading quotient complexes are therefore acyclic. The acyclic-face-union construction of C.50.2.1 gives a normalized quotient contraction retaining all assigned faces:the sum of previously assigned acyclic face subcomplexes is acyclic by the distributive support lattice;its quotient is acyclic;extend the earlier contraction by a chain splitting of that quotient. The explicit corrected chain section and square-zero normalization are the ones proved there. Do this at each rank and endpoint block. It preserves the unit quotient and all earlier choices.

Precomposition with this contraction preserves vanishing on each face. The leading signed Taylor Hom contraction \(H_0\) thus preserves the relative restriction kernel. The omitted source and target terms also preserve it,because the actual cofree coactions and full differentials retain these full face submodels. Every term in the finite perturbation \(H_0(1+\delta H_0)^{-1}\) has the same property. It contracts the full relative kernel.

For graded surjectivity on the relative complexes,define the desired native Taylor map on the union of the unit image and the assigned faces:use the given common-bar value on the former and zero on the latter. Their intersection consists exactly of the unit image of the corresponding common face union,by the leading canonical-word argument. The given relative map vanishes there, so these prescriptions agree. Extend them on a graded complement. This gives a full relative graded lift. Together with the full relative kernel contraction it proves the asserted relative surjective quasi-isomorphism,and the primitive formula in Theorem C.61.2.1 retains every assigned zero face value. Subtracting an already prescribed full extension gives the analogous statement for nonzero compatible values.

The same support argument and acyclic-quotient extension retain the chosen contractions along an increasing system of full finite corners. None of these statements replaces the actual relative class by an absolute class,or treats a clipped shuffle domain as a full factor face. Those separate distinctions are needed in applying the result to native overlaps. \(\square\)

C.61.5. Two solved bar-unit calculations

Exercise C.61.5.1 (the actual index unit; intermediate). For \(K=D_{[2]}\),write the index arrows as \(a:0\to1,b:1\to2,c:0\to2\),and put \(w=sb\mid sa\). Compute its actual unit in \(B\Omega K\), the quotient by that unit image and a normalized quotient contraction. Explain what the full face \(\{0,2\}\) retains.

Solution. The two-arrow bar word satisfies \(d_Kw=-sc\). In \(\Omega K\) put \(A=t(sa),B=t(sb),C=t(sc),H=t(w)\). The retained sign convention C.39.15 gives \(dH=BA-C\). The actual unit therefore has \[ \begin{aligned} \eta_K(w)&=sH+sB\mid sA,\\ \eta_K(sc)&=sC. \end{aligned} \] In \(B\Omega K\),the two differential contributions are \(d(sH)=s(BA)-sC\) and \(d(sB\mid sA)=-s(BA)\). They cancel to give \(d\eta_K(w)=-sC=\eta_K(d_Kw)\). The quotient by the unit image has basis \(u=s(BA),v=sB\mid sA\),with \(dv=-u\). Indeed \(sC=0\) and \(sH=-v\) in that quotient. Its normalized contraction is \(h(u)=-v,h(v)=0\). Each proper full parameter face retains zero quotient here;in particular the face \(\{0,2\}\) still retains its actual direct arrow \(c\) and its unit image. The whole three-vertex face retains the displayed acyclic quotient. Thus the face statement does not erase the direct arrow or identify the two different source paths.

Exercise C.61.5.2 (the signed mapping primitive; intermediate). Take \(K=k\oplus kx\),with \(x\) primitive of degree one and zero differential. At original rank two,describe the quotient of \(B\Omega K\) by the unit image. For the linear map \(f\) to \(k\) that is one on the two-block word and zero on the one-block word,compute its degree and a signed Hom primitive.

Solution. We have \(\Omega K=k[t(x)]\),whose generator has degree two. At original rank two,the unit quotient has basis \(u=s(t(x)^2)\) in degree three and \(v=s(t(x))\mid s(t(x))\) in degree two. Again \(dv=-u,h(u)=-v\). For a degree-minus-two linear map to \(k\) with \(f(v)=1,f(u)=0\),the Hom differential is zero. Its signed primitive has \[ H_0(f)(u)=(-1)^{-2}f(-v)=-1, \qquad H_0(f)(v)=0. \] This map has degree minus three,and its Hom differential on \(v\) is \(-(-1)^{-3}H_0(f)(-u)=1\),as required. This is the leading cut calculation,with trivial endpoint actions. With nontrivial source and target actions,the full finite perturbation in Theorem C.61.1.1 retains their additional terms;the leading cut contraction alone need not contract the entire mapping differential.

Theorems C.61.1.1–C.61.4.1 prove full mapping restriction,exact-edge recording,the fixed native square and relative full-face restriction. Exercises C.61.5.1–C.61.5.2 compute the actual index unit quotient and its signed Hom primitive. Editable SVG source.

C.62. Relative coherent lifts with the original family fixed

A supplied entire common-bar path lifts while retaining the original native first family and its already assigned faces. The relevant mapping kernel is an explicit identity cone;its contraction does not require the original restriction kernel to be acyclic. The generator construction retains every higher path component and both exact common images. Constructing the compatible common path with all native product conditions remains the input required for this lifting step.

C.62.1. A path-recording projection with an elementary cone kernel

Let \(P:\mathcal D\to\mathcal E\) be a unital dg functor surjective on its graded Hom spaces. No acyclicity of its mapping kernels is required in this lemma. Retain chosen object labels in \(\mathcal D\). Define \(\mathcal Q(P)\) on those labels: a degree-\(r\) morphism is a triple \[ \begin{aligned} f&:X\to Y\quad\text{in }\mathcal D,\\ g&:PX\to PY\quad\text{in }\mathcal E,\\ a&:PX\to PY\quad\text{in }\mathcal E,\quad |a|=r-1. \end{aligned} \] Use differential and composition \[ \begin{aligned} D(f,g,a)&=(\partial f,\partial g,\\ &\qquad-\partial a+Pf-g),\\ (f_2,g_2,a_2)&(f_1,g_1,a_1)\\ &=(f_2f_1,g_2g_1,\\ &\qquad a_2Pf_1+(-1)^{|f_2|}g_2a_1). \end{aligned} \] These are exactly the path-category formulas after restricting its first projection along \(P\). The object path in \(\mathcal E\) is the identity of \(PX\). Let \(\operatorname{Path}_1(\mathcal D)\) be the analogous identity-object-path category over \(\mathcal D\).

Lemma C.62.1.1 (keep the native first projection). The map \[ \begin{aligned} S&:\operatorname{Path}_1(\mathcal D)\to\mathcal Q(P),\\ S(f,g,a)&=(f,Pg,Pa) \end{aligned} \] is a unital dg functor,graded-surjective and a quasi-isomorphism on every Hom complex. It fixes the first projection exactly. Its mapping kernel has the normalized contraction \[ k(0,g,a)=(0,-a,0). \] The same result holds in relative Hom spaces vanishing on assigned full faces whenever \(P\) is graded-surjective there.

Proof. C.50.3's signed path identities give the dg category \(\mathcal Q(P)\),since \(P\) preserves the differential, composition and identities. Substitution in those same formulas shows that \(S\) is a dg functor. For a prescribed triple in \(\mathcal Q(P)\),keep its actual \(f\) and lift \(g,a\) graded-linearly through \(P\). This proves graded surjectivity.

An element of the kernel has \(f=0\) and \(Pg=Pa=0\). On the remaining pair its differential is \(d_K(g,a)=(\partial g,-\partial a-g)\). It stays in the kernel because \(P\) is a chain map. With \(k(g,a)=(-a,0)\), \[ \begin{aligned} d_Kk(g,a)&=(-\partial a,a),\\ kd_K(g,a)&=(\partial a+g,0). \end{aligned} \] Their sum is \((g,a)\),and \(k^2=0\). Thus the mapping kernel is contractible even if \(\ker P\) has cohomology: it is the shifted cone of its identity. Surjectivity and this contraction prove the mapping quasi-isomorphism.

All formulas preserve the first projection. They also preserve vanishing on each assigned face,as \(k\) merely moves \(-a\) to the second component. Relative graded lifts exist by the assumed relative surjectivity of \(P\). This proves the relative claim without asserting acyclicity of an arbitrary relative native transformation space. \(\square\)

C.62.2. Lift a whole common path relative to its already assigned faces

Let \(I\) be a finite directed parameter category. Let \(F:\Omega B(kI)\to\mathcal D\) be the actual whole native family,with all its original higher components. Suppose \(H:\Omega B(kI)\to\mathcal Q(P)\) is a supplied entire path recording whose first projection is exactly \(F\). Write its other components as \(G,A\);thus \(G\) is the desired entire common family and \(A\) records the full path from \(PF\) to \(G\). Its object paths are identities. Let a compatible lift to \(\operatorname{Path}_1(\mathcal D)\) already be assigned on a differential-stable union of original free generators,such as a union of full parameter faces.

Theorem C.62.2.1 (relative coherent native path lift). The given lift extends to a whole unital dg functor \(\widetilde H:\Omega B(kI)\to\operatorname{Path}_1(\mathcal D)\) with \(S\widetilde H=H\). Its first projection is exactly the actual native \(F\). Its second projection \(\widetilde G\) and path component \(\widetilde A\) have exact prescribed images \(P\widetilde G=G,P\widetilde A=A\). All earlier face values are unchanged,and every higher generator is retained. This is a finite original-word construction.

Proof. Keep the assigned values. Map a coefficient identity to the true identity triple. For the next original free generator \(x\),choose a graded lift \(v\) of \(H(x)\) under \(S\), keeping its first component exactly \(F(x)\). Its differential uses only shorter original generators or their products,already assigned. Put \[ o=Dv-\widetilde H(dx),\qquad \widetilde H(x)=v-k o. \] The defect has image zero under \(S\),because the whole given \(H\) is a dg functor. Its first component is zero separately, because \(F\) is a dg functor and its earlier values are exact. Applying \(D\) to the defect gives zero:the chain equation has already been proved on all shorter terms of \(dx\),and \(d^2x=0\). Lemma C.62.1.1 therefore gives \(Dko=o\). The corrected value satisfies its chain equation,retains the exact image under \(S\),and keeps the first component fixed. Extend freely to products;the graded Leibniz identity proves their equations too.

Induct on the original string length. The finite directed height bounds every strict-arrow string,so every generator receives its value after finitely many steps. If original arrows with the same endpoints are parallel,their distinct labels are never identified. The assigned differential-stable union is retained because only unassigned generators are corrected. For full parameter faces, merging removes vertices and splitting uses subsets,so that stability is exactly the one proved in C.53.5.1/C.54.4.1.

The first and second projections of \(\widetilde H\) are dg functors by the signed path identities. Its object paths are identities,so it is an actual resolved equivalence from the original native family to \(\widetilde G\),with every higher path component included. The equality \(S\widetilde H=H\) holds on generators and therefore on all their free products. It gives the exact two prescribed common images.

For additional internal full-face or full-corner constraints,apply the relative version of Lemma C.62.1.1 on each mapping block. C.61.4.1 provides that graded surjectivity for the actual bar-unit restriction. The cone contraction preserves those relative subspaces regardless of their own cohomology. Thus compatible earlier values can also be retained along increasing finite corners. This is a lifting result for the given compatible entire common path. It does not infer that common path from unrelated absolute edge primitives. \(\square\)

If a fixed chain-linear section \(J\) of \(P\) is available, the generator recipe can be especially explicit. Choose \(v=(F(x),JG(x),JA(x))\). Only its second component changes under the correction,because \(k o=(0,-o_a,0)\). On a one-arrow generator it gives \[ \begin{aligned} \widetilde G(\alpha)&=F(\alpha)\\ &\quad+J\bigl(G(\alpha)-PF(\alpha)\bigr),\\ \widetilde A(\alpha)&=JA(\alpha). \end{aligned} \] On higher generators it includes the defect of \(J\) with respect to all previously assigned products. A chain-linear section need not preserve multiplication,and those higher correction terms must not be dropped.

C.62.3. Consequence and remaining common-path obligation

For the actual restriction of C61,the theorem lifts a compatible common-bar normalization together with its entire comparison path to native normalized bar modules,retaining the original native first family and already assigned full faces. The new kernel is an identity cone,so this upward lift creates no additional relative null-homotopy obstruction. The possible obstruction identified in C.61.4.1 concerns the earlier construction of a compatible common-bar path with all desired product conditions. It has not been erased by this theorem. Its actual relative class must still be supplied on the whole native overlap domain.

After that common path is constructed,the present theorem retains its whole parameter coherence,not just a set of lifted edges. The separate simultaneous whole-path-sector construction and every external several-transition/grafting covariance mark on the exact C47 domain remain required before the full marked point and rational strong monoidal descent.

C.62.4. Two solved coherent-lift examples

Exercise C.62.4.1 (a nonacyclic restriction kernel; intermediate). Take \(P:k[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2\to k\),concentrated in degree zero. Compute the kernel of the path-recording map \(S\) of Lemma C.62.1.1 and its contraction. Explain why the quasi-isomorphism assertion for \(S\) does not assert that \(P\) is one.

Solution. The kernel of \(P\) is \(k\epsilon\) in degree zero,with nonzero cohomology. The kernel of \(S\) instead has \((\epsilon,0)\) in degree zero and \((0,\epsilon)\) in degree one. Its differential sends the former to \((0,-\epsilon)\) and the latter to zero. The contraction sends \((0,\epsilon)\) to \((-\epsilon,0)\) and the other basis vector to zero. Directly \(d_Kk+kd_K=1,k^2=0\) on both vectors. Thus \(\ker S\) is the contractible identity cone of the nonacyclic \(\ker P\). The two maps have different kernels; \(S\)'s mapping quasi-isomorphism uses exactly this cone.

Exercise C.62.4.2 (the missing triangle term; advanced). Let \(Q=ke\oplus kf\oplus ky\),with \(|e|=|y|=0,|f|=-1\) and \(df=y\). Put \(V=Q\oplus(kg\xrightarrow{d}kz)\), with \(dg=z,|g|=-1,|z|=0\). Let \(\mathcal D\) be the dg endomorphisms preserving the second summand,and let \(P\) project to \(\mathcal E=\operatorname{End}(Q)\). A unital chain-linear section is \(J(a)=\operatorname{diag}(a,a_{ee}1_{kg\oplus kz})\). Define \(K(e)=f,N(f)=g,N(y)=z\),zero elsewhere,and put \(L=\partial K\),so \(L(e)=y\). On \(0<1<2\),take the original native edges \(F_{ij}=1+(j-i)N\). On the common side change only the edge01 to \(1+L\),with path component \(-K\);leave the other two edges equal to one. Compute the lifted higher triangle value. Show why \(JK\) alone fails.

Solution. The functional \(a\mapsto a_{ee}\) annihilates the Hom differential because \(d_Q\) has zero row and column at \(e\). Thus \(J\) is a chain-linear section and sends the identity to the identity. It need not preserve multiplication. The map \(N\) is closed and \(N^2=0\),so \(F_{12}F_{01}=F_{02}\). The original higher triangle is zero.

The common triangle comparison is \(K\),since its differential is \(L=(1)(1+L)-1\). Its higher path component is zero. The native edge values given by Theorem C.62.2.1 are \[ \begin{aligned} \widetilde G_{01}&=1+N+JL,\\ \widetilde G_{12}&=1+N,\\ \widetilde G_{02}&=1+2N, \end{aligned} \] with path components \(-JK,0,0\),respectively. Their triangle defect in the comparison component is \[ \widetilde G_{12}\widetilde G_{01}-\widetilde G_{02} =JL+NJL. \] The differential of the candidate \(JK\) is only \(JL\). The missing term is \(NJL:e\mapsto z\ne0\). The actual kernel correction is \(NJK:e\mapsto g\),so the lifted triangle is \[ \widetilde G_{012}=JK+NJK. \] Indeed \(\partial(NJK)=NJL\),since \(N\) is closed of degree zero. The third component of the native path product on the triangle boundary is \(-(1+N)JK\),which is exactly \(-\widetilde G_{012}\);its higher path component remains zero. Thus the full path equation holds as well as its comparison equation. Finally \(P(NJK)=0\),so its common image is still exactly \(K\),and its first projection is the original zero higher component. Omitting the correction preserves that common image but breaks the native chain equation. This finite dg algebra example illustrates the full lifting formula;it is not an IC mapping space identification.

Lemma C.62.1.1 contracts the mixed path-recording kernel. Theorem C.62.2.1 lifts the supplied entire common path while keeping assigned native faces. Exercises C.62.4.1–C.62.4.2 calculate the cone and the essential higher triangle correction. Editable SVG source.

C.63. Global fixed-root-profile normalization

The full root-tree index is countable and locally forward finite. Its height may be negative;each nonidentity arrow still has positive height jump. The finite-on-original-rank constructions extend to this whole index. Choosing the independent fixed-profile models and their comparisons globally gives exact agreement on intersections of their finite capacities,corners and full parameter faces by restriction. Profile-changing joint execution and external grafting keep their separate domains and higher equations.

C.63.1. The unbounded tree index is locally forward finite

For \(n\ge0\),let \(\mathcal T_n\) have every finite planar operation-rooted tree with \(n\) ordered external leaves. Keep nullary and unary operation vertices. An arrow is the selected set of original operation edges to contract,as in C44. There is no vertex-capacity bound. Put \(h(t)=-V(t)\). If \(n=1\),adjoin an isolated identity-strand object \(\mathbf e\),with no new arrows to operation-rooted trees;set its height zero. Denote this enlarged category by \(\mathcal R_n\). The strand's native functor is the identity. It is not identified with the unary corolla.

Lemma C.63.1.1 (the actual global root index). These are countable directed categories in the strict-height sense. Every object has a finite full forward closure,including its actual parallel arrows. The finite capacity subcategories of C44 are full and forward-closed, and exhaust \(\mathcal T_n\). A nonidentity arrow increases height by its number of selected edges;any strict chain starting at \(t\) has length at most \(V(t)-1\).

For a fixed ordered root input profile \(\mathbf n=(n_1,\ldots,n_m)\),with \(m\) finite and \(n_i\ge0\),the category of independent such root components is literally \(\mathcal R_{\mathbf n}=\prod_i\mathcal R_{n_i}\). It is locally forward finite. Its ordered cut maps and their refined intersections retain the actual product arrow labels.

Proof. All objects and arrows lie in some C44 finite capacity subcategory. Its union/edge-lifting composition rule is independent of that capacity,so defines the global category. A finite tree has at most \(2^{V(t)-1}\) selected contraction sets. Every quotient has no more vertices than the source. Iterating a contraction is again contraction of one original selected set. Thus its whole forward closure consists of finitely many quotients,with finitely many arrows between them. An arrow starting at any quotient also ends in that closure. It is a full finite forward-closed subcategory.

C.44.1.1 gives \(V(t/E)=V(t)-|E|\),and hence the asserted height jump and source chain bound. It also proves that the full subcategory \(V\le L\) is finite and that contraction retains all external leaves. These subcategories are forward-closed and their union contains every finite tree. Countably many finite subcategories give a countable object and arrow set. Adding the isolated identity strand preserves all claims and keeps its label distinct from the unary operation vertex.

An ordered planar forest has one component for each root. Each component's external leaves form a consecutive block;each original external leaf occurs in exactly one block. Contracting operation edges cannot join different root components,so an arrow is exactly its tuple of component selected sets. The same tuple rule gives composition. Thus for the fixed input-block profile these independent forests form the displayed product category,not merely an equivalent one. Its finite forward closure is the product of the finite root forward closures. The summed height is strict on every nonidentity arrow. Ordered regrouping and refinement merely regroup those tuples, retaining their individual selected-set labels. \(\square\)

The native root functors and their full coherence maps are defined on this whole index before a capacity is imposed. They are precisely the actual finite-frame convolution/unit/contraction maps of C44 on each original finite tree. Passing to a larger capacity adds trees; it changes none of an earlier tree's maps. The same common-chain construction of C.44.3.1 supplies all finite higher diagrams at once.

The unsuspended graded central mapping space at a root tree can be identified with that at its \(n\)-corolla using its unique terminal contraction. On an arrow \(t\to u\),the two composites to the corolla are the same original contraction. Their actual enhanced comparison gives the same equality in full transformation cohomology and therefore on graded central mappings. This is a natural graded identification over \(\mathcal T_n\). The identity strand has its identity-functor mapping space. A zero-input root keeps its actual \(\operatorname{RHom}(IC_0,y)\) factor. In a tagged parameter mapping block,also keep the actual arrow-space factor \(k\mathcal R_n(t,u)\);parallel contraction labels are not discarded by this central identification. Ordered roots tensor these spaces by the actual C.57.4.1 identification.

C.63.2. The finite-on-rank constructions extend to this full index

Let each root parameter category be as in Lemma C.63.1.1,or a full finite forward-closed subcategory. A finite strict index word has the same positive height jump as in any capacity containing it. Use the original rank \[ \begin{aligned} R&=\#\{\text{original outside IC letters}\}\\ &\quad+\sum\Delta h. \end{aligned} \] No nonnegative absolute height is needed;only these height differences enter the count.

Theorem C.63.2.1 (global original-rank construction). The ordered cut algebra and its acyclic quotient,the full Taylor and bar-unit restriction contractions,the fixed-projection native cobar lifts, the relative module-action construction,and the coherent path lifts of C55–C62 apply on these full root indices. The actual maps and homotopies can be chosen once on the whole index and then restricted. These restrictions agree exactly on all intersections of their finite corners or full parameter faces. Every value on an original input remains finite.

This assertion concerns a global choice followed by restriction. It does not claim that arbitrary independently prescribed face primitives extend,or that each restricted choice is the result of a fresh canonical finite construction on that face.

Proof. Every finite collection of root objects lies in a finite full forward-closed subcategory:take the union of their finite forward closures. Its product over roots is another such finite corner. These corners form an increasing directed collection, and every finite index word occurs in one. The explicit shuffle, ordered retraction,unit and coproduct formulas on an original word are independent of its corner. The finite C55 and C56 identities therefore hold on the global index as literal equations.

For the comparison cones and quotients asserted to be acyclic, the global complexes are unions of their finite counterparts. A cycle is a finite linear combination of words and lies in one finite corner. The already proved finite acyclicity gives it a primitive in a larger finite corner if needed. Thus the union is acyclic,with an actual finite primitive. This argument also applies to the leading quotient in each fixed original rank: the differential and all the cut and unit maps preserve rank there. Every finite rank-block cycle still belongs to a finite corner and has its primitive in that same rank block by C56/C61. No commutation of Hom with an infinite product is being assumed.

Choose the leading splitting contractions on these global acyclic rank blocks. They can retain the full finite forward-closed corners:at fixed outside endpoints every intermediate parameter object lies in the finite forward closure of its initial endpoint. Compute that block in that finite closure. Any forward-closed corner containing the original word already contains that whole closure. Thus the choice is the same on every such corner. If necessary split further by the actual total composite parameter arrow. Differential,unit,ordered cut projection and shuffle all preserve this composite;their finite comparison cones split over those arrow blocks too. The contraction then preserves those original parallel-arrow composite labels. The outside IC words are left fixed in these leading index choices.

The remaining full module terms consume original IC letters or positive index height exactly as in C.56.4.1 and C.61.1.1. Their perturbation series terminates after at most \(R\) factors on any fixed input. Each leading contraction value is an algebraic vector,so is itself a finite sum. The full global contraction therefore produces an actual finite sum on that input. The same argument applies to the rank-by-rank curvature correction of C.57.1.1. Pure core powers,central unary maps and actual parameter composites are kept in the same blocks.

The actual fixed-projection sections and strict native free-cobar lifts in C46/C52 have the same extension. Their mapping kernels contract in these endpoint/composite blocks. Their source unary generator complex is retained,and the remaining original-rank induction is finite on each generator. The fixed-projection defect correction is the full Hom contraction,not a choice based only on the generator's cohomology. Thus they supply genuine global representatives of the one original native functor diagram.

In the coherent path constructions,the original generator has finite string length. Its differential uses shorter strings. Induction over that length defines the global values,one finite algebraic correction at each step. There is no need for a uniform height bound on all objects at once. It retains every given full coherent native family because that original family is the input, not a family reconstructed from unrelated finite edge choices.

Finally all the constructed cofree maps and homotopies preserve any genuine full parameter face. Their outside coactions only cut the original input word;their central value has the original outer endpoint labels and its retained composite arrow. A full face contains those endpoints and all their actual arrows. No new output parameter vertex occurs. This is the central cofree argument of C.52.5.1. Hence restricting the one global map gives a full map or homotopy on each face. Restricting first to either of two faces and then to their intersection is literally the same restriction. This does not require the auxiliary outside contraction to be the separately chosen one for a nonrectangular face. The full forward-corner statements above ensure finite-stage retention as well. This proves all claims with the stated global-choice convention. \(\square\)

C.63.3. One common product normalization for a fixed root profile

Use the actual global root families just described,with the calibrated extension-field comparison of C48 and all original endpoint/string labels retained. The whole native functor and its represented equivalences are fixed before any finite capacity or full face is selected.

Theorem C.63.3.1 (fixed-profile product normalization before restriction). For every finite ordered root profile \(\mathbf n\),the common one-cross source and target models and their comparison can be chosen on the whole \(\mathcal R_{\mathbf n}\) so that their restrictions to every proper ordered root cut are the prescribed ordered products of the smaller-root choices. Their actual full comparison homotopies are one global assignment. Consequently all restrictions to finite capacities,finite forward-closed corners and full parameter faces agree on their overlaps.

These are the independent fixed-profile product marks. A profile-changing joint execution or external several-transition grafting mark is not asserted to be such a restriction.

Proof. Induct on the number of output roots. Fix the single-root native modules and their actual full comparison on their entire \(\mathcal R_n\),using the original native family and its bar/common-core representatives. Theorem C.63.2.1 applies to these global representatives and contractions. The isolated identity strand keeps its original identity module,and a nullary root keeps its original unit-output mapping module.

At \(m>1\),the already chosen models on all shorter consecutive root profiles prescribe their product actions on every proper ordered cut. On refined cut intersections they give the same flat ordered product,including the single final cross shift, by the shorter-root induction. The global rank construction in Theorem C.63.2.1 and C.57.1.1 therefore extend these actions to the whole current parameter product. C.57.2.1 proves all its finer ordered-cut restrictions too.

The actual native finest comparison of C58 exists on this global family by Theorem C.63.2.1:its strict projection square is wordwise,the represented natural transformations come from the one supplied whole native family,and the full fixed projection kernel contractions are the global finite-on-rank ones. C.57.3.1 extends it to an actual old-to-product-normalized module isomorphism. Thus these models retain their original native interpretation,not just their graded central ranks. Use those actual isomorphisms on both sides to interpret the whole calibrated comparison on the new models.

The full native monoidal square now gives the one global finest primitive by C.61.3.1,C.60.3.1 and C.59.2.1,all valid globally by Theorem C.63.2.1. Prescribe the products of the already normalized shorter-root comparisons on every proper cut. Their refined-intersection compatibility is the induction hypothesis and C41's literal graded regrouping. C.59.3.1 extends and glues their homotopies from that one actual finest primitive. Its central Taylor extension and finite inverse give the global comparison with precisely those cut values. This construction is performed once for the entire profile; no unrelated primitive is chosen on an already named finite face. That proves the induction.

Theorem C.63.2.1's cofree restriction argument shows that all finite capacities and full faces now inherit their maps and homotopies by literal restriction. They agree on every overlap for that reason. This establishes a compatible common path for this whole fixed-profile independent-root diagram,which can also be lifted with the original native first family fixed by C62. It is not an assertion that an arbitrary old collection of face homotopies had zero relative obstruction.

On a given whole nested path graph,apply C.51.3.1 using these global one-cross homotopies whenever the sectors carry these same endpoint/string labels. Each string sector receives its choice once;its copies in different finite corners are the same restriction. The logarithm,whole-path coderivation and exponential are finite on every original word as proved in C51. Thus this step retains the several-cross differential and comparison components. It does not make every external grafting map a strict product:the latter has its distinct actual C47 domain and may have higher central components. Those complete external covariance equations remain required before the marked-point descent can be invoked. \(\square\)

C.63.4. Two solved global-index calculations

Exercise C.63.4.1 (parallel contractions and a bar class; intermediate). Take the unary operation chain with three operation vertices above one external leaf. Describe its complete forward contraction category. Compute a nonzero degree-minus-two class in its internal relative index bar,and explain why larger capacities do not remove it.

Solution. Contract either its upper or lower operation edge. These give two distinct arrows \(\alpha,\beta:t_3\to t_2\). There is one remaining-edge contraction \(\gamma:t_2\to t_1\),and \(\gamma\alpha=\gamma\beta=\delta\),the selected contraction of both original edges. These are the same arrows in every capacity \(L\ge3\). The global heights are \(-3,-2,-1\). In the internal relative index bar, \[ z=s\gamma\mid s\alpha-s\gamma\mid s\beta \] is a nonzero degree-minus-two cycle:both summands have differential \(-s\delta\),so they cancel. No length-three index word starts at \(t_3\),so this cycle is not a boundary in that endpoint block. The actual ordered product shuffle retains this cycle and its two distinct contraction labels. Terminality contracts the augmented full nerve;it does not authorize replacing these internal relative-bar words by a single path.

Exercise C.63.4.2 (negative height and a zero-input root; intermediate). Take root0 to be a unary operation above a nullary operation,root1 to be a unary operation above a binary operation with two external leaves,and root2 to be the isolated identity strand. Determine their input-block profile,full forward product corner and heights. State which central mapping factors remain,and check the height differences used in the original-rank bound.

Solution. The input-block profile is \((0,2,1)\). The two nontrivial root forward closures each have two objects,so their product is the actual four-object square,with heights \(-4,-3,-3,-2\). Each edge has positive height jump one,and a diagonal has jump two. Every capacity \(L\ge2\) containing these two-operation roots has exactly that same full forward square. For source tuple \((x_1,x_2,x_3)\) and target tuple \((y_0,y_1,y_2)\),the actual central tensor is \[ \begin{aligned} &H^\bullet\operatorname{RHom}(IC_0,y_0)\\ &\quad\otimes H^\bullet\operatorname{RHom}(x_1*x_2,y_1)\\ &\quad\otimes H^\bullet\operatorname{RHom}(x_3,y_2). \end{aligned} \] The unit-output and identity-strand mapping factors both remain. Increasing the ambient capacity changes none of them. The rank bounds use the displayed height jumps,so they require no shift to a globally nonnegative height on the infinite index.

Lemma C.63.1.1 constructs the actual locally forward finite root index. Theorems C.63.2.1–C.63.3.1 extend the original-rank constructions and normalize the whole fixed-profile product diagram before finite restriction. Exercises C.63.4.1–C.63.4.2 compute the retained parallel class and negative-height corner. Editable SVG source.

C.64. Joint execution and the complete grafting domain

A grafting transition can execute an outer operation after completing an inner tree. Its source and target frontiers can have different arities. The compatible parameter domain retains these joint transitions and every composable string. A product shuffle lies in that domain exactly when its whole prefix rectangle is compatible. This criterion distinguishes complete shuffle maps from a deletion of forbidden terms.

C.64.1. Global joint indices and compatibility

Let \(\mathcal E_n\) be the union of the categories of C.47.1. Its objects are finite operation-rooted planar trees \(t\) with \(n\) ordered external leaves, together with operation-descendant ideals \(J\). Keep every nullary and unary operation vertex. An arrow \((t,J)\longrightarrow(t/K,J')\) remembers its selected original operation-edge set \(K\), and satisfies \(\pi_K(J)\subseteq J'\). Put \[ h(t,J)=-2V(t)+|J|. \tag{C.64.1} \] For an outer tree with \(m\) leaves, write \(B(t,J)\subseteq[m]\) for the external-leaf positions lying below at least one executed operation vertex. For an inner state \(s=(u,I)\), put \(c(s)=1\) exactly when \(I\) contains all operation vertices of \(u\); otherwise put \(c(s)=0\).

Lemma C.64.1.1 (global joint indices and monotone prerequisites). The category \(\mathcal E_n\) is countable, has strictly increasing integer height on nonidentity arrows, and has a finite full forward closure at every object. Its capacity subcategories are full, forward-closed and exhaustive. A chain from \((t,J)\) has length at most \(2V(t)-|J|-1\). The functions \(B\) and \(c\) are nondecreasing along arrows, where subsets are ordered by inclusion.

For \(m,n_i\geq0\), the compatible grafting domain is the full subcategory \[ \mathcal D_{m;\mathbf n}\subseteq \mathcal E_m\times\prod_{i=1}^m\mathcal E_{n_i}, \qquad B(t_0,J_0)\subseteq\{i:c(t_i,J_i)=1\}. \tag{C.64.2} \] It too is locally forward finite and has full exhaustive capacity corners. It need not be forward-closed in its ambient product.

Proof. Composition is C.47.1's lifted union of original contracted edge sets and the final target ideal. It does not use the capacity. Every finite object and composable string lies in some capacity subcategory, so their unchanged composition rules give a category on the union. Countability follows from the finite number of trees, ideals and arrows at each capacity.

For an arrow, let \(k=|K|\), \(I=\pi_K^{-1}(J')\), and let \(k_{\mathrm{ex}}\) count the contracted edges inside the completed target clusters. C.47.1 proves \[ h(t/K,J')-h(t,J) =k+(k-k_{\mathrm{ex}})+(|I|-|J|). \tag{C.64.3} \] Every term is nonnegative. If \(k>0\), the first is positive. If \(k=0\), positivity fails only for unchanged ideal, the identity arrow. Since \(V\geq1\) and \(|J|\leq V\), every target has height at most \(-1\). Strict increase therefore bounds a chain from the specified source by \(-1-h(t,J)=2V(t)-|J|-1\). An absolute nonnegative height is unnecessary.

Every subsequent quotient of \(t\) is obtained by one of its finitely many original operation-edge subsets. Each such quotient has finitely many ideals. These are all possible forward targets; the full category on those targets has finite arrow sets. It is forward-closed because another quotient still comes from one original subset. Capacity cannot increase under an arrow, proving the capacity assertions.

If an external leaf lies below \(v\in J\), its same external position lies below the quotient vertex \(\pi_K(v)\in J'\). Contracting operation edges never removes an external leaf or changes its order. Thus \(B(t,J)\subseteq B(t/K,J')\). If every original vertex is in \(J\), its image is every quotient vertex, so the arrow condition forces \(J'\) to be complete. This proves monotonicity of \(c\).

The union of embedded executed vertices in a graft is an ideal precisely when an executed outer vertex has every attached inner operation descendant executed. The attached inner trees are exactly the leaves in \(B(t_0,J_0)\). Each must be complete; there is no condition on other inner trees. This proves (C.64.2), including inner trees with no external leaves. At \(m=0\) the condition is empty and the domain is just \(\mathcal E_0\).

A finite product of finite full forward closures is finite. Its intersection with the full compatible subcategory contains the entire forward closure inside that subcategory. An arrow in the subcategory cannot increase any factor capacity, so its capacity corners are full and forward-closed there. They exhaust it. For failure of ambient forward closure, take an unexecuted unary outer corolla and an unexecuted nullary inner corolla. The tuple is compatible. Executing only the outer vertex gives an ambient arrow whose target violates (C.64.2). This completes the proof. \(\square\)

C.64.2. Which complete product shuffles lie in the domain

Set \(n_0=m\) and use the actual reduced category bars \(D_i=B(k\mathcal E_{n_i})\), with the outer factor indexed by \(i=0\). A factor word records a finite composable string of nonidentity arrows, including its endpoints. A length-zero word records its object. In a tensor of factor words \(w_0\otimes\cdots \otimes w_m\), write \(s_i^-\) and \(s_i^+\) for the first and last objects of the \(i\)-th word. The tensor's prefix rectangle consists of all tuples of vertices obtained by independently choosing a prefix of each factor word. Call this tensor word safe when \[ B(s_0^+)\subseteq\{i:c(s_i^-)=1\}. \tag{C.64.4} \] All labels here are original category labels, including parallel contraction arrows. Let \(S\) be the span of safe tensor words in \(D_0\otimes\cdots\otimes D_m\).

Theorem C.64.2.1 (the exact complete-shuffle domain). The prefix rectangle is contained in \(\mathcal D_{m;\mathbf n}\) if and only if (C.64.4) holds. The span \(S\) is a differential graded subcoalgebra, with its colored coaugmentations. The entire usual signed shuffle restricts to a chain coalgebra injection \[ \operatorname{sh}:S\longrightarrow B(k\mathcal D_{m;\mathbf n}). \tag{C.64.5} \] Within the tensor of the actual factor word bases, \(S\) is exactly the linear preimage of \(B(k\mathcal D_{m;\mathbf n})\) under the ordinary shuffle into the ambient product bar. This assertion includes finite linear combinations, not only individual words.

On the sector where the outer ideal is empty at every vertex of its word, every tensor word is safe. General compatible joint transitions are retained in \(B(k\mathcal D_{m;\mathbf n})\), even when they are absent from the safe product-shuffle image.

Proof. Along the outer word the sets \(B\) increase, and along each inner word completeness can only increase, by Lemma C.64.1.1. If (C.64.4) holds, every prefix tuple therefore satisfies (C.64.2). Conversely the prefix tuple with the outer word finished and every inner word at its beginning is in the rectangle. Its compatibility is exactly (C.64.4). This proves the criterion.

Every prefix tuple occurs in some complete interleaving: first take its chosen prefixes, preserving each factor's order, and then take their remaining suffixes. A shuffle term's vertices are prefix tuples. Thus every shuffle term lies in the compatible full subcategory precisely when the full prefix rectangle does. Fullness is relevant here: the simultaneous composite arrows arising in the bar differential are actual arrows of the subcategory whenever their endpoints lie there.

The reduced internal bar differential composes two adjacent arrows in a factor word. It retains that word's endpoints and removes one intermediate vertex. Therefore it preserves (C.64.4). There are no other terms, since the linear categories have degree-zero arrows and zero internal differential. The tensor differential includes its usual Koszul signs and consequently preserves \(S\).

In a term of the tensor coproduct each factor word is cut into a prefix and a suffix. For the prefix tensor, the outer final \(B\) is contained in the old final \(B\), and every inner initial state is unchanged. It is safe. For the suffix tensor, the outer final state is unchanged and every inner initial state occurs later in its word, so its completeness is at least the old initial completeness. It too is safe. All coproduct terms thus lie in \(S\otimes S\). The compatible object identities give exactly the length-zero safe words and their coaugmentations. This proves the subcoalgebra statement, with the inherited tensor coproduct signs.

The full shuffle on bars of degree-zero categories is the signed interleaving map proved in C.34.2 and C.42.1. Its differential cancellation pairs opposite orders of adjacent arrows from different factors; arrows in the same factor give that factor's bar differential. Its coalgebra identity cuts each interleaving at every prefix, with the tensor Koszul sign. These complete identities restrict to \(S\), since every term now lies in the indicated subcoalgebras. This proves the chain and coalgebra assertions in (C.64.5).

For injectivity and the claimed linear preimage, each interleaving has arrows supported in exactly one factor at each step. The nonidentity factor and its original arrow label are recoverable from that product arrow. Reading those steps in their original order recovers each factor word, including its endpoints. Thus different tensor word basis elements have disjoint shuffle supports. Within a single shuffle, the different interleavings also give distinct product-bar basis words and have coefficients \(1\) or \(-1\). This uses the actual arrow labels and holds for parallel arrows. No coefficient can cancel a forbidden interleaving coming from another tensor word. A linear combination has shuffle support entirely in the full compatible bar exactly when every tensor basis word occurring with nonzero coefficient is safe. This proves both assertions.

When the outer ideals are all empty, \(B(s_0^+)=\varnothing\), so the criterion imposes no condition on inner factors. This is precisely the native external-product sector of C.47.3. In general (C.64.2) permits a transition which first completes an inner tree and then executes an outer vertex depending on it. Such a transition need not satisfy (C.64.4) for its separate factor words. It remains an ordinary composable string, and its simultaneous composite remains an arrow, in the full compatible bar. \(\square\)

C.64.3. The full graft map and finite original-word bounds

Theorem C.64.3.1 (full joint grafting and its original domains). Literal grafting defines a functor \[ \mathfrak g:\mathcal D_{m;\mathbf n}\longrightarrow \mathcal E_N,\qquad N=\sum_{i=1}^m n_i, \tag{C.64.6} \] which preserves the sum of the heights (C.64.1), retains the selected edge labels, and sends every nonidentity arrow to a nonidentity arrow. It induces the genuine chain coalgebra map \[ B\mathfrak g:B(k\mathcal D_{m;\mathbf n}) \longrightarrow B(k\mathcal E_N). \tag{C.64.7} \] The composite with (C.64.5) is the complete product shuffle followed by grafting on its exact safe domain. No clipping of unsafe shuffles defines (C.64.7). Nested grafts and restrictions to full parameter faces commute on their actual common domains.

Every finite joint or grafting string and its native enhanced functors and higher comparison cells are contained in finite capacity corners. Their native interpretation and its extension-field comparison are the original ones of C.47.2–3 and C.29. The total original-word rank \[ R=r+\sum_{\text{outside runs}}\Delta h \tag{C.64.8} \] is nonnegative and bounds the total number of nonidentity outside index letters plus the \(r\) original IC primitive letters. It is preserved by grafting of outside index runs. A frontier-changing arrow uses its actual source and target arities; it is not replaced by a tensor power at a fixed arity.

Proof. Choose any finite factor capacities containing a source object and its considered finite strings. The exact compatibility criterion is Lemma C.64.1.1, which is independent of capacities. C.47.3 then grafts the tuple, keeps every factor's operation vertex and joining seam, and embeds the disjoint selected factor-edge subsets without selecting a seam. Its quotient is the graft of the factor quotients. Its executed union is an ideal by compatibility. The original edge-union composition rule is unchanged at larger capacities. It therefore defines the global functor (C.64.6).

There are exactly \(\sum_i V_i\) operation vertices and \(\sum_i|J_i|\) executed vertices in its object image. Consequently \[ h(\mathfrak g(s_0;\ldots,s_m))=\sum_{i=0}^m h(s_i). \tag{C.64.9} \] A nonempty selected factor-edge set remains nonempty in the disjoint embedded union and reduces the grafted vertex count. If every selected edge set is empty but an execution ideal strictly increases, the disjoint executed union strictly increases. These are all nonidentity arrows. Thus the functor never turns a nonidentity into an identity. Different selected sets at a fixed decomposed source retain their distinct embedded labels. Distinct decomposed objects may have the same flattened tree; injectivity on all object colors is not asserted.

On a reduced bar word, apply \(\mathfrak g\) to each arrow, retaining every letter. The output is reduced by noncollapse. Its coproduct is still word cutting. Its differential composes adjacent arrows with the original suspended sign; the functor equation sends their composite to the composite of their images. Hence it is a chain coalgebra map. This proof includes an arrow in which several factors change at once and every higher composable string in the full compatible category. Restricting this map to the complete shuffle image gives the stated composite.

For nested grafts, C.47.3's two groupings have the same embedded operation vertices, seams and executed union. Their common compatibility condition is that this final union be an ideal. Selected contractions are the same lifted embedded unions, so the functors, and therefore their bar maps, agree on that common domain. For a full target face on an object set \(T\), restrict the source to the full subcategory on \(\mathfrak g^{-1}(T)\). Every arrow in it maps to the full face on \(T\), giving the actual restriction square. Pulling back two object sets commutes with intersection; successive face restrictions agree literally. This is a statement about those colored restriction maps. Because different decompositions can flatten to the same object, it does not identify the linear preimage of a face subspace under a noninjective flattened bar map with a basis-support subspace.

A finite list of factor trees has finite maximum capacities. All its forward quotients remain within them by Lemma C.64.1.1, and its grafts remain within their sum. C.47.2 constructs the actual partial-forest functor of each arrow from arbitrary source frontier variables. Its saturation ideal is \(\pi_K^{-1}(J')\), so the source frontier arity is \(n+\sum_{v\in J}(1-r(v))\) and the target arity is the corresponding quantity in the quotient. These can differ. Every such arity in the finite forward closure is bounded by the source leaf count plus its vertex capacity. Finite IC generator selections can be closed under forward images in this finite directed diagram by C.47.2's height induction. Thus its full enhanced native strings, the graft comparisons and all their higher cells are the finite-corner constructions already proved there. Those constructions are defined by the original partial forests, tensor, proper and unit maps; none depends on unused larger-capacity trees. Their restrictions agree. C.29's actual full comparison carries these same maps and all their coherent cells after coefficient extension. Taking their compatible finite restrictions proves the global assertion without independently choosing edge comparisons.

Finally each nonidentity index letter has positive integer height jump by (C.64.3). A run of \(q\) such letters therefore has \(q\leq\Delta h\). Summing proves the bound in (C.64.8). The height is bounded above, not below globally, but its endpoint jumps are positive and telescope; this is all that the bound uses. Equation (C.64.9) preserves those summed endpoint jumps under grafting. Original IC letters are unchanged by an index graft. This proves rank preservation. Any use of this index map with the native functors must keep the actual frontier arities just computed. The theorem supplies their full parameter domain and native interpretation; it does not replace them by a fixed-profile product. \(\square\)

C.64.4. Solved calculations

Exercise C.64.4.1 (intermediate; the first unsafe square). Graft a nullary inner corolla below a unary outer corolla. Record states by \((o,i)\in\{0,1\}^2\), where a one means that the corresponding vertex is executed. Determine the compatible domain and the reduced bar differential after retaining only allowed interleavings of the tensor of the two execution arrows.

Solution. Compatibility is \(o\leq i\). The full domain is the three-object chain \(00<01<11\), including its direct composite \(\delta:00\to11\); \(10\) is forbidden. The graft has two operation vertices, so their heights are \(-4,-3,-2\). Their frontiers have respectively \(0,1,1\) factors. Write \(\alpha:00\to01\) and \(\beta:01\to11\). The first functor is the actual unit output, and the second is the unary operation on that arbitrary output factor. Its mapping complex is retained.

The factor tensor is not safe: the outer final executed vertex requires the inner to be complete initially, whereas its initial state is zero. Its full signed shuffle has two terms. In chronological storage, the term inner-then-outer has coefficient \(+1\), and outer-then-inner has coefficient \(-1\). In target-to-source suspended notation the allowed term is \(w=s\beta\mid s\alpha\). The programme convention \(b_2(sb\mid sa)=-s(ba)\) for degree-zero arrows gives \[ b(w)=-s\delta\ne0. \tag{C.64.EX1} \] The tensor of two single-arrow bar words has differential zero. Clipping its other interleaving therefore fails the chain equation. The full compatible bar retains both \(w\) and \(s\delta\), with precisely (C.64.EX1); there is no failure in that genuine bar complex.

Exercise C.64.4.2 (advanced; two units under one binary operation). Take the binary outer corolla and two nullary inner corollas. Among the tensor bars of their three two-state execution categories, determine the safe-word dimension and compare it with the whole compatible bar. Count the allowed interleavings of the tensor of all three execution arrows.

Solution. With coordinates \((o,l,r)\), compatibility is \(o=0\) or \(l=r=1\). There are five objects \[ 000,\quad010,\quad001,\quad011,\quad111. \tag{C.64.EX2a} \] Their heights are respectively \(-6,-5,-5,-4,-3\), and their frontier arities are \(0,1,1,2,1\). The last arrow executes the actual binary convolution of its two arbitrary frontier factors.

Each two-state factor bar has basis the two object words and its one-arrow word, so the full tensor has dimension \(3^3=27\). If the outer word is the empty word at state zero, all \(3^2=9\) inner pairs are safe. The other two outer basis words end at state one; each then requires both inner words to begin at one. Each inner word must therefore be the empty word at one. This contributes two more, giving \(\dim S=11\).

The full compatible category is the poset on (C.64.EX2a). It has nine strict arrows, seven strict two-arrow strings, and two strict three-arrow strings, in addition to its five objects. Its whole reduced bar has dimension \(5+9+7+2=23\). In particular the simultaneous arrow \(000\to111\) is retained even though the tensor of the three separate execution arrows is unsafe. Among its six interleavings, exactly the two which execute both inner units before the outer operation stay in the compatible domain. This count does not turn their clipped signed sum into a replacement for the full bar. Theorem C.64.3.1 uses all 23 actual words and their composition differential.

Lemma C.64.1.1 gives the positive height jumps and prerequisites. Theorem C.64.2.1 characterizes complete product shuffles, and Theorem C.64.3.1 gives the whole grafting bar map. Exercises C.64.4.1–C.64.4.2 compute the unit and binary domains. Editable SVG source.

C.65. Entire coherent strings and staged model contractions

Transport through a chosen model contraction acts on the full coherent diagram, including its higher components and its path comparison. Consecutive partitions give explicit finite formulas. Nested partitions show that staged contractions give exactly the same transported diagram as their composite contraction. These statements concern diagrams in a single specified dg category, with all map types retained.

C.65.1. Every component of the transported coherent diagram

Let \(I\) be a directed category with its actual parallel-arrow labels. It may be countable and locally forward finite, as in C64. Let \(\mathcal A\) be a dg category. For each object \(s\) choose objects \(X_s,Q_s\) and normalized contraction data in \(\mathcal A\): \[ \begin{gathered} p_s:X_s\to Q_s,\\ i_s:Q_s\to X_s,\\ p_si_s=1,\\ \partial h_s=1-i_sp_s,\\ h_s^2=p_sh_s=h_si_s=0. \end{gathered} \tag{C.65.1} \] The maps \(i_s,p_s\) are closed of degree zero; \(h_s\) has degree minus one. Suppose the entire normalized dg functor \(F:\Omega B(kI)\to\mathcal A\), with objects \(X_s\), is given. For a nonempty composable string \(c=(f_1,\ldots,f_q)\), written chronologically, write \(F[c]\) for its free cobar generator image. Its degree is \(1-q\). The suspended bar word reads in the opposite order. Write \(c/j\) for the string composing its \(j\)-th and \((j+1)\)-st arrows, and \(c_{\le j},c_{>j}\) for its prefix and suffix at that vertex. In the programme convention the generator equation is \[ \begin{aligned} \partial F[c] &=\sum_{j=1}^{q-1}(-1)^{q-j} F[c/j]\\ &\quad+\sum_{j=1}^{q-1}(-1)^{q-j+1}\\ &\qquad\cdot F[c_{>j}]F[c_{\le j}]. \end{aligned} \tag{C.65.2} \] For \(q=1\) the sums are empty. This is C.39.15/C.43.6 on the actual degree-zero index category; in particular the two-arrow generator has differential \(F[f_2]F[f_1]-F[f_2f_1]\).

Partition the chronological string into nonempty consecutive blocks \(c_1,\ldots,c_r\). Between two blocks the indicated \(h\) is at their shared original object. Write \(\Pi_F(c_r,\ldots,c_1)\) for the ordered composite \(F[c_r]h\cdots hF[c_1]\), with one \(h\) at each block seam. Put \[ \begin{aligned} U[c]&=\sum_{c=c_1\cdots c_r}(-1)^{r-1}\\ &\quad\cdot p_{s_q}\Pi_F(c_r,\ldots,c_1),\\ T[c]&=U[c]i_{s_0},\\ A[c]&=(-1)^{q-1}U[c]h_{s_0}. \end{aligned} \tag{C.65.3} \] There are \(2^{q-1}\) partitions, so these are finite sums.

Theorem C.65.1.1 (explicit full coherent transport). The assignments \(T[c]\) give a normalized dg functor \(T:\Omega B(kI)\to\mathcal A\) with objects \(Q_s\). The triples \[ \bigl(F[c],T[c],A[c]\bigr) \tag{C.65.4} \] give an entire dg functor to the path category of C.53.4, whose object at \(s\) is \(p_s:X_s\to Q_s\). Thus this is an actual coherent comparison with the original full diagram, with its prescribed object projections, not merely a collection of edge comparisons.

The construction preserves restriction to every full parameter face and to their intersections, when one family (C.65.1) has been chosen before restriction. It retains parallel arrows and all original composable strings. No uniform global height bound is required for the finite sums in (C.65.3).

Proof. Every term of \(U[c]\) has degree \(1-q\), since its \(r\) functor components contribute \(r-q\) and its \(r-1\) homotopies contribute \(1-r\). Thus \(T[c]\) has the required degree and \(A[c]\) has degree \(-q\). The endpoints and every intermediate object are those of the original string.

Differentiate (C.65.3) using the full Hom derivation rule. Terms from differentiating an \(F\)-block split into its internal adjacent-arrow merges and its two-block products, by (C.65.2). An internal merge has exactly the corresponding term on the first line of (C.65.2) for \(T\). Indeed if it merges the arrows at original position \(j\), the degree of all terms to the left of its block, including the intervening homotopies, is congruent modulo two to the number of arrows in the chronological suffix after that block. Adding the block's internal sign gives \((-1)^{q-j}\). The partition sign remains \((-1)^{r-1}\).

Consider a seam between blocks, with \(L\) original arrows in its chronological suffix, on its target side. Differentiating its \(h\) gives \(1-ip\). With \(r\) blocks the coefficient of its identity term is \((-1)^{r+L}\): the \(F\)-blocks and homotopies to its left have total degree congruent to \(L+1\), and the partition contributes \((-1)^{r-1}\). The product term obtained by differentiating the merged block of the corresponding \((r-1)\)-block partition has coefficient \((-1)^{r-1+L}\). These cancel. This pairs every identity seam with exactly one functor-component product.

The remaining \(-ip\) seam has coefficient \((-1)^{r+L+1}\). Cutting the whole string at that seam gives the product of the corresponding two terms of \(T\). Their partition signs multiply to \((-1)^{r-2}\), while the cobar cut has sign \((-1)^{L+1}\). The product is \((-1)^{r+L-1}\), the same coefficient. Thus all remaining seams are exactly the second line of (C.65.2) for \(T\). This proves its generator equation. Extension to the free cobar by composition and object units is consequently a dg functor.

For the path assertion use the differential and product of C.53.4: \[ \begin{gathered} D(f,g,a)=(\partial f,\partial g,\\ \qquad-\partial a+p_tf-gp_s),\\ (f_2,g_2,a_2)(f_1,g_1,a_1)\\ \quad=(f_2f_1,g_2g_1,\\ \qquad a_2f_1+(-1)^{|f_2|}g_2a_1). \end{gathered} \tag{C.65.5} \] For clarity, the calculation just made, before its final \(i\), gives the full identity \[ \begin{aligned} \partial U[c]&=\sum_j(-1)^{q-j}U[c/j]\\ &\quad+\sum_j(-1)^{q-j+1}\\ &\qquad\cdot T[c_{>j}]U[c_{\le j}], \end{aligned} \tag{C.65.6} \] where \(c/j\) composes its \(j\)-th and \((j+1)\)-st arrows. Its product terms close the suffix component with \(i\) at the cut, while the prefix component retains its original \(X\)-source. Its signs follow from precisely the same two seam counts. For a one-arrow string all sums vanish: \(\partial U=0\). Grouping the partitions by their first chronological block also gives the exact recursion \[ \begin{aligned} p_{s_q}F[c]-U[c] &=\sum_j U[c_{>j}]\\ &\qquad\cdot h_{s_j}F[c_{\le j}]. \end{aligned} \]

Multiply (C.65.6) on the right by \(h_{s_0}\), use \(\partial h=1-ip\), and multiply by \((-1)^{q-1}\). The Hom derivation sign of \(U[c]\) is \((-1)^{1-q}\). The resulting identity is exactly \[ \begin{aligned} &-\partial A[c]+p_{s_q}F[c]\\ &\qquad-T[c]p_{s_0}\\ &\quad=\sum_j(-1)^{q-j}A[c/j]\\ &\qquad+\sum_j(-1)^{q-j+1}\\ &\qquad\quad\cdot A[c_{>j}]F[c_{\le j}]\\ &\qquad+\sum_j T[c_{>j}]A[c_{\le j}]. \end{aligned} \tag{C.65.7} \] The displayed recursion gives the terms containing \(A[c_{>j}]F[c_{\le j}]\) and \(pF\). Equation (C.65.7) is the third component of (C.65.2) for (C.65.4), using (C.65.5) and \(|F[c_{>j}]|=1-(q-j)\). Its first two components were proved above. This proves the entire path functor.

Ordinary identity arguments normalize correctly. A block of length greater than one containing an identity has zero native component. A singleton identity block gives \(ph=0\) at the target end, \(hi=0\) at the source end of \(T\), or \(h^2=0\) internally. For \(A\) the source end also gives \(h^2=0\). The one-letter identity has \(T[1]=pi=1\) and \(A[1]=ph=0\). Thus the usual unital normalization is retained.

All blocks are consecutive parts of the original word. Their composite arrows and endpoints stay in every full subcategory containing its vertices. No additional intermediate vertex is introduced. Choosing the data globally therefore makes both functors and the path restrict term by term; two face restrictions agree on their intersection. At each finite word the sums are finite regardless of the size or negative absolute heights of the index. Every retained arrow is its original label, so parallel arrows are not identified. \(\square\)

C.65.2. Successive contractions give the same entire transport

Suppose each \(Q_s\) has a second normalized contraction \(q_s:Q_s\to R_s\), \(j_s:R_s\to Q_s\), \(k_s\), with \(q_sj_s=1\) and \(\partial k_s=1-j_sq_s\).

Theorem C.65.2.1 (strict staged transport identity). The composite contraction from \(X_s\) to \(R_s\) is \[ \begin{aligned} P_s&=q_sp_s,\quad I_s=i_sj_s,\\ H_s&=h_s+i_sk_sp_s. \end{aligned} \tag{C.65.8} \] Transporting the entire coherent \(F\) first by \((p,i,h)\) and then by \((q,j,k)\) gives exactly the same component on every original string as applying (C.65.3) once using (C.65.8). This is equality of all Taylor components, not just equality of the edge classes. Three or more stages associate strictly. Full-face restrictions preserve this identity.

Proof. The maps \(P,I\) are closed and \(PI=qpij=qj=1\). The Hom derivation identity gives \[ \partial H=(1-ip)+i(1-jq)p=1-IP. \] Also \(H^2=0\): its four terms vanish by \(h^2=hi=ph=k^2=0\) and \(pi=1\). The equations \(PH=HI=0\) follow from the same identities and \(qk=kj=0\). Thus this is the required normalized contraction.

Expand the two uses of (C.65.3). A second-stage partition divides the original string into larger blocks. Within each larger block choose the first-stage partition defining its component. The resulting fine partition has a seam of type \(h\) inside a larger block and a seam of type \(ikp\) between larger blocks. Conversely every fine partition whose seams are independently marked with these two types determines uniquely those two stages of partitions: group blocks across the \(h\)-seams. The resulting ordered composite has the common end maps \(qp\) and \(ij\).

If there are \(r\) fine blocks and \(a\) large blocks, the first-stage partition signs multiply to \((-1)^{r-a}\), and the second-stage sign is \((-1)^{a-1}\). Their product is \((-1)^{r-1}\). No permutation of a map is used; the maps are in the identical target-to-source order. Hence there is no additional Koszul sign. Summing the two seam types gives \(h+ikp=H\) at every seam. This is precisely the single-stage formula using (C.65.8), with matching signs and endpoints.

For three stages the composite homotopy is, in either grouping, \(h_1+i_1h_2p_1+i_1i_2h_3p_2p_1\); the projection and inclusion are the same ordered composites. The two-stage identity therefore proves associativity for three, and induction proves every finite number of stages. All partition identities are on the original string, so commute with the full-face restrictions of Theorem C.65.1.1. The theorem asserts equality of the transported functors; it does not assert that independently chosen auxiliary path homotopies are equal. \(\square\)

C.65.3. Even cohomology does not remove long coherent components

Proposition C.65.3.1 (arbitrarily long nonzero transferred components). For every odd \(N\geq3\) there is a strict diagram of finite cochain complexes on \([N]=\{0<1<\cdots<N\}\), with normalized contractions to complexes supported in even degrees, for which (C.65.3) has a nonzero component on its length-\(N\) consecutive string. Every positive-length component of smaller length is zero. The original strict diagram has no higher components.

Proof. At zero take \(X_0=Q_0=kx\) in degree zero. At \(N\) take \(X_N=Q_N=kz\) in degree \(1-N\), which is even. For \(1\leq j\leq N-1\), take \[ \begin{aligned} X_j&=ke_j\oplus ka_j\oplus kb_j,\\ |e_j|&=0,\quad |a_j|=-j,\\ |b_j|&=1-j,\quad da_j=b_j. \end{aligned} \tag{C.65.9} \] All other differentials are zero. Put \(Q_j=ke_j\), let \(p_j,i_j\) be its projection and inclusion, and set \(h_jb_j=a_j\), with \(h_j\) zero on the other basis vectors. These are normalized contractions. At the two endpoints use the identity contraction and zero homotopy.

The first adjacent arrow sends \(x\) to \(b_1\). For \(2\leq j\leq N-1\), the \(j\)-th adjacent arrow sends \(a_{j-1}\) to \(b_j\) and all other basis vectors to zero. The last adjacent arrow sends \(a_{N-1}\) to \(z\) and all other basis vectors to zero. These are degree-zero chain maps. Every product of two adjacent arrows is zero, because an arrow's image lies in a \(b\)-line, which the next arrow kills. Set every nonadjacent strict arrow to zero. Together with identity maps this is a strict diagram on the full category \([N]\), not just on its adjacent-arrow quiver.

In (C.65.3) every native block of length greater than one is zero. Thus for the full consecutive string there is one contributing partition, into single arrows. Starting with \(x\), its ordered composite successively visits \[ \begin{aligned} x&\longmapsto b_1\longmapsto a_1\longmapsto b_2\\ &\longmapsto a_2\longmapsto\cdots\\ &\longmapsto a_{N-1}\longmapsto z. \end{aligned} \tag{C.65.10} \] Its coefficient is \((-1)^{N-1}=1\), so \(T[0,1,\ldots,N](x)=z\). If a string starts after zero, its source inclusion lands in an \(e\)-line and its first nonidentity arrow kills that line. If it starts at zero but ends before \(N\), its last projection kills its \(b\)-line image. If it skips a vertex, a nonadjacent native arrow is zero. These exhaust every other positive-length string. Thus all shorter components vanish, as claimed.

This proves that even cohomology alone does not force a transported coherent diagram to have only edge components. It does not assert that the displayed long component is invariant under all changes of coherent representative. The statement concerns the exact full transport with the specified native diagram and specified contractions. \(\square\)

C.65.4. Solved calculations

Exercise C.65.4.1 (intermediate; the complete length-three transport). For Proposition C.65.3.1 with \(N=3\), compute the transferred edge, two-arrow and three-arrow components. Remove only the first intermediate acyclic pair at the first stage. Compute the first-stage component on \((0,1,2)\) and its contribution to the second-stage three-arrow component.

Solution. The full transport has all edge and two-arrow components zero. Its only nonzero positive-length component is \[ \begin{gathered} T[0,1,2,3](x)\\ =F[2,3]h_2F[1,2]\\ \qquad\cdot h_1F[0,1](x)\\ =z. \end{gathered} \tag{C.65.EX1} \] The coefficient is positive because its partition has three blocks. If the first stage removes just the pair at object one, the component \(T^{(1)}[0,1,2]\) sends \(x\) to \(-b_2\). Object two has not yet been contracted, so that output remains. At the second stage the two-block partition with blocks \((0,1,2)\) and \((2,3)\) contributes \(-F[2,3]h_2T^{(1)}[0,1,2](x)=z\). Replacing the first-stage functor by its edge maps would lose this term. The intermediate cohomology lines are degree zero and the final one has degree minus two; they are all even.

Exercise C.65.4.2 (advanced; a higher path component with zero transported two-arrow component). In the same example compute \(A[1,2,3]\) and verify the third path equation on \(a_1\). Explain what would fail if this higher path component were omitted while keeping its prescribed edge path components.

Solution. The native two-arrow component is zero. Formula (C.65.3) has \(q=2\), so the minus sign in \(A=(-1)^{q-1}Uh_1\) cancels the minus sign of the two-block term in \(U\). Consequently \[ \begin{gathered} A[1,2,3]\\ =p_3F[2,3]h_2\\ \qquad\cdot F[1,2]h_1,\\ A[1,2,3](b_1)=z. \end{gathered} \tag{C.65.EX2} \] It is zero on the other source basis vectors. Its degree is minus two. Since \(da_1=b_1\), the full Hom differential gives \(\partial A[1,2,3](a_1)=-z\). Meanwhile \(A[2,3](b_2)=z\), and all other terms on the right of (C.65.7) vanish on \(a_1\). Thus that equation reads \(-\partial A(a_1)=z\), exactly \(A[2,3]F[1,2](a_1)\). The corresponding transported two-arrow component is zero because its source inclusion lands in \(ke_1\), which \(F[1,2]\) kills. Omitting the displayed higher path component would therefore break its actual chain equation even though the transported two-arrow component itself is zero.

Theorem C.65.1.1 gives every transported component and the full path comparison. Theorem C.65.2.1 proves strict staged transport, and Proposition C.65.3.1 constructs arbitrary-length examples with even cohomology. Exercises C.65.4.1–C.65.4.2 compute the length-three and higher path signs. Editable SVG source.

C.66. Typed kernel models and coherence lifting

Kernel composition retains the pure core at each intermediate frontier. Tagging kernels by their original source and target states puts the consecutive-block products of a fixed string in one dg category. Their ordered cotensor contractions associate exactly. A canonical-state projection also gives an acyclic kernel on the full normalized natural-transformation complexes; this is the kernel needed to lift specified coherent operator diagrams with their object functors fixed.

C.66.1. A common dg category with all frontier types retained

Fix finitely many state labels \(S\). At state \(s\) let the pure coalgebra be \(C_s=C^{\otimes m_s}\), with its actual coefficient object labels, where \(m_s\geq0\). Distinct states retain distinct copies even when their frontier arities agree. At \(m_s=0\) the pure coalgebra is the genuine coefficient coalgebra. Put \[ \begin{gathered} K=\bigoplus_{s\in S}C_s,\\ E=\bigoplus_{s\in S}E_s, \end{gathered} \tag{C.66.1} \] where \(E_s\) is its split identity coefficient algebra and \(K\) is a relative dg coalgebra over \(E\). Work at finite IC corners first, so the coefficient algebra is split semisimple. Write \(\mathsf{Bicomod}(K)\) for the dg category of dg \(K\)-bicomodules and homogeneous bicomodule maps, with the full Hom differential.

Lemma C.66.1.1 (typed zero extension). Every ordinary dg \((C_t,C_s)\)-bicomodule extends by zero to an object of \(\mathsf{Bicomod}(K)\). Its full homogeneous mapping complex to another object of that same outer type is unchanged. Its mapping complex to an object with a different source or target state label is zero.

For a fixed original composable string of joint arrows, the ordinary cotensor products associated with all its consecutive block partitions have the same outer endpoint type. Thus all those products and their properly typed kernel comparison maps are objects and maps in one dg category, even when intermediate frontier arities change.

Proof. Include each of the two original coaction coalgebras in its summand of \(K\). The old coactions, followed by these inclusions, give the new coactions. Counits, coassociativity and their compatibility are unchanged. Their differential equations are also unchanged, so this is a dg bicomodule. Its coefficient support is exactly \(E_tME_s\).

A homogeneous bicomodule map commutes with the left and right coefficient coactions. Equivalently, after taking counits on the coefficient components, it commutes with the state idempotents on both sides. A map from support \(E_tME_s\) to support \(E_vNE_u\) is therefore zero unless \(v=t\) and \(u=s\): applying the target idempotent \(e_t\) or the source idempotent \(e_s\) gives its entire source value on one side and zero on the other. When the two types agree, the enlarged coaction equations reduce to exactly the old two coaction equations. The map spaces and the Hom differential are identical. This proves all mapping assertions.

The ordinary kernel of an arrow \(f:s\to t\) has target coaction \(C_t\) and source coaction \(C_s\). In any composable sequence the adjacent target and source colors match at their shared state. Cotensoring over that shared coalgebra leaves precisely the outer target and source coactions. The same is true after grouping consecutive blocks. Each partition therefore has the same original outer type. This proves the last claim. It does not replace a kernel product by the kernel of its composite arrow: that replacement requires its actual comparison map. \(\square\)

C.66.2. Ordinary cotensor paths and their normalized contractions

Use ordinary one-cross kernels \(M_f=K(Z_f)=Z_f[-1]\) as in C.41.2. For two successive arrows suppose their graded bicomodules are cofree: \[ \begin{gathered} X=C_u\otimes N_X\otimes C_t,\\ Y=C_t\otimes N_Y\otimes C_s. \end{gathered} \tag{C.66.2} \] All tensor products retain their coefficient balancing. Their differentials may contain the full higher source and target module actions. Suppose \(I_X,P_X,H_X\) and \(I_Y,P_Y,H_Y\) are normalized dg bicomodule contractions over the identity pure cores, and put \(E_X=I_XP_X\).

Theorem C.66.2.1 (typed cotensor contraction and regrouping). The ordinary cotensor \(X\square_{C_t}Y\) is canonically the graded bicomodule \[ \begin{gathered} C_u\otimes N_X\otimes C_t\\ \qquad\otimes N_Y\otimes C_s, \end{gathered} \tag{C.66.3} \] with its induced full differential. Its contraction has inclusion and projection given by the two factor maps on the cotensor, and homotopy \[ H=H_X\otimes1+E_X\otimes H_Y \tag{C.66.4} \] restricted to that equalizer, with its graded tensor evaluation signs. Iterating in the original target-to-source order gives the same contraction in every parenthesization. All intermediate pure cores remain in (C.66.3) and its longer analogues.

For a path of \(q\) successive ordinary kernels, the corresponding whole graph sector has \(q\) cross suspensions. Independent ordered output roots have the single final cross suspension of C.41.4. The two statements retain their respective types and degree shifts.

Proof. Define the inclusion of (C.66.3) in \(X\otimes Y\) by coproduct on its sole middle \(C_t\)-factor: \[ \begin{gathered} c\otimes x\otimes a\otimes y\otimes b\\ \longmapsto\sum c\otimes x\otimes a_{(1)}\\ \qquad\otimes a_{(2)}\otimes y\otimes b. \end{gathered} \tag{C.66.5} \] Coassociativity puts its image in the cotensor equalizer. Applying the counit to one of the two middle copies is an inverse on the image. Conversely apply that same counit to the equalizer equation of an arbitrary element of \(X\otimes Y\). It states that the element is exactly (C.66.5) applied after that counit. This proves surjectivity onto the full equalizer as well. The two coactions defining the equalizer are chain maps; thus it has the induced differential with every original higher action. This is an explicit cofree calculation and makes no assertion that arbitrary cotensor functors are exact.

Every factor map preserves both coactions, with the homogeneous tensor sign for a map of degree minus one. Consequently their tensors preserve the cotensor equalizer. The maps \(I,P\) satisfy \(PI=1\). On the ambient tensor differential, the full Hom derivation rule gives \[ \begin{gathered} \partial H=(1-E_X)\otimes1\\ \qquad+E_X\otimes(1-E_Y)\\ =1-E_X\otimes E_Y. \end{gathered} \tag{C.66.6} \] This restricts to the equalizer. The side conditions also restrict: \(PH=HI=0\), and in \(H^2\) each mixed term contains either \(H_XE_X\) or \(E_XH_X\), while the two diagonal terms contain \(H_X^2\) or \(H_Y^2\). All are zero. Thus these are the full normalized contraction identities.

For three factors, both groupings identify with the subspace in the original threefold tensor satisfying the two middle equalizer equations. Coassociativity of the two middle coproducts identifies it with the same cofree ordered expression. Both grouped homotopies expand to \[ \begin{gathered} H_1\otimes1\otimes1\\ \quad+E_1\otimes H_2\otimes1\\ \quad+E_1\otimes E_2\otimes H_3. \end{gathered} \] Their Koszul evaluation signs are those of these same ordered graded maps.
