Inclusions and projections are likewise the same ordered tensors. Induction proves every parenthesization. Each middle pure core occurs once in the cofree expression (C.66.3), so none has been counited away.

Restoring the crossed bar sector suspends each of its \(q\) successive central mapping factors, lowering degree by \(q\). In the independent root product C.41.4 first takes the ordinary tensor of all root kernels and then suspends once. These are the indicated two formulas. At a zero frontier the matching middle coalgebra is the coefficient coalgebra; cotensor there is the corresponding balanced ordinary tensor. All central mapping factors, including a unit-output kernel, still occur. No unary operation vertex or graft seam is removed by the cotensor identification. \(\square\)

C.66.3. The specific full natural-transformation kernel is acyclic

Let \(A\) be an augmented unital dg input category over its split identity coefficients, using its actual normalized reduced bar. Let \(P:B\to D\) be a unital dg functor whose mapping-complex maps, on the selected object images, are degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphisms. For example use the actual canonical counit \(\epsilon_b:Q_b=\Omega B U_b\to U_b\), including its finite additive matrix envelope. Fix unital dg functors \(F,G:A\to B\). Write \(\operatorname{Nat}_\infty(F,G)\) for the full normalized natural-transformation complex, with all its source-bar Taylor components.

Theorem C.66.3.1 (actual projection kernel and relative coherent lifting). Postcomposition gives a degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphism \[ \begin{gathered} \operatorname{Nat}_\infty(F,G)\\ \longrightarrow\operatorname{Nat}_\infty(PF,PG). \end{gathered} \tag{C.66.7} \] Its kernel has a normalized contraction finite on each original source-bar input. This does not assert that either full natural-transformation complex is acyclic. The construction retains normalized units, identity-valued outputs of nonidentity input arrows, and full source-object faces.

Consequently a full coherent parameter diagram in the target functor category, with specified object functors \(PF_j\), lifts to the source functor category with those chosen \(F_j\) fixed. The assertion applies to the free parameter source \(\Omega B(kJ)\), retaining any already assigned compatible union of full parameter faces. It requires the entire typed target diagram as input, rather than only the classes of its edge maps.

Proof. A normalized Taylor component is an arbitrary homogeneous linear map from a reduced source-bar word to \(B(Fx_0,Gx_q)\). Applying \(P\) projects that entire output mapping space. Choose graded sections of its surjections over the split coefficient actions, separately for each endpoint pair. Semisimple splitting gives these choices. They lift every Taylor component. Thus (C.66.7) is degreewise surjective, including its component of source length zero. Postcomposition is a dg functor on the full natural-transformation categories: the complete differential and vertical products are the cofree Hom formulas of C.53.1, and the dg functor \(P\) preserves each output differential, composition and identity in those formulas. Scalar outputs are retained.

Let \(V_{x,y}\) be the kernel of \(B(Fx,Gy)\to D(PFx,PGy)\). It is acyclic, since this is a surjective quasi-isomorphism. The splitting proof of C.30.1 gives a normalized coefficient-linear contraction \(h_{x,y}\) on it. Choose these once for every endpoint pair. The kernel of (C.66.7) consists exactly of the normalized Taylor maps valued in these \(V_{x,y}\).

Its leading differential \(d_0\) contains the output kernel differential and the source unary differential on every original bar letter. Postcompose a Taylor value with its endpoint contraction to obtain \(H_0\). The Hom derivation rule cancels the two source-unary terms and gives \(d_0H_0+H_0d_0=1\), with \(H_0^2=0\). Put \(\delta=d-d_0\). Every remaining term either composes adjacent source letters, or consumes a nonempty source prefix or suffix in a functor action. Thus when evaluated on an original word of length \(L\), it uses the Taylor map on words of length strictly less than \(L\). The same statement permits normalized higher functor components, which consume larger nonempty pieces.

The maps \(H_0\) preserve that input length. Therefore the formula \[ \begin{gathered} H=H_0(1+\delta H_0)^{-1}\\ =\sum_{r\geq0}(-1)^rH_0(\delta H_0)^r \end{gathered} \tag{C.66.8} \] has only finitely many terms on each input, at most \(L+1\). C.35.1's contraction calculation, applied with zero retract, gives \(dH+Hd=1\) and \(H^2=0\). This contracts exactly the projection kernel. It proves the quasi-isomorphism in (C.66.7). The source bar is reduced, so every step retains normalization at identity arguments. Output identities were never projected away. Endpoint contractions and the source word operations add no new source object; full-face restrictions therefore retain these same formulas when their endpoint choices were made before restriction.

Finally consider a free parameter generator \(x\) of original string length \(q\). Its differential has only lower-length generators and their composites. Suppose their lifted images have already been assigned. Choose a graded lift \(v\) of its given entire target Taylor cochain and set \(o=\partial v-\widetilde F(dx)\). Its projection is zero by the target chain equation, and \(\partial o=0\) by the previously assigned generator equations and \(d^2x=0\). Its corrected image \(v-Ho\) has the same exact projection and satisfies the generator chain equation. This constructs the whole dg functor by induction on \(q\). Object units are their prescribed identity maps. Generators on already assigned faces are kept; only the remaining generators receive corrections. Their overlaps are the same original strings, so compatible prescribed unions stay fixed. This proves the relative lifting assertion. The proof contracts a specified projection kernel and uses no contraction of an arbitrary natural-transformation complex. \(\square\)

C.66.4. Solved calculations

Exercise C.66.4.1 (advanced; the essential second projection-kernel correction). Construct a full normalized natural-transformation projection whose kernel needs a nonzero second perturbation correction. Compute one such primitive, and show that the full natural-transformation complex need not be acyclic.

Solution.

For (C.66.7) use \(A=k[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)\), with \(|\varepsilon|=2\). Put \(V=kx\oplus K\), where \(|x|=0\) and \(K\) has the three acyclic pairs \[ \begin{gathered} a_0\xrightarrow{d}b_1,\\ c_1\xrightarrow{d}d_2,\\ e_2\xrightarrow{d}f_3. \end{gathered} \] The subscripts are degrees. Let \(B\) be the dg algebra of endomorphisms preserving \(K\), and let \(P:B\to k\) be its quotient action on \(V/K\). Its allowed matrix entries are one quotient entry, six entries from the quotient into \(K\), and 36 entries within \(K\). Thus \(\dim B=43\) and \(\dim\ker P=42\). Every kernel matrix has image in \(K\). Postcomposing with the homotopy sending \(b_1,d_2,f_3\) to \(a_0,c_1,e_2\), respectively, contracts that kernel, so \(P\) is a surjective quasi-isomorphism. The functors \(F,G\) send the ordinary identity to the identity of \(V\), with \(F(\varepsilon)=0\) and \(G(\varepsilon)(a_0)=d_2\), \(G(\varepsilon)(c_1)=f_3\), zero on the other basis vectors. This is a closed degree-two square-zero endomorphism.

For a natural cochain of total degree \(r\), write \(\phi_q\) for its value on \((s\varepsilon)^{\otimes q}\). Its value-map degree is \(r+q\). The kernel differential is \[ \begin{gathered} (\partial\phi)_q =\partial_{\operatorname{End}(V)}\phi_q\\ \qquad+(-1)^rG(\varepsilon)\phi_{q-1},\\ \phi_{-1}=0. \end{gathered} \] The bare kernel cycle \(v:x\mapsto b_1\), zero elsewhere, has degree one. Formula (C.66.8) gives the degree-zero primitive with values \(x\mapsto a_0\) at \(q=0\), \(x\mapsto-c_1\) at \(q=1\), and \(x\mapsto e_2\) at \(q=2\). The second correction is essential: omitting it leaves an uncancelled \(-f_3\) at source length two. Indeed its differential has the values \(b_1\), \(-d_2+G(\varepsilon)a_0=0\), and \(f_3-G(\varepsilon)c_1=0\) at lengths zero, one and two. Every higher value is zero since \(G(\varepsilon)e_2=0\).

The target functors \(PF,PG\) both kill \(\varepsilon\). Their full natural-transformation complex has one closed scalar coefficient at each Taylor length \(q\), in total degree \(-q\), and zero differential. The projection maps onto it. Its scalar coefficients have chain lifts by the matrices supported solely on the quotient \(kx\). They are closed because \(G(\varepsilon)x=0\). They cannot be boundaries since their projected values are nonzero. Thus at Taylor-prefix length \(L\) there are \(L+1\) independent quotient cohomology classes. The kernel is contractible, while those classes remain in the full complex.

Exercise C.66.4.2 (intermediate; retained intermediate cores and a Koszul sign). Let \(C=k\oplus ku\), with \(|u|=1\), zero differential and primitive coproduct on \(u\). Use pure cores \(C^{\otimes m_s}\) along the arity path \(0\to2\to1\to0\). For every ordinary kernel use central complex \(N=ke\oplus ka\oplus kb\), with \(|e|=|b|=0\), \(|a|=-1\), \(da=b\), and \(Hb=a\). Compute the three-kernel path dimension and its retract dimension. Evaluate its homotopy on the word \((1,e,u,b,u\otimes u,e,1)\).

Solution. In target-to-source order the cofree path is \[ \begin{gathered} C^{\otimes0}\otimes N_3\otimes C\\ \qquad\otimes N_2\otimes C^{\otimes2} \otimes N_1\otimes C^{\otimes0}. \end{gathered} \] Its dimension is \(1\cdot3\cdot2\cdot3\cdot4\cdot3\cdot1=216\). The retract replaces each \(N_i\) by \(ke\); both middle cores remain, so its dimension is \(2\cdot4=8\). The graded coalgebra \(C^{\otimes2}\) has \[ \begin{gathered} \Delta(u\otimes u) =(u\otimes u)\otimes1\\ \quad+1\otimes(u\otimes u)\\ \quad+(u\otimes1)\otimes(1\otimes u)\\ \quad-(1\otimes u)\otimes(u\otimes1), \end{gathered} \] where the last sign comes from interchanging two odd primitives.

Only the homotopy at \(N_2\) acts on the specified word. The preceding \(u\) has odd degree, so its tensor evaluation sign is minus: \[ \begin{gathered} H(1,e,u,b,u\otimes u,e,1)\\ \qquad=-(1,e,u,a,u\otimes u,e,1). \end{gathered} \] Applying the differential gives the original word: its sign at \(da=b\) is also minus. The word has zero differential and its projection is zero, which verifies \(dH+Hd=1-IP\) on this input. The bare three-cross sector has degree minus three after restoring its three suspensions; the independent three-root product has its one final suspension and bare degree minus one.

Lemma C.66.1.1 retains the outer state types. Theorem C.66.2.1 gives the full cotensor contraction, and Theorem C.66.3.1 lifts coherent operator cells through the specific Nat-projection kernel. Exercises C.66.4.1–C.66.4.2 compute its essential second correction and retained middle-core sign. Editable SVG source.

C.67. Coherent operator strictification

Canonical cobar sources admit strict operator models with an actual invertible full natural comparison. Their identity bare components give a finite inverse on each original source input. Conjugating an entire operator diagram therefore retains every higher cell and fixes operators already strict. Full marked postcomposition also retains the higher components of a change of enhanced model.

C.67.1. The counit and the full A-infinity projection kernel

All bars and cobars in this section are the actual augmented reduced ones, over the split coefficient category. Let \(A\) be an augmented unital dg category; its mapping degrees need not be nonnegative. Its canonical counit is \[ \epsilon_A:\Omega BA\longrightarrow A. \tag{C.67.1} \]

Theorem C.67.1.1 (finite-on-original-words counit and full projection). The counit is degreewise surjective and a quasi-isomorphism on mapping complexes. It has a normalized linear mapping-complex contraction finite on each original \(A\)-word. The contraction commutes with retained source faces and augmented coefficient-preserving dg input maps.

Theorem C.66.3.1 also holds when its fixed functors \(F,G\) are normalized uncurved unital \(A_\infty\) functors. Its full Nat-projection remains graded-surjective, with a contractible kernel and the same finite-on-input correction. Only the specified mapping projection kernels are contracted.

Proof. Write a cobar word as nonempty bar blocks of original reduced \(A\)-morphisms. Let \(r\) be its total number of original morphisms. The counit sends a word all of whose blocks have one letter to its ordered product in \(A\); it kills a word containing a longer block. In particular its one-letter generators map onto every reduced mapping, and its coefficient map retains the units. This proves graded surjectivity.

First keep the original unary differential and the cobar differential inserting block cuts, and omit the internal binary bar compositions. On a fixed original word with \(r\geq2\), remove its first boundary if its first block consists of one original letter and that boundary is present; otherwise give zero. The coefficient is \((-1)^{|a|}\), where \(a\) is that first original letter in target-to-source order. This is the inverse coefficient of its first-cut term in C.39.15. Call this operator \(H_0\). At \(r=0,1\) it is zero.

In the leading cut differential, adding and removing that first boundary give the identity. Adding another boundary before or after removing the first gives opposite coefficients by the degree-one Leibniz sign, so all those terms cancel. The unary differential on the first letter changes \(|a|\) by one, giving the opposite removal coefficient. The unary terms on the other letters cancel by the same tensor sign. This gives the normalized leading contraction onto the coefficient and single-letter complex. Its inclusion \(I_0\) places a reduced \(A\)-mapping in one single-letter block.

Restoring binary bar composition is a perturbation \(\delta\) strictly decreasing \(r\). The first-cut homotopy preserves \(r\), so \[ H_\epsilon=H_0(1+\delta H_0)^{-1} \tag{C.67.2} \] is finite on every original word. The perturbed inclusion stays \(I_0\), since \(\delta I_0=0\). The image of every nonzero term of \(H_\epsilon\) contains a block of length at least two, so \(\epsilon_AH_\epsilon=0\); also \(\epsilon_AI_0=1\). Applying the counit to the perturbed contraction identity shows that its projection is exactly \(\epsilon_A\). Thus \[ \begin{gathered} dH_\epsilon+H_\epsilon d\\ \qquad=1-I_0\epsilon_A,\\ H_\epsilon^2=H_\epsilon I_0=0,\\ \epsilon_AH_\epsilon=0. \end{gathered} \tag{C.67.3} \] This proves the mapping-complex assertion without a convergence claim based on cohomological degree. Every formula uses the same original letters and their compositions. It therefore commutes with the indicated restrictions and input maps. The inclusion \(I_0\) is a linear chain section; its multiplicativity is not part of this claim.

For the second assertion use the full Taylor description in C.66.3. An \(A_\infty\) functor's additional terms consume a nonempty input word. Uncurvedness excludes a zero-input functor term. Consequently every additional term in the full Nat differential again evaluates its Taylor map on a strictly shorter original source input. The degreewise lifts and the leading kernel contraction are unchanged. The finite formula (C.66.8) therefore contracts this same full projection kernel. All higher functor outputs, including scalar identities, remain in that differential. This also proves the relative coherent lifting statement for these functor objects. \(\square\)

C.67.2. Strict operator objects with an actual full natural isomorphism

Let \(L\) be a conilpotent coaugmented relative dg coalgebra and put \(A=\Omega L\). Its actual unit gives the dg section \[ \begin{gathered} \sigma_A=\Omega\eta_L,\\ \sigma_A:A\longrightarrow\Omega BA,\\ \epsilon_A\sigma_A=1_A. \end{gathered} \tag{C.67.4} \] Write \(\iota_A:A\to\Omega BA\) for the normalized \(A_\infty\) unit, with bar map \(\eta_{BA}\). For an uncurved normalized unital \(A_\infty\) functor \(F:A\to B\), with \(B\) a unital dg category, let \(F^\sharp:\Omega BA\to B\) be its strict representative retaining its complete outputs, as in C.43.2. Define \[ F^{\mathrm{st}}=F^\sharp\sigma_A. \tag{C.67.5} \]

Theorem C.67.2.1 (full coherent strictification and an actual dg retraction). There is a closed invertible full natural transformation \(\alpha_F:F\to F^{\mathrm{st}}\), with identity bare components. Its inverse is finite on each original source-bar input. If \(F\) is already a strict dg functor, then \(F^{\mathrm{st}}=F\) and \(\alpha_F=1_F\) exactly.

The assignment on objects, together with \[ \theta\longmapsto \alpha_G\,\theta\,\alpha_F^{-1}, \tag{C.67.6} \] is a dg retraction of \(\operatorname{Fun}_\infty(A,B)\) onto its full dg subcategory of strict dg functor objects. The full Nat complexes and every higher parameter cell are retained. Hence it conjugates an entire coherent parameter diagram, rather than replacing just its edge maps. It fixes an already strict-object subdiagram literally.

Proof. The unit and counit are the actual coproduct formulas. On a free generator \(t\ell\) of \(\Omega L\), the one-bar-letter term of \(\eta_L(\ell)\) is \(s(t\ell)\). All other terms have longer bar length and are killed by the counit. This proves the second identity in (C.67.4) on generators and therefore on all cobar words. The other triangle identity gives \(\epsilon_A\iota_A=1_A\) as a full normalized functor: after applying the counit to the unit expansion of an original bar word, the term cut into its individual original letters is exactly that word, and all other terms are killed.

The functors \(\iota_A,\sigma_A:A\to\Omega BA\) have the same object map and their postcompositions with \(\epsilon_A\) are both exactly \(1_A\). Apply Theorem C.67.1.1's full Nat-projection kernel to these two functors. Choose the graded preimage \(u^0\) of the identity target transformation which has identity bare components and zero higher components. Its defect \(\partial u^0\) is in that projection kernel, is closed, and has zero source-length-zero component. With its contraction \(H\), put \[ u=u^0-H(\partial u^0). \tag{C.67.7} \] It is closed and has exact image the identity. The correction still has zero bare component: its leading homotopy preserves input length, and its perturbation uses shorter input words. Thus \(u\) has identity bare components.

View a full natural transformation as its actual cofree source-bar map. After identifying the two underlying graded fibers by their identity bare maps, \(u-1\) consumes positive source length. Its geometric inverse is therefore finite on every original input. The full cut composition proves both inverse identities. The differential derivation rule and \(\partial u=0\) make the inverse closed. Thus this is an actual invertible transformation, not just equality of its cohomology class.

Postcomposition by the strict dg functor \(F^\sharp\) is a dg functor on the full Nat categories, by the output-composition argument of C.66.3. It sends \(u\) to \(\alpha_F\). The recovery identity \(F^\sharp\iota_A=F\) is C.43.2's exact free-generator identity, including its scalar outputs. Its other end is (C.67.5). For strict \(F\), one has \(F^\sharp=F\epsilon_A\) on every free generator. Hence \(F^{\mathrm{st}}=F\) and \(\alpha_F=F(\epsilon_Au)=1_F\) exactly.

Closed degree-zero conjugation preserves differentials, products and identities on full Nat complexes. It gives the stated dg retraction, and fixes all morphisms between already strict objects. Applying that dg functor to every generator of a given \(\Omega B(kJ)\)-diagram retains its whole chain equation and every higher parameter generator. On an assigned face with strict objects all the conjugating transformations are identities.

For restrictions along retained coalgebra faces and their canonical cobar maps, \(\sigma_A\) is natural by its unit formula. The counit contraction in Theorem C.67.1.1 preserves the original labels and letters. Choosing that contraction in (C.67.7) makes the universal transformation and its finite inverse restrict to the same formulas. Thus the construction retains the original compatible faces as well. \(\square\)

C.67.3. Model change retains the entire functor-category diagram

Let \(W:B\to D\) be a normalized uncurved unital \(A_\infty\) functor between dg categories. The input and output here need not be augmented. For the finite insertion calculation use the tensor bar on all mapping spaces, retaining identity outputs as actual mapping letters. Normalized functors and normalized pre-natural transformations form the usual unital subspaces of that calculation.

Theorem C.67.3.1 (full postcomposition and double strict models). There is a normalized unital \(A_\infty\) functor \[ \begin{gathered} W_*:\operatorname{Fun}_\infty(A,B)\\ \longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}_\infty(A,D) \end{gathered} \tag{C.67.8} \] whose object map is actual composition with \(W\). Its higher components retain every higher component of \(W\). They are finite on each original input word. When \(W\) is strict dg, (C.67.8) is exactly the dg functor of postcomposition on every full Taylor component.

Suppose both the operator source \(A\) and parameter source \(T\) are augmented cobars. Any whole normalized coherent model-change diagram \(S:T\to\operatorname{Fun}_\infty(A,B)\), including a normalized \(A_\infty\) one, therefore has a strict dg parameter model in \(\operatorname{Fun}_\infty(A,D)\) with strict dg operator objects. It carries actual full natural isomorphisms to the model-change diagram. An already strict parameter face with strict operator objects is fixed whenever its postcomposed face has those properties.

Proof. Work in suspended coordinates. A pre-natural transformation \(\phi:F_0\to F_1\) of degree \(|\phi|\) has suspended core degree \(|\phi|-1\), including its zero-input object component. Its cofree expansion has the original \(F_0\)-outputs before that component and the original \(F_1\)-outputs after it. For a sequence \(\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_r\), expand an original source word into consecutive pieces with these \(r\) marked transformation components in their prescribed order. Fill every intervening unmarked run with the appropriate original functor. Empty transformation inputs are allowed; an empty unmarked run contributes its coefficient coaugmentation.

Apply the actual bar map of \(W\) to that ordered output word and take its single-letter corestriction. This defines the \(r\)-th suspended component of (C.67.8). All signs are the tensor evaluation signs of the marked maps: a marked map of suspended degree \(|\phi_i|-1\) crossing a preceding source piece of degree \(d\) contributes \((-1)^{(|\phi_i|-1)d}\). No input or output identity is discarded. If the source word has length \(L\), its unmarked functor outputs contribute at most \(L\) letters, by uncurvedness, and the marked slots contribute \(r\). Thus only \(W_m\) with \(m\leq L+r\) occurs. Every consecutive partition and every such marked expansion is finite. Unsuspending gives the required component degree \(1-r\).

We verify the full equation by retaining the marked slots in the bar equation \(BW\,b_B=b_D\,BW\). A term of \(b_B\) wholly inside an unmarked functor run is its original functor equation, with the source differential on those same inputs. A term meeting one marked component is exactly the full differential of that natural transformation. A term joining two adjacent marked components gives their vertical source composition. On the other side, cutting the marked sequence into consecutive nonempty groups gives the vertical products of the corresponding components of (C.67.8). These are all terms: the dg categories have only unary differentials and binary mapping compositions. Their signs are those of the same suspended tensor maps, in the same order, in the displayed bar equation. Thus each term has its identical signed counterpart. This is the complete functor equation.

Ordinary unit arguments normalize as follows. In a nontrivial higher component an identity transformation supplies an identity mapping to a higher component of \(W\), which vanishes by strict unitality. For its unary component \(W_1\) takes that identity to the identity. The same unit cancellation in the original functor and transformation differentials preserves the normalized source cochains. When \(W_m=0\) for \(m>1\), more than one marked slot contributes zero, and the single marked slot is precisely \(W_1\) on that full Taylor output. This proves the strict dg special case. The unreduced tensor bar in this insertion calculation is not used as an augmented bar-cobar counit; that counit is the reduced augmented construction of Theorem C.67.1.1.

Apply (C.67.8) to the whole supplied parameter diagram. Then apply Theorem C.67.2.1's dg retraction for the operator source \(A\). Its objects are now strict dg operator models, with every parameter and full Nat component retained. Finally apply Theorem C.67.2.1 to this parameter functor, whose source is the cobar \(T\) and whose target is the dg full Nat category. This makes the parameter functor strict without changing its object map, so the operator objects stay strict. Both steps come with their actual full natural isomorphisms from Theorem C.67.2.1. Its retraction fixes a strict-object subcategory pointwise, and fixes an already strict parameter functor exactly. This proves the relative assertion and the whole model-change statement. \(\square\)

C.67.4. Solved calculations

Exercise C.67.4.1 (advanced; the extra unit term and an actual comparison). Compute the strict section for the nonminimal source \(\Omega B(k[2])\), including its degree-minus-one generator. Give its full comparison with the \(A_\infty\) unit, and exhibit a scalar-output operator whose strict model needs that extra term.

Solution.

Take \(A=\Omega B(k[2])\), with objects \(0,1,2\), degree-zero arrows \(a:0\to1\), \(b:1\to2\), \(c:0\to2\), the product \(D=ba\), and a degree-minus-one generator \(H\) with \(dH=D-c\). Its mapping basis has eight elements including identities. In \(\widehat A=\Omega BA\), the mapping basis has ten elements: the three identities, \(a',b',c',D',H',V\), and \(P=b'a'\). The nonzero differentials are \[ dH'=D'-c',\qquad dV=P-D'. \] The counit sends \(V\) to zero, \(P,D'\) to \(D\), and \(H'\) to \(H\). Its linear section sends \(H\) to \(H'\) and \(D\) to \(D'\). Its strict section instead satisfies \[ \sigma_A(H)=H'+V,\qquad\sigma_A(D)=P. \] The extra unit term is essential: \(d(H'+V)=P-c'\), which is the strict section's value on \(D-c\). The linear section's value \(H'\) instead has differential \(D'-c'\).

For the universal comparison, use the two functors \(\iota_A,\sigma_A\) and the full Nat-projection of the counit. Let \(u^0\) have identity bare components and zero higher components, and let \(\phi\) have the single higher value \(\phi(D)=V\). Its full differential has the values \[ \begin{gathered} (\partial\phi)(D)=P-D',\\ (\partial\phi)(H)=V,\\ (\partial\phi)(a,b)=-V. \end{gathered} \] These are exactly \(\partial u^0\). Thus \(u=u^0-\phi\) is closed and has higher value \(-V\) on \(D\). Its exact inverse is \(u^0+\phi\): two positive-length pieces supported only on the arrow \(D:0\to2\) cannot compose. Projection kills its higher values and gives the identity. This calculation retains both the source unary differential of \(H\) and the two-arrow word \((a,b)\).

For a scalar-output operator example take \(X=ke\oplus kf\oplus ky\), with \(|e|=|y|=0\), \(|f|=-1\), \(df=y\). Let \(K(e)=f\), \(L=\partial K\). Send \(a',b'\) to \(1_X\), \(c',D'\) to \(1_X-L\), \(H'\) to zero and \(V\) to \(K\). This is the strictification of a normalized non-strict \(A_\infty\) operator on \(A\). Its strict model sends \(H\) to \(K\), since \(\partial K=L=1_X-(1_X-L)\). The full comparison has value \(-K\) on the original source morphism \(D\), or on its generator \(D'\) in the resolved comparison path. Omitting \(V\) would assign zero to \(H\) while its required strict differential is the nonzero \(L\). Both nonidentity arrows \(a,b\) retain their actual identity outputs.

Exercise C.67.4.2 (advanced; the marked postcomposition sign). Let the operator source be \(k[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)\), with \(|\varepsilon|=2\). Let \(F_j\) select object \(j\) of \([2]\) and kill \(\varepsilon\). Write \(a_q,b_p,c_r\) for full natural cochains supported at the indicated Taylor lengths, with values the arrows \(a,b,c=ba\). For the model change \(W\) with \(W_1(a)=W_1(b)=1_X\), \(W_1(c)=1_X-L\), and \(W_2(b,a)=K\), compute \((W_*)_2(b_p,a_q)\).

Solution. The cochain degrees are \(-q,-p,-r\), respectively, since \(s\varepsilon\) has degree one. The full vertical product is \[ b_pa_q=(-1)^{pq}c_{p+q}. \] In the marked formula the suspended \(a_q\)-component has degree \(-q-1\). It crosses a preceding source piece of degree \(p\), so \[ (W_*)_2(b_p,a_q)=(-1)^{(q+1)p}K \] at Taylor length \(p+q\). The two terms of its source/cut equation give \[ \begin{gathered} (-1)^{p+1+pq}(1_X-L)\\ \qquad+(-1)^{p+pq}1_X\\ =(-1)^{p+pq}L. \end{gathered} \] This is precisely the differential of the displayed marked component. At \(p=1,q=0\) that component is \(-K\). Using \(+K\) would give a nonzero discrepancy \(2L\) over the characteristic-zero field. For a coefficient operator source there are no source letters and the marked formula gives \((W_*)_r=W_r\) itself. Thus C.65.3.1's actual length-three, five and seven examples retain their nonzero higher model-change components.

Theorem C.67.1.1 gives the actual augmented counit and full projection kernel. Theorem C.67.2.1 gives a full natural isomorphism and dg retraction to strict operator objects. Theorem C.67.3.1 retains the marked postcomposition data. Exercises C.67.4.1–C.67.4.2 compute the necessary unit term and marked sign. Editable SVG source.

C.68. Native operator models through dg bridges

Full natural transformations can be lifted through a specified mapping projection even when their source has no augmentation. An actual dg bridge retains the geometric object representatives, their positive models and their entire comparison. On fixed overall input and output types, this gives relative models of the complete native partition diagrams.

C.68.1. Full normalized lifting without a source augmentation

Use the full normalized natural-transformation cochains of uncurved unital \(A_\infty\) functors. They vanish on ordinary unit arguments in positive source length. Their differential can be computed on the tensor bar of all source mapping spaces; no augmented bar-cobar counit is applied to that possibly unaugmented source. All coefficient actions are over the split semisimple identity category.

Theorem C.68.1.1 (actual projection fibers, sections and equivalences). Let \(P:B\to D\) be a relative unital dg functor with surjective quasi-isomorphisms on its selected mapping complexes. The full Nat projection of C.66.3 and C.67.1 remains a surjective quasi-isomorphism for normalized unital functors from an unaugmented dg source. Its kernel contraction is finite on every original input.

If the object labels and their coefficient maps have sections, \(P\) has a normalized unital \(A_\infty\) section on those labels. Its postcomposition with \(P\) is exactly the identity functor, including all higher components. Finally a closed full natural transformation whose bare object maps are homotopy equivalences is invertible in the full Nat cohomology category, with actual full inverse cochains and homotopies.

Proof. First split the mapping projection kernels over the coefficient actions, as in C30. The leading differential of a Taylor cochain includes the output unary differential and all original source unary differentials. Applying the kernel contraction to its output gives the leading Hom contraction. All remaining terms consume at least one source letter: they compose adjacent source inputs or apply a nonempty functor action. These statements use the full tensor bar, including products with unit outputs.

The normalized cochains are stable under that differential. When an input is a unit, its neighboring source-composition terms cancel the corresponding functor unit actions; higher unital functor components at that input vanish. The leading contraction preserves normalization since it changes only the output. Thus both the leading differential and its remaining perturbation preserve this normalized subspace. The finite series \[ H=H_0(1+\delta H_0)^{-1} \tag{C.68.1} \] contracts exactly the projection kernel on each input length. Graded Taylor sections lift normalized cochains by assigning zero at their unit inputs. This proves the first assertion. No augmentation of the source was used.

For a section, choose a graded mapping section preserving the coefficient maps. Correct its chain defect by the output kernel contraction; the defect is zero on the coefficients, so this gives a coefficient-preserving chain section \(j_1\). At source word length \(q\geq2\), the known lower-length components give the full Stasheff obstruction \(O_q\). It takes values in the mapping kernel, because after projection the chosen components are exactly the strict identity. Keep the entire unary complex of the length-\(q\) source generators. The obstruction is closed in that Hom complex: its differential is the length-\(q\) component of the source square-zero equation and of the already assigned lower equations. Postcomposition with the kernel contraction contracts this Hom complex. Set \(j_q=H_0O_q\), with the sign fixed by the equation \(\partial j_q=O_q\). This gives the next component with zero projection. If one input is a unit, the two adjacent source-unit terms and the corresponding target-unit term cancel; hence \(O_q\) is normalized and so is \(j_q\). Induction constructs the full unital section. This is induction on original input length, retaining the nonminimal unary complex, rather than induction assuming its basis generators are cycles.

For the last assertion, fix a closed natural transformation \(u:F\to G\) whose object maps are homotopy equivalences. Composition by a bare object map is a quasi-isomorphism on every appropriate mapping complex: its inverse and Hom homotopies are given by composition with its actual homotopy inverse and its two homotopies, with the Hom derivation signs. The cone of this leading map is therefore acyclic. Split and contract that cone over the coefficient actions. In the cone of composition by the full \(u\), all further terms consume positive source length. The same finite perturbation contracts that cone on each original input. Thus composition by \(u\) is a quasi-isomorphism on the full Nat complexes.

In particular choose a closed \(v:G\to F\) whose class maps to \([1_G]\) under postcomposition by \(u\). Then \(uv\) is homotopic to \(1_G\) in the full complex. Faithfulness of that same composition on \(H^0\) gives \(vu\simeq1_F\). Both differences are actual boundaries in full Nat complexes, giving the asserted inverse and homotopies. The contractions concerned a specified projection kernel or a cone of composition by an actual equivalence; arbitrary Nat complexes have not been declared acyclic. \(\square\)

C.68.2. Relative replacement of a complete coherent diagram

Let \(\mathcal E\) be a dg category and choose closed homotopy equivalences \(u_i:X_i\to Y_i\). Use the path category with maps \((f,g,a)\), whose differential and composition are those of C.53.4, and whose object at \(i\) is this actual \(u_i\).

Lemma C.68.2.1 (relative full-diagram replacement). Both path projections have graded-surjective quasi-isomorphisms on their full mapping complexes. Given a whole \(\Omega B(kJ)\)-diagram on the \(X_i\)'s and an already assigned compatible full-face path to a diagram on the corresponding \(Y_i\)'s, the path extends to the whole parameter diagram with those object maps fixed. Its second projection retains every assigned face exactly. The assertion also holds for a countable locally forward finite parameter category, using the same original-word induction.

Proof. The first projection's mapping kernel has components \((g,a)\) and differential \[ (g,a)\longmapsto(\partial g,-\partial a-gu_i). \] It is a shifted cone of precomposition by \(u_i\). This is an actual mapping-complex quasi-isomorphism, since \(u_i\) has a homotopy inverse. Its cone is acyclic. The second projection has the cone of postcomposition by \(u_j\), with the same conclusion. Each projection is graded surjective because its retained component can be chosen arbitrarily. Split and contract each such kernel over the coefficient category. These are contractions of the specified path-projection kernels.

Keep the assigned path generators. For each remaining original parameter generator choose a graded lift of its specified first component. Its chain defect is a closed element of the projection kernel, because its differential uses only previously treated shorter strings. Subtract its kernel primitive. The resulting generator image has the same exact projection and satisfies its chain equation. Extend by the free cobar composition. This is the relative induction of C.66.3, now with the displayed actual path kernels. Every original generator lies at finite string length. A common face is the same original word on both sides, so prescribing compatible unions retains all of them. This proves both assertions, including the full path comparison. \(\square\)

C.68.3. A bridge with the actual geometric object representatives

Let \(v:U\to G\) be a unital dg quasi-equivalence. In the application \(U\) is the positive IC model or its finite additive matrix envelope; \(G\) is the chosen geometric dg model, including the actual forward perverse images. It need not be augmented. For every needed \(y\in G\) choose \(x\in U\) and a closed homotopy equivalence \(u:vx\to y\). Include the canonical choices \((x,vx,1_{vx})\).

Theorem C.68.3.1 (the full dg model bridge). There is a dg category \(R(v)\) whose objects are those triples \((x,y,u)\). A degree-\(r\) mapping has components \[ \begin{gathered} f\in U^r(x,x'),\quad g\in G^r(y,y'),\\ a\in G^{r-1}(vx,y'). \end{gathered} \] Its differential and composition are \[ \begin{gathered} D(f,g,a)\\ \quad=(\partial f,\partial g,\\ \qquad-\partial a+u'v(f)-gu),\\ (f_2,g_2,a_2)(f_1,g_1,a_1)\\ \quad=(f_2f_1,g_2g_1,\\ \qquad a_2v(f_1)\\ \qquad+(-1)^{|f_2|}g_2a_1). \end{gathered} \tag{C.68.2} \] The two projections \(p:R(v)\to U\), \(q:R(v)\to G\) are graded-surjective quasi-isomorphisms on every selected mapping complex. The canonical-object inclusion \(j:U\to R(v)\) is a strict dg functor with \(pj=1_U\) and \(qj=v\). The bridge has its actual resolved comparison from \(vp\) to \(q\), with object components \(u\), and that comparison restricts to the identity on \(j(U)\).

The bridge is used as a dg target. No augmentation of this expanded object category is assumed or used.

Proof. Formula (C.68.2) is the path construction after applying \(v\) to the first component. The square-zero differential uses closedness of \(u,u'\), and the third product component has its Hom Leibniz sign \((-1)^{|f_2|}\). In a triple product its third component expands to \(a_3v(f_2f_1)+(-1)^{|f_3|}g_3a_2v(f_1) +(-1)^{|f_3|+|f_2|}g_3g_2a_1\) in both groupings. Together with the ordinary dg identities on \(U,G\), these calculations prove all dg category identities. Its identity maps are \((1_x,1_y,0)\).

Both projections are plainly graded surjective. The kernel of \(p\) is the cone of precomposition \(G(y,y')\to G(vx,y')\) by \(u\). This is a quasi-isomorphism because \(u\) is a homotopy equivalence. The kernel of \(q\) is the cone of \[ U(x,x')\longrightarrow G(vx,y'),\qquad f\longmapsto u'v(f). \] That map is a quasi-isomorphism by the quasi-equivalence on Hom complexes and the homotopy equivalence \(u'\). Both kernels are acyclic, proving the mapping assertions. The canonical inclusion sends \(f\) to \((f,v(f),0)\) between the canonical objects. Formula (C.68.2) proves its dg and retraction identities exactly.

There is a strict dg functor from this bridge to the path category of \(G\), sending its object to \(u:vx\to y\) and its map to \((v(f),g,a)\). This is the actual resolved comparison. Its object maps are homotopy equivalences, and Theorem C.68.1.1 gives full inverse transformations when they are needed. On the canonical inclusion its objects are identity maps and every third component is zero. Thus its comparison there is exactly the identity. Keeping all three components also retains a geometric object which is merely homotopy equivalent to its positive-model representative; it is not identified with that representative as a dg object. \(\square\)

C.68.4. Native partition operators at fixed overall arities

Use \(U_n=(\Omega C)^{\otimes n}\) and the common cobar state \(V_n=\Omega(C^{\otimes n})\), with the actual surjective quasi-isomorphism \(\rho_n:V_n\to U_n\) of C41/C52. At zero arity all three pure input models are the coefficient category. The fixed positive generator model has an actual strict dg quasi-equivalence into the geometric IC model. Explicitly, write \(C=B\mathcal M\) for the minimal IC model in C34, and let \(I:\mathcal M\to G\) be its full enhanced inclusion from the normalized transfer of C33. On a free cobar generator \(t c\), define \(v(t c)\) to be the corresponding Taylor value of \(I\). The full functor equation for \(I\) is the twisting equation, so extending multiplicatively defines a strict dg \(v:\Omega C\to G\). Its composite with C34's unit \(\mathcal M\to\Omega C\) is exactly \(I\), by the same consecutive-partition reconstruction. Both that unit and \(I\) are mapping-complex quasi-isomorphisms, so \(v\) is one as well. Tensor powers retain those quasi-isomorphisms by the split tensor contractions of C30.1. Finite additive images use C38's full matrix balancing. Write \(v_n:U_n\to G_n\) for this ordered tensor input model and its finite additive extension.

For one original joint string, let \(J\) be its consecutive-block partition category, directed by merging blocks. Retain each actual composite contraction label. Its native objects are operators with fixed overall input arity \(a\) and output arity \(b\); intermediate frontier arities can vary. More generally the same assertion applies to any directed native parameter diagram of this same overall type, on the complete C64 domain. Use the full enhanced native diagram of C47: its functors and every higher transformation are evaluated on all their original source mapping inputs. In dg models these are exactly its normalized full functor-category cochains.

Theorem C.68.4.1 (relative native operator models at fixed outer type). The whole native diagram has a strict dg parameter model whose objects are strict dg operators \(V_a\to V_b\), with its actual full native comparison. Suppose an already assigned compatible union of full parameter faces is given in these positive models, together with its actual full native face comparison. The construction retains those faces exactly.

For collapsed original-string faces, choose the model data once on each actual ordered block sequence. The resulting fixed-outer-type diagrams then agree on their shared faces. This retains complete partition diagrams; strict external-root product and source-end-changing graft covariance still require their full common marked presentation.

Proof. On the primitive IC tuple inputs, precompose the actual native operators with the strict dg input model \(v_a\rho_a\). This gives their full normalized diagram in \(\operatorname{Fun}_\infty(V_a,G_b)\). Here the higher cochains are the supplied enhanced native cells of C47, not edge classes selected afterwards. Theorem C.67.2.1 makes the operator objects strict and retains the whole parameter diagram. If the parameter model itself is initially \(A_\infty\), apply C.67.3's second strictification as well. On a face already strict in both senses, these retractions fix all its data.

An actual face comparison can first be used to put the whole geometric diagram under that exact boundary convention: apply Lemma C.68.2.1 in the full functor category, with the given face path. Outside that face use identity object equivalences. This changes the whole diagram through its actual path and makes the prescribed face exact. Thus the following construction may assume that the geometric face is \(v_b\) of its given positive-model face.

Form the bridge \(R(v_b)\), including the geometric operator image objects. Such objects are perverse finite IC sums by C47; their needed homotopy equivalences to finite additive \(v_b\)-images are their actual IC decomposition isomorphisms in the enhanced category. Choose these object resolutions once. For a strict geometric operator \(V_a\to G_b\), choose those bridge objects over its primitive source objects. Lift its free cobar generators through \(q:R(v_b)\to G_b\). The mapping kernel is acyclic by Theorem C.68.3.1. The full unary complex of each source generator stage is retained, exactly as in C.46.2; its Hom kernel is contracted by the output kernel homotopy. Correcting the closed defect therefore gives a strict operator lift. No target augmentation is needed. Extend from primitive tuple inputs to their finite additive envelopes by the actual matrix functor.

On an assigned positive face, use instead the canonical lift \(j\) of its whole positive diagram. It has the exact prescribed geometric image. Theorem C.68.1.1's full Nat projection for \(q\), followed by C.66.3's relative free-parameter induction, now lifts the entire strict geometric parameter diagram with these operator objects fixed. The prescribed whole face lifts are retained. Projection by \(p\) gives strict operators into \(U_b\) and the whole dg parameter diagram there, with the assigned faces exact.

The bridge's resolved comparison retains the full native interpretation. For complete cochains this can be written by the marked construction of C.67.3 with the closed bridge comparison in its distinguished slot. Its bar equation is the corresponding commutator identity: unmarked terms are functor equations, marked terms are its full transformation differential, and cuts give its naturality equation. Every term uses the same suspended maps and signs, and on a source word of length \(L\) with \(r\) parameter marks there are at most \(L+r+1\) output letters. Thus this gives the actual entire comparison. Its object maps are homotopy equivalences; Theorem C.68.1.1 supplies full inverses and homotopies, first in the operator category and then in the parameter category. On the assigned canonical face the comparison is the identity, because the bridge's third components there are zero.

Finally lift each strict operator into \(U_b\) through the actual \(\rho_b:V_b\to U_b\). The source is a cobar and the target mapping projection is surjective with acyclic kernel, so the same full generator complex argument gives strict operators \(V_a\to V_b\). On assigned faces keep their existing lifts. The full Nat projection of C66 lifts the whole parameter diagram with those operator objects fixed, and retains all its prescribed faces exactly. This proves the positive-state assertion, including arities zero and the original unit-output functors.

All constructions use the actual block composite and the original source and target labels. If an internal original-string cut is collapsed, its partition category is the full face with that cut absent. Its block objects and composites are literally those same ordered blocks. Choose bridge resolutions, graded sections and kernel contractions once on these data. C67's canonical units and corrections restrict to the same faces. At each free parameter stage the lift is a graded section minus its closed kernel defect primitive, so the same original generator receives the same correction on every shared face. Induction over those original generators gives the claimed common family. The locally forward finite C64 bounds place each calculation in a finite corner; they do not replace its whole compatible domain by a clipped shuffle domain. \(\square\)

C.68.5. Solved calculations

Write \(E_{a,b}\) for the matrix sending \(b\) to \(a\), with all other basis vectors sent to zero. Products are in target-to-source order.

Exercise C.68.5.1 (a forced higher component for an unaugmented source; advanced). Let \[ \begin{gathered} V=ke\oplus kf\oplus ky,\\ |e|=|y|=0,\\ |f|=-1,\quad df=y,\\ G=\operatorname{End}(V),\\ v(\lambda)=\lambda1_V. \end{gathered} \tag{C.68.3} \] Construct the one-object bridge of Theorem C.68.3.1 and a normalized unital \(A_\infty\) section of its geometric projection. Prove that no graded unital algebra augmentation \(G\to k\) exists. Compute a nonzero second component of the composite section \(w:G\to k\), retaining the source unary differential.

Solution. Put \(h=E_{f,y}\), \(E=E_{e,e}\), and \(\beta(g)=g_{ee}\). Thus \(dh+hd=1-E\), \(h^2=Eh=hE=0\), and \(\beta\) is a unital linear chain map. For a homogeneous \(g\) set \[ \begin{gathered} H_G(g)=hg\\ \quad+(-1)^{|g|}Egh\\ \quad-\beta(g)h. \end{gathered} \tag{C.68.4} \] The Hom derivation rule gives \[ \begin{gathered} \partial H_G+H_G\partial=1-v\beta,\\ H_G^2=\beta H_G=H_Gv=0. \end{gathered} \tag{C.68.5} \] For example the first two terms in (C.68.4) contract to the inclusion \(g\mapsto\beta(g)E\); the final term changes that inclusion to \(\beta(g)1_V\), since \(\partial h=1-E\). The three displayed side conditions follow from \(h^2=Eh=hE=0\) and the zero \(ee\) entry of \(hg,Egh,h\). These are identities on every homogeneous matrix. They show directly that \(v\) is a mapping-complex quasi-isomorphism.

The bridge has maps \((f,g,a)\) of dimensions \(1+9+9=19\), with \(a\) shifted as in (C.68.2). Its geometric projection kernel is contracted by \[ \begin{gathered} k_q(f,0,a)\\ \quad=(\beta(a),0,-H_G(a)). \end{gathered} \tag{C.68.6} \] Indeed inserting (C.68.5) into (C.68.2) gives \(Dk_q+k_qD=1\) on that kernel. Its scalar projection kernel is contracted by \(k_p(0,g,a)=(0,-a,0)\), the cone-of-identity contraction. The two kernel dimensions are respectively \(10\) and \(18\). The chain section of the geometric projection is \[ j_1(g)=(\beta(g),g,-H_G(g)). \tag{C.68.7} \] It preserves the unit by (C.68.5).

Here is an explicit all-length recursion. For a full suspended input word \(c=sg_1|\cdots|sg_q\), use the bar differential whose unary term is \(s\partial g\) and whose binary term on adjacent letters is \((-1)^{|g_i|-1}s(g_ig_{i+1})\), with the preceding suspended tensor sign. Write \(b_1,b_2\) for those two parts, and use \(j[c]\) for the corresponding unsuspended cobar generator image. For \(q\geq2\) set \[ \begin{gathered} O[c]=j[b_2c]\\ \quad-\sum_{c=c_L|c_R}(-1)^{|c_L|}\\ \qquad{}\cdot j[c_L]j[c_R],\\ j[c]=k_qO[c]. \end{gathered} \tag{C.68.8} \] Both sides use shorter words in the first two lines. Theorem C.68.1.1 proves that this solves the full equation \(D j[c]=j[b_1c]+O[c]\), including its source unary terms. It also proves the ordinary-unit normalization at every length. Geometric projection of every higher component is zero.

Let \(A=E_{e,y}\), \(B=E_{y,e}\), and \(C=E_{e,f}\). Then \[ \begin{gathered} \partial A=-C,\quad \partial B=0,\\ AB=E,\\ \beta(A)=\beta(B)=0. \end{gathered} \tag{C.68.9} \] In the scalar projection of (C.68.8) at \(sA|sB\), the obstruction is \(-\beta(AB)+\beta(A)\beta(B)=-1\). Its second scalar component on \((A,B)\) is zero by degree. Consequently its full source unary equation is \(0=-w_2(C,B)-1\), and hence \[ w_2(E_{e,f},E_{y,e})=-1. \tag{C.68.10} \] Thus the higher section cannot be replaced by its linear component.

Finally, every nonzero-degree matrix must map to zero under a graded map to \(k\). The identities \(E_{e,f}E_{f,e}=E_{e,e}\), \(E_{y,f}E_{f,y}=E_{y,y}\), and \(E_{f,e}E_{e,f}=E_{f,f}\) then force all three diagonal matrices to map to zero under any such algebra map. Their sum is \(1_V\), so no unital graded algebra augmentation exists. The full normalized argument therefore applies to a source for which an augmented reduced bar-cobar counit is unavailable. \(\square\)

Exercise C.68.5.2 (distinct geometric representatives and their entire path; advanced). Enlarge the geometric category to the two actual complexes \(X_0=V\) and \(X_1=Q=ke\), with projection \(p:V\to Q\), inclusion \(i:Q\to V\), and the same \(h\) as above. Use bridge objects \(r_0=(k,V,1_V)\), \(r_1=(k,Q,p)\). Compute their full bridge mapping dimensions and a normalized homotopy retraction. Check its third-component sign on full natural-transformation cochains for the source \(k[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2\), \(|\epsilon|=2\), when every functor sends \(\epsilon\) to zero.

Solution. A map \(r_i\to r_j\) has a scalar component, a matrix \(X_i\to X_j\), and a shifted matrix \(V\to X_j\). Thus \[ \begin{gathered} \dim R_{00}=19,\\ \dim R_{01}=7,\\ \dim R_{10}=13,\\ \dim R_{11}=5. \end{gathered} \tag{C.68.11} \] Their sum is \(44\). On the kernel of the scalar projection the contractions are \[ \begin{gathered} i=0:\quad k_p(0,g,a)\\ \quad=(0,-a,0),\\ i=1:\quad k_p(0,g,a)\\ \quad=(0,-ai,(-1)^r ah), \end{gathered} \tag{C.68.12} \] where \(r\) is the input total degree. Substituting \(pi=1\), \(ip=E\), and \(\partial h=1-E\) into (C.68.2) gives \(Dk_p+k_pD=1\) and \(k_p^2=0\).

For the other kernel, put \(\beta_j(a)=a_{ee}\), \(h_0=h,h_1=0\), and let \(E_j\) project \(X_j\) onto its \(e\)-line. On a homogeneous \(a:V\to X_j\) set \[ \begin{gathered} H_j(a)=h_j a\\ \quad+(-1)^{|a|}E_jah\\ \quad-\beta_j(a)h_j. \end{gathered} \tag{C.68.13} \] Its contraction identity is \(\partial H_j+H_j\partial=1-u_j\beta_j\), where \(u_0=1_V,u_1=p\). To check this, the first two terms contract to the map \(a\mapsto\beta_j(a)i_jp\), with \(i_0=i,i_1=1_Q\). The last term changes this to \(\beta_j(a)u_j\), because \(\partial h_j=u_j-i_jp\). The side conditions follow as in (C.68.5). Hence \((f,0,a)\mapsto(\beta_j(a),0,-H_j(a))\) contracts the geometric projection kernel. The scalar and geometric projection kernels have total dimensions \(40\) and \(28\).

The closed maps \(F:r_0\to r_1\), \(I:r_1\to r_0\), and their degree-minus-one homotopy are \[ \begin{gathered} F=(1,p,0),\\ I=(1,i,h),\\ H_R=(0,h,0),\\ H_R\in R^{-1}(r_0,r_0). \end{gathered} \tag{C.68.14} \] Their products give \[ \begin{gathered} FI=1_{r_1},\\ D H_R=1_{r_0}-IF,\\ H_R^2=0,\\ F H_R=H_R I=0. \end{gathered} \tag{C.68.15} \] In contrast, \(D(1,i,0)=(0,0,1-E)\ne0\). The third component of the actual inverse map is necessary. There is no strict dg object isomorphism between these bridge objects: its geometric projection would give an invertible graded map from a three-dimensional complex to a one-dimensional complex.

For the last assertion, a cochain of total degree \(r\) at source Taylor length \(q\) has bridge output degree \(r+q\). Its third component has ordinary matrix degree \(r+q-1\). Since the source actions on \(\epsilon\) vanish, its Nat differential is the bridge differential. Composing a left cochain at length \(p\) and total degree \(r_2\) with a right one at length \(q\) and total degree \(r_1\) has tensor coefficient \((-1)^{r_1p}\). Thus the two third-component terms in the bridge are \[ \begin{gathered} (-1)^{r_1p}a_2v(f_1),\\ (-1)^{r_1p+r_2+p}g_2a_1. \end{gathered} \tag{C.68.16} \] Computing instead in the path of full Nat complexes gives the second sign \((-1)^{r_2+(r_1-1)p}\), which is equal to the one displayed. The first signs agree directly. This checks the resolved comparison with its full Taylor composition. On the canonical inclusion \(j(U)\), every third component is zero and the comparison is the identity. \(\square\)

Theorems C.68.1.1 and C.68.3.1 give the full normalized projection and actual dg bridge. Lemma C.68.2.1 and Theorem C.68.4.1 retain prescribed full faces of the fixed-outer-type operator diagram. Exercises C.68.5.1–C.68.5.2 compute the forced second component and the actual homotopy retraction. Editable SVG source.

C.69. Full horizontal operator composition

Evaluation retains every marked natural transformation and every original source input. Its complete coalgebra formula gives associative horizontal substitution, including the mixed higher term relating the two whiskering orders. The formulas also retain the higher components of a nonlinear change of enhanced model.

C.69.1. Evaluation with every parameter mark retained

Let \(A,B,C\) be unital dg categories over the chosen split coefficients. Use normalized uncurved unital A-infinity functors and their full natural transformation dg categories \(\operatorname{Fun}_\infty(A,B)\), as in C.53.1, C.67.3 and C.68.1. Here \(B_{\rm full}A\) means the tensor bar on ALL original mapping spaces, including ordinary identity letters. It is used only for explicit formulas. No quasi-isomorphism claim for its unreduced bar-cobar counit is used.

The suspended natural transformation \(s\theta\) has degree \(|\theta|-1\). On an original source word \(c\), its suspended output map is evaluated with that degree. For clarity, all words below are in target-to-source order.

Theorem C.69.1.1 (the complete evaluation coalgebra map). There is a chain coalgebra map \[ \begin{gathered} \operatorname{ev}_{A,B}:\\ B_{\rm full}\operatorname{Fun}_\infty(A,B)\\ \quad\otimes B_{\rm full}A\\ \longrightarrow B_{\rm full}B. \end{gathered} \tag{C.69.1} \]

Its object value at \((F,x)\) is \(F(x)\). At an operator word of length \(r\) and a source word of length \(L\), its values are finite sums of output words of length at most \(L+r\). Its one-operator-letter formula is the full marked natural transformation expansion, including its source-length-zero term. The construction retains units, all original object/arrow labels and every parameter and source cut.

Proof. Suppose the operator word is \(s\theta_r|\cdots|s\theta_1\) between \(F_0,\ldots,F_r\). Split the source word into consecutive pieces. Assign one piece, possibly empty, to each \(\theta_i\), retaining their original order. Between these marked pieces allow any number of nonempty pieces assigned to the intervening functor \(F_i\). Evaluate each piece by that functor's suspended Taylor map, or by \(s\theta_i\) at a marked piece, and concatenate the resulting \(B\)-letters. Sum over all these assignments.

Each marked map is used exactly once. Move \(s\theta_i\), originally before the entire source input, past the source letters preceding its assigned piece. Its coefficient is

\[ (-1)^{(|\theta_i|-1)|c_{<i}|}, \tag{C.69.2} \] where \(|c_{<i}|\) is the total suspended degree of the original source letters preceding that marked piece.

Multiply those coefficients over all marks. Unmarked suspended functor maps have degree zero. Thus this rule specifies every tensor-evaluation Koszul sign without a separate choice of signs at empty pieces. It is the same rule as C67's marked insertion, now keeping the whole output word.

There are at most \(L\) unmarked pieces and exactly \(r\) marked pieces. There are finitely many placements, including the empty marked pieces; each Taylor value is an algebraic finite sum. This proves the bound and finiteness.

A cut of an output word lies between two evaluated pieces. It therefore cuts both the operator word and the original source word, at their unique corresponding positions. Conversely, an operator cut and a source cut, together with an assignment on each side, concatenate to exactly one assignment with that output cut. Reordering the two right/left tensor factors contributes the ordinary tensor-coalgebra sign. It is exactly the sign obtained by moving the original suspended marks past the same source letters in the concatenated assignment. This proves the coalgebra equation. It includes cuts before or after an empty marked piece.

For the chain equation expand the unary differential and adjacent binary composition on the output. On an unmarked run their terms are exactly the bar functor equation for its \(F_i\). At one marked output and its neighboring unmarked runs they are the defining full Nat differential, including the left and right functor actions. If two marked outputs become adjacent, their binary composition is precisely the full vertical Nat product, with its suspended binary sign. These are the unary and binary terms of the operator bar differential, since the target \(B\) is a dg category.

On the source side an original unary term remains in its assigned piece. An adjacent source-composition term internal to a piece appears in the same functor or Nat equation. At a boundary between two pieces its two possible placements have the opposite signs of the corresponding output cut terms; these are the cut terms in the same bar equations. Thus every term is accounted for by an unmarked run, one marked slot, two marked slots, or a cut between their pieces. The signs agree by the stated tensor rule: a degree-one differential passing a preceding suspended piece has exactly its tensor differential sign, and merging two marked slots has the defining suspended Nat product sign. The equations of C53.1 and C67.3 therefore give \[ \begin{gathered} b_B\operatorname{ev}_{A,B}\\ \quad=\operatorname{ev}_{A,B}d_\otimes,\\ d_\otimes=b_{\operatorname{Fun}}\otimes1\\ \qquad+1\otimes b_A, \end{gathered} \tag{C.69.3} \] with the graded tensor convention on the second summand.

This proves the chain equation on every original input, rather than only on closed parameter marks. Empty operator words give the original full bar map of \(F\). Ordinary identities are retained as outputs; higher normalized components vanish at an ordinary source unit and the neighboring unit terms cancel as in C68.1. No input identity was erased in this calculation. The piece/cut formulas do not introduce a new original source object, so they retain the asserted labels and restrictions. \(\square\)

C.69.2. Entire horizontal composition and exact associativity

Theorem C.69.2.1 (full horizontal substitution). Evaluation determines a chain coalgebra map \[ \begin{gathered} M_{A,B,C}:\\ B_{\rm full}\operatorname{Fun}_\infty(B,C)\\ \quad\otimes B_{\rm full}\operatorname{Fun}_\infty(A,B)\\ \longrightarrow B_{\rm full}\operatorname{Fun}_\infty(A,C). \end{gathered} \tag{C.69.4} \]

Its object map is \((G,F)\mapsto GF\). It is associative as an entire coalgebra map, with the identity functors as strict units. It retains the full higher horizontal components. It is not asserted to be a strict dg bifunctor on the underlying full Nat categories.

On operator words of lengths \(r,s\) and an original \(A\)-input of length \(L\), its evaluated values are finite and have \(C\)-output length at most \(L+r+s\). With any finite number of nested operator levels the analogous bound is \(L\) plus the sum of the original parameter lengths. No degree-positivity assumption is used for this bound.

Proof. First define the single-output Nat Taylor cochain of \(M\) on nonempty combined operator input by the single \(C\)-letter projection of \[ \begin{gathered} \operatorname{ev}_{B,C}\bigl(u\otimes\\ \qquad\operatorname{ev}_{A,B}(v\otimes c)\bigr),\\ u\in B_{\rm full}\operatorname{Fun}_\infty(B,C),\\ v\in B_{\rm full}\operatorname{Fun}_\infty(A,B),\\ c\in B_{\rm full}A. \end{gathered} \tag{C.69.5} \]

This specifies its value on every original \(A\)-word, including length zero. The two empty operator words instead specify the object \(GF\). These values have the required degree: a one-letter output has its single suspension, whereas the input has \(r+s\) suspended operator letters. Its ordinary Nat degree is consequently the sum of the ordinary parameter degrees minus \(r+s\) plus one. Tensor evaluation uses exactly the signs of Theorem C.69.1.1.

Reconstruct the coalgebra map \(M\) from this single-output map. Explicitly, split each of the two operator words into \(m\) consecutive pieces, allowing empty pieces but never two empty pieces in the same column. In column \(j\) apply the just-defined one-output cochain to the outer and inner pieces, and concatenate its \(m\) suspended outputs. Write \(u_j,v_j\) for the outer and inner pieces in column \(j\). The coefficient for reordering the original tensor into these columns is \[ (-1)^{\sum_{i<j}|v_i||u_j|}, \tag{C.69.6} \] where the degrees are suspended bar degrees. Sum over the columns and all \(m\) from \(1\) to \(r+s\). This is the consecutive-cut reconstruction into the cofree tensor bar. Its coalgebra equation follows by cutting the column sequence. It is the unique coalgebra map with the specified object and one-output values: the length-\(m\) component of a coalgebra map is its iterated coproduct followed by its one-output projection in all \(m\) slots.

There is an exact evaluation identity \[ \begin{gathered} \operatorname{ev}_{A,C}(M_{A,B,C}\otimes1)\\ \quad=\operatorname{ev}_{B,C} (1\otimes\operatorname{ev}_{A,B}). \end{gathered} \tag{C.69.7} \]

Both sides are coalgebra maps. Their one-\(C\)-letter projections agree by the definition of \(M\): only a single marked Nat output can contribute to that projection on nonempty operator input. The empty operator input gives the ordinary bar map of the composite \(GF\) on both sides. The cofree uniqueness just proved therefore gives the entire identity.

To check the chain equation for \(M\), use the chain equations for both evaluations in this identity. The resulting defect is a coderivation over \(M\). Its one-Nat-letter component, evaluated on each original \(A\)-word, is the one-\(C\)-letter component of that identity's chain defect, and hence is zero. The ordinary source unary differential is among these chain defects. A coderivation into a cofree bar is determined by its one-letter component, by cutting on its two sides. Thus the entire defect is zero.

For three operator levels, evaluate either proposed associative composite on an original \(A\)-word. Repeated application of the exact evaluation identity gives in both cases the same nested three evaluations, with the same tensor associativity identification. All its signs move the same original homogeneous factors through the same permutation. Taking one-output components and using cofree uniqueness proves exact associativity of \(M\). Equivalently both expansions are the same planar levelled consecutive-piece assignments; flattening those levels does not change the original cuts.

Evaluation by an identity functor has only its linear Taylor component. The piece formula therefore gives the identity map on every full Nat word when either identity functor is substituted as the empty operator level. This proves strict units. Normalization of higher parameter components also follows directly: an identity parameter mark gives an ordinary identity output; the next positive Taylor map vanishes at that argument. If no such positive Taylor map occurs, the component is the required unary identity component. Ordinary source-unit normalization is the same argument applied inside the pieces. Finally the two evaluations bound their output lengths first by \(L+s\), then by \(L+s+r\). Iteration proves the last assertion, including arbitrary nonminimal unary input complexes. \(\square\)

C.69.3. The mixed higher seam cannot be omitted

Lemma C.69.3.1 (the actual mixed composition homotopy). Let \(\theta:F_0\to F_1\) and \(\eta:G_0\to G_1\) be closed degree-zero full Nat maps. The one-output part of \(M\) on \(s\eta\otimes s\theta\) is a degree-minus-one full Nat cochain \(K\). With target-to-source word order it satisfies \[ \begin{gathered} dK=(\eta F_1)(G_0\theta)\\ \qquad-(G_1\theta)(\eta F_0). \end{gathered} \tag{C.69.8} \]

Proof. The entire coalgebra image of that two-mark input has one-letter part \(sK\) and two-letter part \[ \begin{gathered} s(\eta F_1)|s(G_0\theta)\\ \qquad-s(G_1\theta)|s(\eta F_0). \end{gathered} \tag{C.69.9} \]

The minus sign is the tensor-coalgebra interchange of the two suspended degree-minus-one marks. Their source differential is zero. Applying the target bar differential, whose binary sign on two degree-zero maps is minus, gives exactly the displayed equation. This is a chain homotopy between the two full whiskering products. It need not vanish even when all four functor objects are strict dg functors. \(\square\)

C.69.4. Solved calculations

Exercise C.69.4.1 (a nonzero mixed composition term; advanced). Let \(A=k\). Let \(B\) have objects \(0,1\), their identities, and the arrow complex from \(0\) to \(1\) with basis \(a^{-1},b^0,c^0\), differential \(da=b\), and no other nonidentity mappings. Let \[ \begin{gathered} X=ke^0\oplus kf^{-1}\\ \qquad\oplus ky^0,\\ df=y,\\ K_X(e)=f,\\ K_X(f)=0,\\ K_X(y)=0,\\ L=\partial K_X,\\ C=\operatorname{End}(X). \end{gathered} \tag{C.69.10} \] Both objects of every \(G_t:B\to C\), for \(t=0,1,2\), map to \(X\). Define their nonidentity arrow images by \[ \begin{gathered} G_t(a)=tK_X,\\ G_t(b)=tL,\\ G_t(c)=1-tL. \end{gathered} \tag{C.69.11} \] Find a closed full transformation \(\eta:G_0\to G_1\) with identity bare components, and compute the mixed term for \(\theta=c\) between the two object functors \(k\to B\). Check the role of the source differential and ordinary identity outputs.

Solution. The only nonzero matrix entry of \(L\) is \(L(e)=y\). It is closed and nonzero. The maps \(G_t\) preserve \(da=b\), since \(\partial(tK_X)=tL\); all other differential equations are immediate. There is no composable pair of nonidentity arrows, and identity products are preserved. Thus all three are strict unital dg functors.

Set the bare components of \(\eta\) to \(1_X\), and set \[ \begin{gathered} \eta_1(c)=K_X,\\ \eta_1(b)=-K_X,\\ \eta_1(a)=0. \end{gathered} \tag{C.69.12} \] Higher normalized source components vanish. At source length one its degree-zero Nat differential is \[ \begin{gathered} (d\eta)_1(z)=\partial\eta_1(z)\\ \quad-\eta_0(1)G_0(z)\\ \quad+G_1(z)\eta_0(0)\\ \quad+\eta_1(dz). \end{gathered} \tag{C.69.13} \] At \(c\) this is \(L-1+(1-L)=0\). At \(b\) it is \(-L+L=0\). At \(a\) it is \(K_X-K_X=0\), with the second term here supplied by \(\eta_1(da)\). Ignoring the original source unary differential would leave a nonzero defect. The bare components are closed. A source identity is handled by its two canceling unit actions. Any longer normalized input contains an identity and vanishes; its neighboring unit terms cancel in the same way. Thus \(\eta\) is closed in the full normalized complex.

For \(\theta=c\), the one-letter part of the nested evaluation is \(\eta_1(c)=K_X\). The two full whiskering products in (C.69.8) are \(1_X\) and \(1_X-L\). The mixed cochain consequently has \(K_0=K_X\), and \(dK_0=L\ne0\). Its entire two-mark coalgebra value is \[ \begin{gathered} sK_X+s1_X|s1_X\\ \quad-s(1_X-L)|s1_X. \end{gathered} \tag{C.69.14} \] The binary bar differential of its two-letter part is \(-sL\), canceling \(s\partial K_X\). Dropping the one-letter mixed term therefore breaks the full chain equation. The identity matrices in those two-letter terms are actual output letters; removing them would break that same equation. \(\square\)

Exercise C.69.4.2 (nonlinear change of model and full marked composition; advanced). Use the normalized \(A_\infty\) model map \(w:\operatorname{End}(X)\to k\) of Exercise C.68.5.1, including its nonzero second component. At either source object of \(B\), take two bare cochains with matrix values \(E_{e,f}\) and \(E_{y,e}\), in that target-to-source order. Compute the bare component of the second Taylor operation of \(w_*\). Explain how the exact evaluation identity controls arbitrary marked words, rather than only this one bare value.

Solution. Both linear scalar images are zero. Their composite input has the higher value proved in (C.68.10), so \[ \begin{gathered} (w_*)_2(E_{e,f},E_{y,e})_0\\ \qquad=-1. \end{gathered} \tag{C.69.15} \] Its degree is consistent: the two ordinary parameter degrees are \(1,0\), so the second operation has output degree \(1+0-1=0\). Replacing \(w\) by its linear map would give zero and lose this actual full operation.

On a complete operator word, partition its original parameter letters into nonempty consecutive groups. The group output is the single-letter part of \(B w\) applied to that group's full evaluation. Concatenate these outputs over all groupings. This is exactly the cofree formula in the proof of Theorem C.69.2.1 when the outer operator word is empty and its object is \(w\). Evaluation of this entire reconstructed bar word equals \(B w\) of the original full evaluation, by (C.69.7). Each side retains all ordinary source identities, every original unary differential, and all higher \(w_q\) allowed by the original input length. Its finiteness bound is the one proved in Theorem C.69.2.1; no truncation at the linear or bare component is involved. \(\square\)

Theorems C.69.1.1–C.69.2.1 give complete evaluation and associative horizontal substitution. Lemma C.69.3.1 identifies the mixed full-cochain homotopy. Exercises C.69.4.1–C.69.4.2 compute the required nonzero source and model-change components. Editable SVG source.

C.70. Split model bridges and horizontal transport

A full-differential contraction retains conditions imposed on an entire split source image. It gives an exact identity-leading unit comparison and transports the complete operator bars across changing intermediate types. The construction keeps the higher Taylor terms of its split models.

C.70.1. A relative contraction preserved by the full differential

Let \(K\) be the full normalized Nat kernel of a graded-surjective mapping quasi-isomorphism, with fixed unital \(A_\infty\) functor objects and a dg target. Use the original source-word Taylor filtration from Theorem C.68.1.1. Choose the output kernel contraction \(H_0\), with \(H_0\) squared zero. Its leading Hom differential \(d_0\) includes every source unary differential. Thus

\[ d_0H_0+H_0d_0=1. \tag{C.70.1} \]

Every term of \(\delta=d-d_0\) consumes positive original source input length. This means that its evaluation on a word of length \(L\) uses cochain values at shorter source lengths; no assertion about the cohomological degrees of those words is needed.

Theorem C.70.1.1 (full-differential relative contraction). Put

\[ \begin{gathered}T=dH_0+H_0d=1+J,\\ H=H_0T^{-1}\\ \quad=H_0\sum_{n\geq0}(-J)^n.\end{gathered} \tag{C.70.2} \]

The series is finite on each original input, and \(H\) is a normalized contraction of \(K\). If a graded subspace \(K_{\rm rel}\) of \(K\) is stable under the full differential \(d\) and \(H_0\), then \(H\) preserves \(K_{\rm rel}\). Separate stability under \(d_0\) and \(\delta\) is not required.

Proof. The leading identity gives \(J=\delta H_0+H_0\delta\), so \(J\) consumes positive original input length. Its inverse series has at most \(L+1\) terms on a word of length \(L\). Both \(dT=Td\) and \(H_0T=TH_0\) hold: the first follows from \(d\) squared zero, and the second from \(H_0\) squared zero, since both \(H_0 T\) and \(T H_0\) equal \(H_0dH_0\). These identities extend to the finite inverse series on each input. Consequently

\[ \begin{gathered}dH+Hd=TT^{-1}=1,\\ H^2=H_0^2T^{-2}=0.\end{gathered} \tag{C.70.3} \]

All operations preserve normalized source-unit conditions. If \(K_{\rm rel}\) is stable under \(d\) and \(H_0\), it is stable under \(T\), \(J\) and each term of the finite inverse. Therefore \(H\) preserves \(K_{\rm rel}\). This proof uses the full differential to establish relative stability, even if its leading and perturbing parts do not separately preserve the imposed source-image condition. \(\square\)

One useful such condition is vanishing after precomposition with a fixed unital \(A_\infty\) functor \(j\). Precomposition of full Nat cochains is a dg functor, by the bar formula in Theorem C.69.2.1. Its kernel is stable under \(d\). Postcomposition of its output values by the fixed endpoint contraction \(H_0\) preserves this vanishing condition as well. This remains true when \(Bj\) contains lower-word-length Taylor outputs: for each fixed original outer endpoint pair the same output contraction applies to every term.

C.70.2. An exact unit relative to a chosen split source image

Let \(q:R\to G\) be a unital dg functor, identical on its object labels and graded-surjective and quasi-isomorphic on mappings. By Theorem C.68.1.1 choose a normalized unital \(A_\infty\) section \(j:G\to R\) with \(qj=\operatorname{Id}_G\) exactly. The endomorphism \(E=jq\) of \(R\) is then exactly idempotent as an \(A_\infty\) functor, and it fixes the object labels. No augmentation of \(G\) or \(R\) is assumed.

Theorem C.70.2.1 (an actual relative identity-leading unit). There is a closed degree-zero full Nat isomorphism

\[ u:\operatorname{Id}_R\longrightarrow E, \tag{C.70.4} \]

with bare components \(1_R\) and with the exact full identities

\[ \begin{gathered}q_*u=\operatorname{Id}_q,\\ u j=\operatorname{Id}_j.\end{gathered} \tag{C.70.5} \]

Its inverse is finite on each original source word and has the same two projection/restriction identities. In particular

\[ \begin{gathered}u E=\operatorname{Id}_E,\\ E_{*,1}(u)=\operatorname{Id}_E.\end{gathered} \tag{C.70.6} \]

Here \(E_{*,1}\) is the unary full postcomposition operation. Higher mixed one-output components containing this unit and an image of \(j\) vanish by ordinary parameter-unit normalization. The entire bar operation still retains its usual identity-letter insertion terms.

Proof. In \(\operatorname{Nat}_\infty(\operatorname{Id}_R,E)\), start with \(u_0\) having bare components \(1_R\) and all positive Taylor components zero. Its \(q\) projection is exactly the identity of \(q\). Also \(u_0 j\) is exactly \(\operatorname{Id}_j\): the empty source component is the identity and the uncurved bar map \(Bj\) sends a positive word to positive words. The two restricted functor objects coincide, since \(\operatorname{Id}_Rj=j\) and \(Ej=jqj=j\). Thus the chain defect \(d u_0\) takes values in ker \(q\) and vanishes after precomposition \(j\). Its bare component is zero.

This relative kernel is stable under the full Nat differential. Its leading output contraction \(H_0\) preserves vanishing on \(Bj\), as just proved. Theorem C.70.1.1 therefore contracts it. Define

\[ u=u_0-Hd u_0. \tag{C.70.7} \]

The defect is closed, so \(du=du_0-dHdu_0=0\). The correction remains in ker \(q\) and vanishes on \(Bj\), proving both exact identities. Neither \(H_0\) nor \(J\) creates a shorter required cochain input, so a cochain with zero bare component retains that property. Hence \(u\) still has bare components \(1_R\).

Write \(u=1+n\) as a graded full Nat matrix between its two functor objects. Each \(n\) term consumes positive original input length. The convolution series \(1-n+n^2-\cdots\) is therefore finite on each input, is a two-sided inverse by multiplication of the finite geometric series, and is closed by the full dg product derivation rule. The dg functors \(q_*\) and precomposition \(j\) preserve these exact inverse identities, so the inverse projects and restricts to their identity transformations too.

Finally \(uE=(uj)q=\operatorname{Id}_E\) by strict associativity of precomposition. Entire horizontal associativity from Theorem C.69.2.1 gives

\[ \begin{gathered}E_{*,1}(u)=j_{*,1}(q_*u)\\ \quad=j_{*,1}(\operatorname{Id}_q)\\ \quad=\operatorname{Id}_E.\end{gathered} \tag{C.70.8} \]

The last equality is normalized unitality of the entire postcomposition functor.
