The actual cut coefficient is \((-1)^{1+i+d(v)+\chi}\). After rescaling it is therefore exactly \((-1)^i\), the augmented order-complex coboundary sign.

The unary terms also have an explicit transformed sign. Before rescaling, differentiating an original letter has the sign of all preceding interleaved suspended letters, plus the number of preceding cobar blocks. The change in \(\pi\) converts the first part to the sign in the original first-word-then-second-word tensor order. The change in \(\sum_vd(v)\) counts the internal vertices after its block. Adding that count to the preceding block count gives \(k-1\). Thus the transformed unary operator is \((-1)^{k-1}d_{\rm orig}\). The augmented order cochain degree is \(k-2\). Consequently this is the tensor differential of the finite augmented grid-order cochains with the original letter complex equipped with \(-d_{\rm orig}\), followed by the cohomological shift \([-2]\). The shift is even and does not change the differential sign. A contraction on the first factor therefore anticommutes with the entire original unary operator. No assumption of zero unary differential is used here.

Suppose \(p\geq2\). In the proper grid poset choose \(a=(1,0)\) and the closure \(c(v)=\max(v,a)\). Its value is never the excluded top: increasing a first coordinate from zero to one cannot make that coordinate \(p\). Its value is not the bottom either. The order maps satisfy \(\operatorname{Id}\leq c\) and \(\operatorname{const}_a\leq c\).

For completeness, if order maps \(f\leq g\) are comparable, their chain prism on a strict simplex is the alternating sum \[ \begin{gathered}P(f,g)(\sigma)\\ \quad=\sum_i(-1)^i\tau_i,\\ \sigma=[v_0<\cdots<v_t],\\ \tau_i=[fv_0\leq\cdots\leq fv_i\\ \qquad\leq gv_i\leq\cdots\leq gv_t],\end{gathered} \tag{C.75.2} \] with repeated-vertex terms set to zero. The inequalities hold because the maps preserve order and \(f\leq g\). In its boundary, deleting a vertex away from the seam cancels the corresponding prism of the boundary; deleting a seam vertex cancels the neighboring seam, except for the two end terms. Hence \(\partial P+P\partial=g_*-f_*\). This includes the augmented empty simplex, on which the prism is zero. Let \(Q\) send that empty simplex to \([a]\) and all other basis simplices to zero. Directly \(\partial Q+Q\partial=(\operatorname{const}_a)_*\). Therefore \[ \begin{gathered}Q-P(\operatorname{Id},c)\\ \quad+P(\operatorname{const}_a,c).\end{gathered} \tag{C.75.3} \] contracts the full augmented chain complex. Dualize this finite poset, tensor with the original letter complex and conjugate the preceding sign rescaling. This contracts the actual leading source block, including unary terms. If \(q\geq2\), interchange the coordinates and use \((0,1)\) instead.

The target leading block is the tensor product of the two original-word cut complexes. If either count is at least two, its factor is contracted by the first-boundary homotopy of Theorem C.72.1.1. Tensoring that homotopy with the other factor, with its differential signs, contracts the whole target block. Thus the leading projection is a quasi-isomorphism in these cases, and its surjective mapping kernel is acyclic.

If \(p=0\) or \(q=0\), the projection on the entire block is just the corresponding single-factor identity. The only remaining case is \(p=q=1\). The proper grid has two incomparable vertices. Its augmented cochains are \(k\to k^2\), with diagonal differential, tensored with the original two-letter complex as above. The target has one copy of that original complex. Explicitly the source mixed generator satisfies \[ \begin{gathered}D_0\mathsf t(sa\otimes sb)\\ \quad=(-1)^{|a|}\bigl(x_ay_b\\ \qquad-(-1)^{|a||b|}y_bx_a\bigr).\end{gathered} \tag{C.75.4} \] The two ordered products project respectively to \(x_a\otimes y_b\) and \((-1)^{|a||b|}x_a\otimes y_b\). Under the displayed source rescaling and the target rescaling \((-1)^{|a|}\), their map is the difference \(k^2\to k\). Its kernel is the image of the diagonal, contracted by its inverse from that image to the augmented copy of \(k\). The rescaled source and target unary differential is the same \(-d_{\rm orig}\). This contraction therefore includes the full unary terms. It proves the leading quasi-isomorphism in the last case.

For the short exact sequence used above, the kernel of a surjective chain map between acyclic complexes is acyclic directly: a kernel cycle has a source primitive; its image is a target cycle; lift a target primitive and subtract its differential from the source primitive. This gives a kernel primitive. Choose coefficient-linear normalized contractions on these actual leading kernels, separately at every original \((p,q)\), using the splitting argument of Section C.30.1. The scalar block has zero kernel. These choices preserve total original count.

The actual \(\rho\) still has this same graded kernel. The binary bar products, scalar binary outputs, and scalar unary outputs strictly lower total original count, exactly as in Theorem C.74.1.1. Since both full and leading projections are chain maps, their difference preserves the kernel. If \(H_0\) is the chosen leading kernel contraction, the actual kernel contraction is the finite perturbation \[ \begin{gathered}H\\ \quad=H_0(1+\delta H_0)^{-1}.\end{gathered} \tag{C.75.5} \] Every further factor strictly lowers the original count, so the series terminates on every input. Lemma C.35.1.1 proves the contraction and its normalized side conditions. The actual kernel is therefore acyclic; together with graded surjectivity, this proves the claimed mapping quasi-isomorphism of \(\rho\). Applying its contraction to \((1-s_\rho\rho)\) also gives the full linear mapping SDR with that actual section.

Finally, factor bar functors never send a nonempty word to the coalgebra coaugmentation: even a coefficient output is an ordinary one-letter bar output. Hence a mixed generator stays mixed before normalization and projects to zero on both sides of the naturality equation. A pure-factor generator has exactly its \(QF\) or \(QG\) image. Coefficient outputs and all their actual unit relations were already checked. Extending by products proves exact naturality for the entire factor functors. Zero-identity objects are treated as in Theorem C.72.1.1. \(\square\)

C.75.2. The strict shuffle common-input span

Theorem C.75.2.1 (the actual unital tensor span). The full tensor-bar shuffle induces a strict unital dg functor \[ \begin{gathered}\zeta:T(A,B)\\ \quad\longrightarrow Q^{\mathrm u}(A\otimes B).\end{gathered} \tag{C.75.6} \] It is a mapping quasi-isomorphism, and its exact actual counit square is \[ \begin{gathered}\epsilon_{A\otimes B}\zeta\\ \quad=(\epsilon_A\otimes\epsilon_B)\rho.\end{gathered} \tag{C.75.7} \] Thus \(T(A,B)\) is a common input for the two actual unital tensor models, with the given literal object labels. The shuffle side need not be graded-surjective. This span is strictly natural for strict dg factor maps; no tensor product of general \(A_\infty\) functors is inferred.

Proof. Embed a first-factor bar letter as \(s(a\otimes1)\) and a second-factor letter as \(s(1\otimes b)\), and sum their ordered shuffles with the suspended Koszul signs. The adjacent unequal-factor bar products cancel in pairs using the graded commutation in \(A\otimes B\); equal-factor bar products and unary terms give the original factor differentials. Cutting a shuffle is the same as first choosing a cut in each factor and then shuffling both pieces, with the tensor interchange sign. These are precisely the chain and coalgebra calculations of Section C.39.3, and do not use algebra augmentations or positive mapping degrees. Thus the actual full shuffle is a chain coalgebra map here as well.

A coefficient input becomes a global coefficient letter. On a generator of total length at least two, each shuffled word containing that argument is therefore a higher unit-degenerate generator in the target \(Q\), and is zero. A single coefficient generator becomes its actual coefficient. Cobar of the shuffle therefore descends to the stated strict unital dg map.

Check its counit on the original free generators. A single pure letter maps to the corresponding \(a\otimes1\) or \(1\otimes b\) on both sides. At higher total length the shuffle gives words of that same length, whose one cobar block has zero counit. On the other side a mixed generator has zero \(\rho\), and a pure higher block has zero factor counit. Coefficients agree. Extending by products gives the entire exact square, including all scalar products in the differentials.

The actual factor counits are mapping quasi-isomorphisms by Theorem C.72.1.1, and their tensor is one by the split tensor contractions of C.30.1. Theorem C.75.1.1 therefore makes the right-hand composite a quasi-isomorphism. The target counit \(\epsilon_{A\otimes B}\) is also one by Theorem C.72.1.1. Applying these two invertible maps on mapping cohomology proves that \(\zeta\) is a quasi-isomorphism. Finally the original shuffle, coefficient relations and counits commute with strict dg factor maps on every original letter; their full maps and the quotient span consequently do so as well. For example, if each factor has a nonzero reduced mapping \(a,b\), the target has the independent one-letter generator \(x_{a\otimes b}\) in its mixed reduced tensor summand. Every letter in every shuffled image instead belongs to one of the two pure axis summands. Freeness of the normalized graded target makes that mixed generator absent from the image. This proves the stated lack of a general graded-surjectivity conclusion. \(\square\)

C.75.3. Solved tensor calculations

Exercise C.75.3.1 (the kernel size and an odd commutator; advanced). For two copies of \(A=\operatorname{End}(ke^0\oplus kf^{-1}\oplus ky^0)\), \(df=y\), determine the source, target and kernel dimensions at total original rank at most three. Set \(a=E_{ef}\) in each factor, let \(X=\mathsf t(sa\otimes1)\), \(Y=\mathsf t(1\otimes sa)\), and \(z=\mathsf t(sa\otimes sa)\). Compute the differential, kernel primitive and full shuffle image associated to \(XY+YX\).

Solution. Each factor has eight reduced basis letters. At positive total rank \(r\), the source has \((r+1)8^r\) generators, according to the two factor lengths. Thus its generator counts at ranks one, two and three are \(16,192,2048\). Free products give the full word counts \(1,16,448,12288\). A single factor's normalized cobar word counts are \(1,8,128,2048\), since the \(r-1\) internal boundaries can each be present or absent. The target tensor therefore has word counts \(1,16,320,6144\). The exact graded section gives

\[ \begin{gathered}\dim T_{\leq3}=12753,\\ \dim(Q_A\otimes Q_A)_{\leq3}\\ \quad=6481,\\ \dim(\ker\rho)_{\leq3}=6272.\end{gathered} \tag{C.75.8} \]

The differential and kernel contraction retain this finite total-rank subcomplex, so the actual kernel SDR applies to all these kernel vectors. This dimension calculation alone is not the proof of its acyclicity.

Here \(|a|=1\) and \(da=0\). Its suspension has degree zero. The two full tensor cuts give

\[ \begin{gathered}Dz=-XY-YX,\\ \rho(XY)=x_a\otimes x_a,\\ \rho(YX)=-x_a\otimes x_a.\end{gathered} \tag{C.75.9} \]

Thus the degree-two kernel cycle \(XY+YX\) has the actual primitive \(-z\). The minus sign is the factor \((-1)^{|a|}\) in the mixed cut calculation, not an unsigned commutation rule. If \(u=a\otimes1\) and \(v=1\otimes a\), its entire shuffle value is

\[ \begin{gathered}\zeta(z)=\mathsf t(su|sv)\\ \quad+\mathsf t(sv|su).\end{gathered} \tag{C.75.10} \]

The two coefficients are positive because both suspended input degrees are zero. The target binary bar products cancel, since \(uv=-vu\), while its cut terms are exactly the images of \(-XY-YX\). Both shuffle terms are therefore part of the actual chain equation. \(\square\)

Exercise C.75.3.2 (a scalar product remains in the tensor differential; advanced). In the first copy of that algebra take \(a=E_{ef}\), \(b=E_{fe}\); in the second take \(c=E_{ye}\). Write \(h_{u,v}=\mathsf t(su|sv)\) in the first normalized factor and \(y_c=\mathsf t(sc)\) in the second. Compute \(D(h_{a,b}\otimes y_c)\), including the original unary differential, and check its actual counit.

Solution. Matrix multiplication and the original differential give

\[ \begin{gathered}da=dc=0,\quad db=c,\\ ab=1-E_{ff}-E_{yy}.\end{gathered} \tag{C.75.11} \]

The first suspension has degree zero. Hence the first-factor two-letter generator, of degree minus one, has differential

\[ \begin{gathered}Dh_{a,b}=h_{a,c}+1\\ \quad-x_{E_{ff}}-x_{E_{yy}}\\ \quad-x_ax_b.\end{gathered} \tag{C.75.12} \]

Since \(Dy_c=0\), the actual tensor differential is

\[ \begin{gathered}D(h_{a,b}\otimes y_c)\\ \quad=h_{a,c}\otimes y_c\\ \qquad+1\otimes y_c\\ \qquad-x_{E_{ff}}\otimes y_c\\ \qquad-x_{E_{yy}}\otimes y_c\\ \qquad-(x_ax_b)\otimes y_c.\end{gathered} \tag{C.75.13} \]

Its counit is zero: the higher block has zero counit and the remaining coefficient is \((1-E_{ff}-E_{yy}-ab)\otimes c=0\). This agrees with the counit of \(h_{a,b}\otimes y_c\), which is zero. If the scalar product output were omitted, the displayed derivative would instead have counit \(-1\otimes c\ne0\). It would fail the actual counit chain equation. The source's scalar bar term can vanish inside a mixed higher generator through unit degeneration, while this scalar term in a product of pure-factor blocks still survives. The normalized quotient and tensor projection preserve precisely that distinction. \(\square\)

Theorem C.75.1.1 gives the actual normalized tensor projection and its contracted kernel; Theorem C.75.2.1 gives the full shuffle span and exact counit square. Exercises C.75.3.1–C.75.3.2 compute the odd commutator, actual finite kernel dimensions and surviving scalar tensor term. Editable SVG source.

C.76. Finite-factor tensor comparisons and ordered cuts

Every finite ordered family has a common normalized tensor input. Its projection, full multishuffle and regrouping squares retain all unit and unary terms. One finite contraction commutes with every ordered cut, so all intermediate tensor kernels inherit compatible primitives.

C.76.1. All finite factors and one contraction for every ordered cut

Let \(A_1,\ldots,A_m\) be unital dg categories over the split coefficients of Section C.30.1. Put \(T_m=T(A_1,\ldots,A_m)\), as in Theorem C.74.1.1. Keep their literal object tuples and their original factor mapping words. Define \(\rho_m:T_m\to\bigotimes_iQ^{\mathrm u}(A_i)\) on a free generator by its pure-factor value if exactly one factor word is nonempty, and by zero otherwise. The products use the actual graded tensor signs.

More generally, for an ordered partition \(\pi=(I_1|\cdots|I_r)\) into nonempty consecutive blocks write \(T_{I_j}=T(A_i:i\in I_j)\) and define \[ \begin{gathered}\kappa_\pi:T_m\\ \quad\longrightarrow\bigotimes_jT_{I_j}.\end{gathered} \tag{C.76.1} \] It keeps a generator in its single supporting group and kills it if its nonempty factor words meet two groups. Let \(s_\pi\) be the linear section that orders the group blocks consecutively, and set \(P_\pi=s_\pi\kappa_\pi\). For an elementary cut \(c\) write \(P_c\). A partition can be specified by its set \(C\) of cuts.

Theorem C.76.1.1 (finite-factor resolution with simultaneous cut contraction). The maps \(\rho_m\) and every \(\kappa_\pi\) are strict unital dg functors, graded-surjective and mapping quasi-isomorphisms. Their linear sections are actual chain sections. The cut projections satisfy \[ \begin{gathered}P_CP_D=P_DP_C\\ \quad=P_{C\cup D}.\end{gathered} \tag{C.76.2} \] Successive refined \(\kappa\) regroupings are exactly the direct finer regrouping, under the stated ordered tensor identifications.

There is one normalized linear mapping SDR for \(\rho_m\), finite on every original factor word, whose homotopy commutes with every \(P_C\). Its restriction contracts each actual \(\ker\kappa_\pi\). The canonical projection and regrouping maps are strictly natural for entire normalized unital factor functors. No naturality of an arbitrary auxiliary contraction under unrelated factor functors is asserted. At zero factors the maps are coefficient identities; at one factor \(\rho_1\) is the identity of the normalized unital resolution.

Proof. The chain calculation for \(\rho_m\) is the same mixed-cut calculation as in Theorem C.75.1.1. A cut can have two nonzero projected outputs only if the generator's support lies in two factors. Those two orientations cancel with the tensor interchange sign. With three or more nonempty factors at least one cut output is mixed and projects to zero. Pure generators have their ordinary factor differential. The same argument with group coalgebra degrees proves that every \(\kappa_\pi\) is a dg functor. The unit relations descend by Theorem C.74.1.1: a higher unit input is either mixed and killed or remains degenerate in its one group. The normal ordered group lift is a graded section. Its differential is exactly the tensor derivation differential on those groups, including scalar outputs. Thus it is also a linear chain section.

Here is the leading quasi-isomorphism for arbitrary \(m\). Retain all original reduced-letter counts \(\mathbf p=(p_1,\ldots,p_m)\). Keep the full quotient-unary differential and every cobar cut as \(D_0\). For fixed ordered factor words, a cobar word with \(k\) blocks is a chain of \(k-1\) proper interior vertices in the product grid \(\prod_i[0,p_i]\). The endpoints are the zero and full count tuples. All monotone nonzero steps are retained, including simultaneous steps.

Write \(w_{j,i}\) for the suspended word in block \(j\), factor \(i\). The permutation taking the original factor order to the block order has Koszul exponent \[ \begin{gathered}\Pi=\sum_{j<\ell}\sum_{u>v}\\ \qquad|w_{j,u}||w_{\ell,v}|.\end{gathered} \tag{C.76.3} \] Rescale a source chain by \[ \begin{gathered}\lambda=(-1)^{\Pi+k-1+\nu},\\ \nu=\sum_xd(x),\end{gathered} \tag{C.76.4} \] where \(d(x)\) is the suspended original prefix degree at each internal vertex. Cutting a block changes \(\Pi\) by the tensor-cut exponent \(\sum_{i<j}|r_i||l_j|\). The additional vertex changes the rest of the exponent by \(1+d(x)\). Exactly as in Theorem C.75.1.1, the resulting cut coefficient is the ordinary order-cochain insertion sign. On a unary term the permutation sign restores the original factor order and the prefix-degree change counts the later vertices; with the preceding block count their total is \(k-1\). Thus the entire leading source block is the finite augmented grid-order cochain complex tensored with the original factor-letter complex equipped with minus its unary differential, followed by the even shift \([-2]\). This identifies the full unary complex, rather than only its graded letters.

If some \(p_i\geq2\), choose the atom with coordinate one in that position and zero elsewhere. Joining a proper vertex with that atom never reaches the top. The identity and constant-atom order maps are both below this closure. The explicit prism of Theorem C.75.1.1 therefore contracts the proper grid's augmented complex, with the full original unary terms after the displayed rescaling. The target's corresponding leading tensor block is contracted by the first-boundary contraction in that factor, with the preceding factor tensor signs. Both blocks are acyclic.

It remains to examine profiles with every \(p_i\) zero or one. Ignore only the inactive grid coordinates in this calculation; their actual coefficient object labels are still retained in the category. If \(s\) coordinates are active, the proper grid is the poset \(\mathcal P_s\) of nonempty proper subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,s\}\). Its augmented cochain complex has one-dimensional cohomology in degree \(s-2\), and no other cohomology. The following finite induction proves this fact.

For \(s=1\) the poset is empty and its augmented chain complex is the coefficient field in degree minus one. For \(s\geq2\), remove the coatom \(b=\{1,\ldots,s-1\}\). The remaining poset contracts by adjoining the atom \(\{s\}\): its join can be the top only at the removed coatom. This is again the explicit comparable-order-map prism of C.75.1. The relative augmented chains of the full poset modulo this contracted subcomplex consist exactly of \([\sigma|b]\), where \(\sigma\) is an augmented chain in \(\mathcal P_{s-1}\), including its empty chain. The boundary deleting \(b\) lies in the removed subcomplex, and the other boundary terms are \([\partial\sigma|b]\). Thus relative homology is that of \(\mathcal P_{s-1}\) one degree higher. A standard shifted chain convention inserts the degree sign; the displayed relative boundary formula specifies it without ambiguity. Quotienting by an acyclic subcomplex preserves homology: lift a quotient cycle, correct its boundary in the acyclic subcomplex, and use the same primitive argument for boundaries. This direct argument proves the induction. Dualizing the finite chain spaces proves the stated cohomology.

The leading projection is its orientation functional on maximal chains. Such a chain is a permutation \(\sigma\) of the \(s\) active factors, added one at a time. Its two Koszul exponents, from suspended block order and unsuspended tensor order, together with the prefix rescaling give \[ \begin{gathered}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\Theta,\\ \Theta=(-1)^\eta,\\ \eta=s-1\\ \quad+\sum_i(s-i)(|a_i|-1).\end{gathered} \tag{C.76.5} \] To verify this sign, interchange two adjacent added factors. The two Koszul exponents change by \(|a|+|b|+1\) modulo two, and the prefix sum changes by \(|a|+|b|\). Their total changes by one. For the identity order the overall sign is the displayed \(\Theta\), proving the formula for every permutation. Rescale the target by \(\Theta\). Its unary sign at factor \(i\) is the original unsuspended tensor sign plus \(s-i\), which equals the top source sign \((-1)^{s-1}d_{\rm orig}\) at that position. The functional therefore has the full unary compatibility as well.

This signed maximal-chain functional kills a cochain boundary: the two refinements at a missing maximal-chain vertex differ by an adjacent transposition and cancel. It takes value one on the identity-order top cochain. Since the cohomology of the finite poset complex is one-dimensional in precisely that degree, the functional is a quasi-isomorphism to that line. Its finite split kernel contraction tensors with the original full letter complex. This proves the leading projection's quasi-isomorphism also in these profiles. The all-zero profile is the actual coefficient identity, handled separately.

For each ordered partition, the exact identity on generators is \[ \begin{gathered}(\bigotimes_j\rho_{I_j})\kappa_\pi\\ \qquad=\rho_m.\end{gathered} \tag{C.76.6} \] With the leading differentials, the target tensor of group projections is a quasi-isomorphism by the preceding arbitrary-grid argument and the split tensor contractions of C.30.1. The displayed equation consequently proves the leading quasi-isomorphism of \(\kappa_\pi\). Its leading mapping kernel is therefore acyclic, with full unary terms retained. The actual quasi-isomorphisms will follow from the simultaneous perturbed kernel contraction below; they are not assumed in this leading step.

We now arrange one contraction for all cuts. On a free cobar word, \(P_C\) kills it unless every generator's support lies wholly in one \(C\)-block. On the survivors it stably sorts those generators by their ordered block, with the Koszul sign of that permutation. Applying two ordered sorts kills precisely the generators crossing either cut set and then gives the unique stable sort for the common finer blocks. Each pair that needs interchanging is interchanged once; the product of its degree signs is therefore the same in either order. This proves \(P_CP_D=P_{C\cup D}\), including coefficient balancing. The same single-support generator test proves exact successive \(\kappa\) regrouping on generators; the dg tensor products extend it to all words.

The elementary commuting chain idempotents split each leading original profile into their finite joint sectors \[ \begin{gathered}E_J=\prod_{c\in J}(1-P_c)\\ \qquad\cdot\prod_{c\notin J}P_c.\end{gathered} \tag{C.76.7} \] They are orthogonal, sum to the identity and commute with \(D_0\). Their nonempty \(J\) sectors sum to the kernel of the finest projection, which is the actual graded kernel of \(\rho_m\). Any such sector is a chain direct summand of some acyclic \(\ker P_c\), and hence is acyclic: project a primitive in that kernel by \(E_J\). Choose a coefficient-linear normalized contraction separately on every such full unary sector and original profile, by C.30.1. Their sum \(H_0\) commutes with every \(P_c\) and preserves the original counts.

The remaining binary, scalar-binary and scalar-unary terms strictly lower total original count. They commute with every \(P_c\), because both the full differential and \(D_0\) commute with those projections. They preserve each actual kernel. The finite perturbation \(H=H_0(1+\delta H_0)^{-1}\) consequently contracts the full kernel, is normalized, and still commutes with all cut projections. Each \(\ker\kappa_\pi=\ker P_\pi\) is contained in \(\ker\rho_m\), so restriction gives its contraction as well. Extend by the finest kernel projector to obtain the full \(\rho_m\) SDR with its actual normal-order chain section. Every value is finite in original total count. Together with the already proved graded surjectivity, these actual kernel contractions prove all the asserted full quasi-isomorphisms.

Finally the entire normalized factor bar functors preserve nonempty bar outputs before the actual coefficient relations are imposed. The same support test therefore gives strict naturality of all projection and regrouping maps, including coefficient-valued higher outputs. Coefficient identities give \(m=0\); \(T_1=Q^{\mathrm u}(A_1)\) gives \(m=1\). Zero-identity objects are handled as in Theorem C.72.1.1. For finite additive envelopes use the elementary matrix-unit balanced-tensor calculation in the proof of Theorem C.38.1.1: it identifies every composable matrix word with its outer rectangular matrix entry, and cuts and merges agree entry by entry. That calculation is independent of the positivity assertions later in that theorem. It applies to the present unit relations and coefficient-linear contractions as well. No native nonidentity arrow is identified with a formal identity merely because its image happens to be a unit. This proves all assertions. \(\square\)

C.76.2. Full shuffle spans and exact regrouping squares

For the same ordered partition set \(A_{I_j}=\bigotimes_{i\in I_j}A_i\). Let \(\zeta_m:T_m\to Q^{\mathrm u}(\bigotimes_iA_i)\) be the full multishuffle. Applying the group shuffles inside the original tensor bar and then cobar gives \[ \begin{gathered}L_\pi:T_m\\ \quad\longrightarrow T(A_{I_1},\ldots,A_{I_r}).\end{gathered} \tag{C.76.8} \]

Theorem C.76.2.1 (one common input for all ordered tensor regroupings). These are strict unital dg mapping quasi-isomorphisms. They satisfy the exact entire equations \[ \begin{gathered}\epsilon_{\otimes_iA_i}\zeta_m\\ \quad=(\bigotimes_i\epsilon_{A_i})\rho_m,\\ \rho_rL_\pi\\ \quad=(\bigotimes_j\zeta_{I_j})\kappa_\pi,\\ \zeta_rL_\pi=\zeta_m.\end{gathered} \tag{C.76.9} \] Successive group-shuffle regroupings are exactly the direct group shuffle. The shuffle and group-shuffle maps are strictly natural for strict dg factor maps. All zero- and one-factor maps are the coefficient and factor identities already specified.

Proof. The full multishuffle is the sum over all interleavings of the ordered factor words, with their suspended Koszul signs. Cutting such an interleaving is exactly cutting each original factor word and shuffling the two parts. Binary bar products of adjacent distinct-factor letters cancel in pairs by graded commutation in the tensor category. Unary and same-factor binary terms give the factor differential. These are the full chain and coalgebra calculations of Section C.39.3 and Theorem C.75.2.1, with every ordinary unit output retained. A coefficient input becomes a global coefficient letter in each affected group. The higher degenerate generators therefore vanish in the normalized target; single coefficient generators become their actual coefficients. This proves that both \(\zeta_m\) and \(L_\pi\) descend as strict unital dg functors.

The first counit equation is checked on a single pure letter and on every higher generator exactly as in Theorem C.75.2.1, then on products. By Theorem C.76.1.1, the actual factor counits of Theorem C.72.1.1 and split tensor contractions, its right-hand composite is a quasi-isomorphism. Its left-hand counit is also one. Hence \(\zeta_m\) is a quasi-isomorphism.

For the second equation test a free generator's support among the groups. If it meets more than one group, both sides project to zero. If it meets one group, both sides are that group's entire shuffle, in its designated tensor slot. Single coefficients also agree. This proves the equation on all products with the graded tensor signs. Since \(\rho_r\), every \(\zeta_{I_j}\) and \(\kappa_\pi\) are quasi-isomorphisms, the equation proves that \(L_\pi\) is one too.

For the last equation and successive regrouping, an interleaving of interleavings has a unique flat interleaving. Conversely a flat ordered interleaving uniquely determines all its grouped interleavings by reading the original factor labels. Their signs multiply to the sign of the same permutation of the original suspended letters. Thus every full bar word, not only its one-letter projection, agrees exactly. Cobar and the unit quotients preserve that equality. On zero or one factors the formulas are the specified identities. Strict dg factor maps preserve these original letters, products and coefficients, proving the claimed naturality. A tensor product of general original \(A_\infty\) functors has not been introduced in this argument. \(\square\)

C.76.3. Solved Boolean and overlapping-cut calculations

Exercise C.76.3.1 (a Boolean cut class must be retained; advanced). Let each \(A_i=k1\oplus ka_i\), for \(i=1,2,3\), be the unital dg algebra with \(|a_i|=1\), \(a_i^2=0\), and zero differential. In the part of \(T_3\) containing exactly one original \(a_i\) in each factor, compute the complete cut complex and its cohomology. Describe its projection to \(Q(A_1)\otimes Q(A_2)\otimes Q(A_3)\).

Solution. For a nonempty subset \(S\subseteq\{1,2,3\}\), let \(x_S\) be the single cobar generator with letter \(sa_i\) in factor \(i\in S\) and empty word otherwise. Every suspended letter has degree zero, so every \(x_S\) has degree one. At this original profile, each source cobar word is an ordered partition of the three factor labels. There is one one-block word, six two-block words and six three-block words. Their complex is

\[ k^1\longrightarrow k^6\longrightarrow k^6, \tag{C.76.10} \]

in degrees one, two and three. The actual differential here is entirely its cut differential: the original unary maps are zero, and two original letters never occur in the same factor. For example, with \(z=x_{\{1,2,3\}}\),

\[ \begin{gathered}Dz\\ \quad=-\sum_{S\in\mathcal P_3}x_Sx_{S^c}.\end{gathered} \tag{C.76.11} \]

The proper Boolean poset has singleton and two-element-subset vertices; the six strict inclusion edges form a hexagon. Its augmented incidence map has rank one at the first step. A function on its six vertices has zero edge differences exactly when it is constant, since the hexagon is connected. Thus the next incidence map has rank five. It follows that the displayed source complex has zero cohomology in degrees one and two and one-dimensional cohomology in degree three.

Write \(X=x_{\{1\}}\), \(Y=x_{\{2\}}\), \(Z=x_{\{3\}}\). The projection kills every word with a mixed generator. On the maximal word \(W_\sigma=X_{\sigma(1)}X_{\sigma(2)}X_{\sigma(3)}\) it gives

\[ \begin{gathered}\rho_3(W_\sigma)=\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\\ \qquad\cdot\bigl(x_{a_1}\otimes x_{a_2}\\ \qquad\otimes x_{a_3}\bigr).\end{gathered} \tag{C.76.12} \]

The sign is the permutation of three odd, unsuspended pure generators. The signed maximal-chain functional is therefore the actual projection onto this one surviving class. In particular \(XYZ\) is not a boundary: its actual tensor counit image is \(a_1\otimes a_2\otimes a_3\ne0\) in a target with zero differential. Its kernel is contracted; the surviving tensor class is retained. \(\square\)

Exercise C.76.3.2 (one primitive equation does not fix every cut value; advanced). In the same three-factor example take \(v=ZXY\). Let \(P_1\) correspond to \(1|23\) and \(P_2\) to \(12|3\). Compute both projections and their two composites. Find a primitive in \(\ker\rho_3\) for \(v-XYZ\) with zero \(P_2\)-value, and exhibit a second kernel primitive whose \(P_2\)-value is nonzero.

Solution. Stable graded sorting gives

\[ \begin{gathered}P_1(ZXY)=-XZY,\\ P_2(ZXY)=XYZ,\\ P_1P_2(ZXY)=XYZ,\\ P_2P_1(ZXY)=XYZ.\end{gathered} \tag{C.76.13} \]

The first projection interchanges two odd generators; the second moves \(Z\) across two of them. Set \(x_{13}=x_{\{1,3\}}\) and \(x_{23}=x_{\{2,3\}}\). The mixed cut formulas give \(Dx_{13}=-XZ-ZX\) and \(Dx_{23}=-YZ-ZY\). Consequently

\[ \begin{gathered}K=-x_{13}Y-Xx_{23},\\ DK=ZXY-XYZ,\\ \rho_3K=0,\quad P_2K=0.\end{gathered} \tag{C.76.14} \]

For the derivative, the two terms in \(XZY\) cancel by the degree-one product sign. Each term of \(K\) has a generator crossing the \(12|3\) cut, so its \(P_2\)-projection is zero. This is the required projected primitive equation.

In the entire source complex the degree-two cochain \(s=XY+YX\) is closed, lies in \(\ker\rho_3\), and is nonzero as an actual free-algebra vector. It is itself the boundary of \(-x_{\{1,2\}}\). It has a different original profile from \(K\), which is allowed when choosing an arbitrary primitive in the whole complex. Adding it gives

\[ \begin{gathered}D(K+s)\\ \quad=ZXY-XYZ,\\ \rho_3(K+s)=0,\\ P_2(K+s)=s\ne0.\end{gathered} \tag{C.76.15} \]

Thus the primitive equation and even its zero whole-tensor projection do not force the required intermediate cut value. The contraction of Theorem C.76.1.1 commutes with \(P_2\), so on \(v-XYZ\in\ker P_2\) it chooses a primitive with exactly zero \(P_2\)-value. Its simultaneous cut property is additional structure, not a conclusion from an unconstrained primitive. \(\square\)

Theorem C.76.1.1 gives every finite-factor projection with a simultaneous ordered-cut contraction; Theorem C.76.2.1 gives exact full multishuffle and regrouping squares. Exercises C.76.3.1–C.76.3.2 retain the Boolean tensor class and compute a primitive with its required intermediate cut value. Editable SVG source.

C.77. Entire evaluation and coherent native operator cubes

An exact whole evaluation identity is preserved when lifted operators and their comparison cubes are composed. It supplies one compatible boundary for each sequential native composition, whose relative kernel filler retains every formal-unit degeneracy and higher source component.

C.77.1. The exact projected-evaluation condition is preserved by composition

For a dg category \(A\), write \(Q_A=Q^{\mathrm u}(A)\), with \(\epsilon_A\) and \(\iota_A\) as in Theorem C.72.2.1. Let \(K\) be a full conilpotent relative parameter coalgebra with its original object labels. Let \(J=I^{\otimes d}\) be the actual cube coalgebra of Theorem C.74.2.1, including all cells and ordinary faces. Parameters are normalized at their coefficient units; cube variables have their stated counit.

Suppose \(\Phi:K\to B_{\rm full}\operatorname{Fun}_\infty(A,B)\) is an entire native parameter map. Write \(\mathcal U_{A,B}=\operatorname{Fun}_\infty(Q_A,Q_B)\). A cube of its operator lifts is a chain coalgebra map \[ \begin{gathered}\widehat\Phi:K\otimes J\\ \quad\longrightarrow B_{\rm full}\mathcal U_{A,B}.\end{gathered} \tag{C.77.1} \] whose object values are the strict dg operators \(QF\). Its positive Taylor map vanishes on the coefficient coaugmentation of \(K\), even when the cube variable is nonempty. Thus the object values are fixed throughout the cube. Call such a lift admissible if its entire bar restriction along \(\iota_A\) is \[ \begin{gathered}B(r_{A,B})\widehat\Phi\\ \quad=B((\iota_B)_*)\Phi\\ \qquad\cdot(1_K\otimes\epsilon_J).\end{gathered} \tag{C.77.2} \] Here \((\iota_B)_*\) includes every higher postcomposition operation of Theorem C.69.2.1. Its linear component alone is not substituted for that bar map.

Theorem C.77.1.1 (entire projected evaluation and its closure). Admissibility is equivalent to the following exact equation on all source and parameter words: \[ \begin{gathered}\widehat E=\operatorname{ev}_{Q_A,Q_B}\\ \qquad\circ(\widehat\Phi\otimes B\iota_A),\\ E=\operatorname{ev}_{A,B}(\Phi\otimes1)\\ \qquad\circ(1_K\otimes\epsilon_J\otimes1),\\ \widehat E=B\iota_B\,E.\end{gathered} \tag{C.77.3} \] All sides retain ordinary identity outputs and source-unary terms. Horizontal composition of any admissible lifted cubes is admissible for the corresponding entire native composite, with tensor cube coordinates and the actual Koszul interchange. Restrictions to ordinary cube faces and full supplied parameter subcoalgebras remain admissible.

Proof. Precomposition by an entire functor is a strict dg functor on full Nat categories. The exact evaluation identity of Theorem C.69.2.1 therefore identifies evaluation of the left restriction map with evaluation of \(\widehat\Phi\) on \(B\iota_A\). The same identity identifies evaluation after entire postcomposition by \(\iota_B\) with \(B\iota_B\) after original evaluation. Substituting the displayed admissibility equation gives the required evaluation equation.

Conversely, project the evaluation equation to a single target mapping letter and evaluate on every original \(A\)-word, including the empty word at each object. This recovers every full Nat Taylor component of the one-parameter-letter projections on the two proposed bar maps. A cofree target bar map is determined by these projections and its coefficient map, as proved in Theorem C.69.2.1. Their coefficient maps are already the same fixed object maps. Hence their entire bar maps are equal, which is precisely admissibility.

For closure let \(\widehat\Psi\) be an admissible cube from \(B\) to a third dg category \(C\), with native map \(\Psi\). On their full parameter and cube tensor product form the entire horizontal map \(M_Q(\widehat\Psi\otimes\widehat\Phi)\), moving the original homogeneous factors through the required tensor permutation. Evaluate it on \(B\iota_A\). By the exact nested evaluation identity this is first the entire inner evaluation and then the entire outer evaluation. Inner admissibility says its full output is exactly \(B\iota_B\) of the native inner output, with the inner cube counit. It is therefore in the precise input of outer admissibility, including every ordinary unit and every higher output word. Outer admissibility now makes the whole result \(B\iota_C\) of the nested native evaluations, with both cube counits. Applying the nested identity again gives the native horizontal composite. This is the required evaluation equation for that composite, so the equivalence just proved gives its admissibility. Its object types agree exactly because \(QG\,QF=Q(GF)\), by Theorem C.72.2.1.

This argument applies to arbitrary higher kernel corrections that still obey the entire admissibility equation. It does not assume that a bare postcomposition projection is horizontally multiplicative on unrelated Nat cochains. The whole inner output lying in \(B\iota_B\)'s image is the step that permits the outer evaluation equation to be used.

For finiteness, the cubical coalgebra is finite, although its vertices are group-like. The positive twist is zero on the coefficient part of \(K\). Consequently every nonzero positive output piece consumes positive original parameter rank; there are at most that many pieces. For each fixed number of pieces, the iterated cube diagonal is a finite sum. Full evaluation has the finite marked bound of C69 on every original source word. Thus the reconstructed maps and all equations are actual finite sums, without assuming that the cube itself is conilpotent. Composing with a face or a supplied parameter subcoalgebra simply restricts these same equations. This proves every assertion. \(\square\)

C.77.2. One coherent family for every sequential native composition

Fix dg categories \(A_0,\ldots,A_n\) and let \(\mathcal O_i=\operatorname{Fun}_\infty(A_{i-1},A_i)\), with its full normalized Nat dg category. The native sequential composition is the entire associative map \(M\) of Theorem C.69.2.1. The common parameter category is \(T_n=T(\mathcal O_n,\ldots,\mathcal O_1)\), with all original operator labels and the actual normalized unit relations of C74.

Theorem C.77.2.1 (strictly unital coherent operator-model cubes). The operator maps \(\mathcal Q\) of Theorem C.73.2.1 extend to a family \(W_n\) of admissible cubes of dimension \(n-1\), defined on the entire common parameter coalgebra of \(T_n\). Their fixed object value is \(Q(F_n\cdots F_1)\). They have the following ordinary faces. At coordinate zero, the chain of native operators splits there and the face is the entire horizontal composition of the two smaller cubes. At coordinate one, the two adjacent native slots merge by their full native \(M\), and the face is the smaller cube pulled back along that full merge map. The coordinates retain their original seam labels.

The whole family can retain any previously supplied compatible free-generator faces and their full cubes. Choose it once before full native parameter restrictions. Its pullbacks then agree exactly on all shared native full faces and include every original higher cell. Formal identity-functor slots have the normalized degeneracies described below; identity-valued nonidentity native arrows retain their own labels. The empty sequential chain has its actual identity operator and no positive cube coordinate.

Proof. At \(n=1\), take the entire \(\mathcal Q\) of C73. Its exact restriction is the admissibility equation by Theorem C.73.2.1. Suppose all smaller cubes have been chosen simultaneously. On the boundary of \(I^{n-1}\) prescribe the faces in the statement. Splitting a zero coordinate uses the two smaller cubes, with their parameter and cube factors regrouped by the actual tensor coalgebra interchange. Merging a one coordinate uses the full native composition coalgebra map, followed by the previously chosen smaller cube. Both descend through the actual parameter-unit relations, by C69 and Theorem C.74.1.1.

These are compatible whole boundary values. On an intersection of two zero faces, both expressions are the entire three-level horizontal composition of the same smaller cubes; exact associativity of \(M_Q\) in C69 makes them equal. On two one faces, both expressions are the same smaller cube pulled back along the two full native merges. If the merges are disjoint they commute under tensor interchange; if adjacent they agree by entire native associativity. On a zero and a distinct one face, the native merge occurs inside one of the two split pieces. Both orders give that same smaller cube's prescribed face, composed with the other piece. Tensor-factor permutations move the same original homogeneous elements through the same permutation in every case, so the Koszul signs agree. All codimension-two intersections therefore agree; every higher face intersection is their literal iterated restriction.

Every boundary face is admissible by Theorem C.77.1.1 and the induction. Its exact projected map is the one \((\iota_{A_n})_*\) of the entire native \(n\)-fold composition, independent of the cube coordinates. The operator object is likewise independent of its parenthesization, since the strict Q-models compose exactly. Use the actual restriction projection of Theorem C.73.1.1 on that fixed labelled object family. It is a graded-surjective mapping quasi-isomorphism with an actual contracted kernel. The relative cube extension of Theorem C.74.2.1 therefore fills precisely this supplied boundary, with precisely this entire projected map. Its domain \(T_n\) retains the full source-unary generator differential and all constants, as required by that theorem. The filler is consequently admissible. No absolute Nat acyclicity has been used.

Here are the formal-unit degeneracies and their compatibility. Define \(\mu:I\otimes I\to I\) by the minimum of the two vertices and by \[ \begin{gathered}\mu(e\otimes v_1)=e,\\ \mu(v_1\otimes e)=e,\\ \mu(e\otimes v_0)=0,\\ \mu(v_0\otimes e)=0,\\ \mu(e\otimes e)=0.\end{gathered} \tag{C.77.4} \] It is a dg coalgebra map. On a vertex this follows from its group-like diagonal. On an edge with other vertex \(v_1\), its two diagonal terms are exactly \(e\otimes v_1+v_0\otimes e\) after applying \(\mu\) to both factors. With other vertex \(v_0\), every term has a zero edge factor. On \(e\otimes e\), both middle diagonal terms have a factor of this latter kind, and the two extreme terms also give zero. This proves the coalgebra equation on all nine basis elements. The chain equation on two edges is \(e-0-e+0=0\); the edge-vertex equations are the corresponding vertex differences. Its unit is \(v_1\) and its absorbing vertex is \(v_0\).

It is associative: at vertices this is associativity of minimum. With one edge, the result is that edge exactly when all other vertices are \(v_1\); otherwise it is zero. With at least two edges both parenthesizations are zero. This covers every homogeneous triple and all successive products.

When an interior operator slot is the formal identity functor with only its coefficient parameters, delete that slot and pull back the smaller cube by \(\mu\) on its two adjacent seam coordinates. At an endpoint identity slot delete its one adjacent coordinate by the interval counit. These prescriptions agree with the already assigned zero and one faces: \(\mu(v_0,-)\) is the constant zero vertex, while \(\mu(v_1,-)\) is the identity coordinate. This is exactly the split versus native-merge face rule. Several identity deletions agree by associativity of \(\mu\), its counit equation and strict native/Q identity composition. They also agree on ordinary parameter-unit faces by normalized unitality of C69 and C73. No interval reversal is used.

The no-letter formal-unit parameter faces are actual differential-stable free-generator faces of \(T_n\), by Theorem C.74.1.1. The preceding compatible smaller cubes prescribe their entire cubical values. Apply the relative clause of C74's extension to retain them exactly along with any other compatible assigned free-generator-face cubes. An already assigned family must have these same entire boundaries; no extension assertion is made for an arbitrary inconsistent face list. This completes the induction in \(n\).

Finally each actual native string or joint parameter diagram enters by its supplied full parameter coalgebra map to the original \(\mathcal O_i\) categories. Pull back the whole chosen \(W_n\) along those maps and the actual cube faces. Two such pullbacks to the same full native face are the same literal map, because the original native maps already agree there and the family was chosen globally first. All ordinary unit outputs, higher native transformations, original composite labels and nonminimal source-unary terms are therefore retained. This is a restriction of the entire supplied native diagram, not its reconstruction from unrelated edge classes. A nonrectangular compatible joint domain uses its actual whole index coalgebra as in C64; this construction clips no shuffle and inserts no missing intermediate object. This proves the claimed operator-model comparison family. \(\square\)

C.77.3. Solved cube calculations

Exercise C.77.3.1 (a whole boundary needs its interior value; advanced). Let \(E=k1\oplus kx\oplus ky\), with \(|x|=-1\), \(|y|=-2\), \(dy=x\), \(dx=0\), and square-zero ideal \((x,y)\). The quotient \(p:E\to k\) kills that ideal. For the free unital dg algebra on a degree-zero closed generator \(a\), prescribe a relative square with zero vertex values, value \(x\) on the bottom edge \(e\otimes v_0\), and zero on its other three edges. Fill it over the zero quotient image and compute what happens if its top cell is omitted.

Solution. A degree-zero cochain \(\phi:I^2\to E\) takes the top cell to degree minus two. The entire tensor differential is \[ \begin{gathered}d(e\otimes e)\\ \quad=v_1\otimes e-v_0\otimes e\\ \qquad-e\otimes v_1+e\otimes v_0.\end{gathered} \tag{C.77.5} \] The given boundary consequently has value \(x\) on that derivative. Set \(\phi(e\otimes e)=y\). Then its Hom differential on the top cell is \(dy-\phi(d(e\otimes e))=x-x=0\). The edge and vertex equations hold because \(dx=0\). All its values are in \(\ker p\), so its quotient is the required constant zero. Sending \(a\) to this closed convolution cochain and extending by products gives the whole strict dg map. If the top value is set to zero, the differential instead has value \(-x\ne0\) on that cell. The boundary itself has not changed; its needed interior primitive is the substantive filler. \(\square\)

Exercise C.77.3.2 (an identity slot can have a nonconstant cubical degeneracy; advanced). Let \(E=k1\oplus k\alpha\oplus k\beta\), with \(|\alpha|=0\), \(|\beta|=-1\), \(d\beta=\alpha\), and square-zero ideal \((\alpha,\beta)\). The interval cochain \(\psi\) has values zero at \(v_0\), \(\alpha\) at \(v_1\), and \(\beta\) at \(e\). Compute the full square \(\psi\mu\) that occurs when a middle formal identity slot is deleted.

Solution. The interval Hom differential is zero: \(d\beta-(\alpha-0)=0\). The minimum map gives only one nonzero vertex value of its square, at \(v_1\otimes v_1\), equal to \(\alpha\). Its two edges with the other coordinate \(v_1\) have value \(\beta\); its two edges with other coordinate \(v_0\) have value zero. Its top value is zero. On the top derivative in Exercise C.77.3.1 these values give \(\beta-0-\beta+0=0\), and the remaining differential equations are the same interval equation. Thus the full square is closed, as required by the coalgebra pullback.

It is not the constant zero square even though its inserted native operator is an identity: its \((v_1,v_1)\) value is the original \(\alpha\), and its two edge components are the original homotopy. The formal identity fixes the specified degeneracy, including all of these components. It does not erase an already nonconstant comparison. \(\square\)

Theorem C.77.1.1 proves the exact projected-evaluation law and closure; Theorem C.77.2.1 constructs the coherent native sequential operator cubes. Exercises C.77.3.1–C.77.3.2 compute a required square interior and a nonconstant formal-unit degeneracy. Editable SVG source.

C.78. Full tensor-unit restriction and external comparisons

The full normalized tensor-unit restriction records the entire mapping complex and has an actual finite kernel contraction. Its canonical tensor and shuffle squares lift supplied whole native external comparisons while keeping the original source differential and coefficient outputs.

C.78.1. The tensor unit records the entire mapping complex

Let \(A_1,\ldots,A_m\) be unital dg categories over the split degree-zero coefficients of Section C.30.1. Set \(K=\bigotimes_iB_{\rm full}A_i\) and \(T=T(A_1,\ldots,A_m)\). The canonical full coalgebra map \[ \eta:K\longrightarrow B_{\rm full}T, \tag{C.78.1} \] is the bar-cobar unit of Lemma C.39.4.1 followed by the actual normalized quotient of Theorem C.74.1.1. In particular this is a map between genuine full dg coalgebras. We do not declare their naive reduced unit quotients dg coalgebras: scalar differential or product outputs can give those quotients curvature.

Fix normalized uncurved unital functors \(F,G:T\to D\), with \(D\) a dg target. Their full bar maps precomposed with \(\eta\) are full multi-input functors on \(K\). Full multi-Nat cochains between them have one central target mapping value on each original tuple of input words, including the empty tuple. Their differential and vertical product are the full coalgebra/coderivation convolution formulas on \(K\). Normalize positive cochains by making them zero at any ordinary coefficient input in any factor. This normalization concerns inputs, and retains actual coefficient outputs.

Theorem C.78.1.1 (full normalized tensor-unit restriction). Restriction gives a graded-surjective dg functor on the labelled operator family, \[ \begin{gathered}r_\eta:\operatorname{Nat}_\infty(F,G)\\ \quad\longrightarrow\operatorname{Nat}_K(F\eta,G\eta).\end{gathered} \tag{C.78.2} \] It is a quasi-isomorphism on the complete mapping complexes. Its actual kernel has a normalized contraction finite on every original reduced factor-letter input. Thus the unit records full transformation classes, primitives and their whole higher coherent diagrams, not only bare values. No augmentation or positive cohomological mapping degrees are assumed.

Proof. A normalized Nat cochain on \(T\) is determined by its central Taylor values on the normalized graded source inputs. In the graded free description of C74 these are outer bar words of nonempty cobar monomials; each cobar generator is a nonempty tuple of original reduced factor words. For an original reduced tuple \(c\), the unit's one-bar-letter, one-cobar-generator component is exactly \(s(\mathsf tc)\). Its other components have several outer bar letters. This exhibits an injective graded map on the normalized input tuples: the displayed distinguished components are separate for every \(c\). Any central multi-Nat cochain therefore extends by assigning its value on those components and zero on all other positive source inputs, with the same bare value. This proves graded surjectivity, without asserting that this graded section is a chain section.

If an original input has a coefficient argument, every surviving term of its unit image contains an ordinary coefficient input in an outer bar slot. A higher cobar block containing it has already vanished by C74; a surviving one-letter coefficient block is the actual coefficient. Thus normalized Nat cochains restrict to precisely the stated normalized multi-Nat cochains. Before this normalization, restriction is a chain map and preserves the cofree composition formula because \(\eta\) is a chain coalgebra map. It consequently preserves both on the normalized spaces as well. For clarity their stability can also be deduced from the graded extension just given: if \(\psi=r_\eta\phi\), then \(d\psi=r_\eta(d\phi)\) is again normalized. The same argument applies to products. This defines the normalized dg mapping category directly from the genuine full complexes; no curved reduced-bar square-zero assertion is hidden in this step.

Count all original reduced \(A_i/S_i\) letters in a tuple and in an outer bar word of cobar monomials. Let the total be \(R\). For the leading differential retain the full projected original unary complexes, the cobar splits and the outer bar multiplication of cobar monomials. Discard native factor bar multiplications, scalar outputs and positive functor-action terms only for this leading calculation. Write \(K_0=\bigotimes_iT^c(s(A_i/S_i))\), with its projected unary differential. Then the leading source is the genuine augmented \(T_0=\Omega K_0\), and its normalized input bar is \(B_{\rm red}\Omega K_0\). The leading unit is the same graded iterated-coproduct formula as \(\eta\).

In every fixed original rank the leading unit is a quasi-isomorphism. Here is the finite argument, independent of cohomological degree bounds. Filter \(B_{\rm red}\Omega K_0\) by the number \(r_0\) of original noncoaugmented \(K_0\)-elements before they are grouped into cobar monomials and outer bars. Each such element contains positive original rank, so \(r_0\leq R\). Cobar splitting increases \(r_0\); the original unary and outer bar merge preserve it. At fixed \(r_0\geq2\), the associated quotient is the first-boundary cut complex of C.39.4. Its contraction inserts a missing outer cut after the first original \(\mathsf tc_1\), with coefficient \((-1)^{|c_1|}\), and is zero if that cut is present. Cutting then merging gives the identity. Every other merge cancels in the two orders, and the same coefficient makes the original unary terms cancel as proved in C.39.4. Thus this contracts the full quotient, including its unary complex. At \(r_0=1\), the unit is the identity on the original \(K_0\)-element. Finite elimination in its comparison cone through \(1\leq r_0\leq R\) proves acyclicity of that cone in the exact original-rank block. At rank zero the unit is the coefficient identity.

The leading unit is graded-injective, so its quotient input complex is acyclic. Choose a coefficient-linear normalized contraction \(h_Q\) on that quotient, separately in its original-rank and endpoint blocks, using C.30.1. Identify the leading restriction kernel with central Hom cochains on this quotient. The Nat convention requires its sign to be stated: for a degree-\(r\) central cochain, \[ \begin{gathered}D_0\phi=d_D\phi\\ \qquad+(-1)^r\phi b_0.\end{gathered} \tag{C.78.3} \] It is the ordinary Hom convention with source differential \(-b_0\). Consequently its kernel contraction is \[ H_0\phi=(-1)^{r+1}\phi h_Q. \tag{C.78.4} \] Indeed the two target-unary terms in \(D_0H_0+H_0D_0\) cancel, and the remaining terms are \(\phi(h_Qb_0+b_0h_Q)=\phi\). The square and side conditions follow from the normalized \(h_Q\). This retains the bare central target differential and the complete source unary, cobar and bar-merge terms; it is not a Hom calculation on cohomology.

Now restore the full mapping differential \(D_0+\delta\). A native factor bar multiplication lowers original rank; its scalar output lowers it further. Scalar unary outputs also lower it. Every nontrivial source or target functor action consumes a positive-rank piece of the original input. Even when that action's output is a coefficient it has consumed that input piece. Ordinary unit-input terms have already canceled in the normalized complex; they do not supply a rank-zero positive action. Hence \(\delta\phi\) on rank \(R\) uses \(\phi\) only on smaller ranks. The restriction kernel is stable under the full differential and under the leading differential. On that same actual kernel the finite perturbation \[ \begin{gathered}H\\ \quad=H_0(1+\delta H_0)^{-1}.\end{gathered} \tag{C.78.5} \] therefore terminates word by word. Lemma C.35.1.1 gives \(DH+HD=1\), \(H^2=0\). The kernel is contracted, and the graded-surjective chain restriction is consequently a quasi-isomorphism. Its full dg composition property was already proved. This proves the entire assertion. \(\square\)

C.78.2. The actual full tensor squares and lifted native comparisons

For the same family write \(\rho_A:T(A_i)\to\bigotimes_iQ_{A_i}\) and \(\zeta_A:T(A_i)\to Q_{\otimes_iA_i}\) for C76's actual maps. Let \(\operatorname{sh}_A\) denote the full factor-bar shuffle. All unit maps here are their actual entire bar-cobar units followed by the indicated normalized quotients.

Theorem C.78.2.1 (canonical multi-input model and actual comparison lifting). The exact whole coalgebra identities are \[ \begin{gathered}B\rho_A\,\eta_A\\ \quad=\operatorname{sh}_{Q_A}\\ \qquad\circ(\bigotimes_iB\iota_{A_i}),\\ B\zeta_A\,\eta_A\\ \quad=B\iota_{\otimes_iA_i}\operatorname{sh}_A.\end{gathered} \tag{C.78.6} \] For normalized unital factor functors \(F_i:A_i\to B_i\), the actual strict dg common-input map \(T(F_i)\) of C74 satisfies \[ \begin{gathered}\rho_BT(F_i)\\ \quad=(\bigotimes_iQF_i)\rho_A.\end{gathered} \tag{C.78.7} \] and \[ \begin{gathered}B(\zeta_BT(F_i))\eta_A\\ \quad=B\iota_{\otimes_iB_i}\\ \qquad\circ\operatorname{sh}_B\\ \qquad\circ(\bigotimes_iBF_i).\end{gathered} \tag{C.78.8} \] These equations define a full multi-input comparison without introducing a tensor product of general original \(A_\infty\) functors.

If an actual native external operator \(F_{\rm ext}\) and its supplied full comparison with the right multi-input expression are given, that comparison, its inverses and its higher covariance lift through the specific contracted mapping kernel of Theorem C.78.1.1. Compatible prescribed free-generator faces and their full projection data can be retained.

Proof. Project the first proposed unit identity to one target bar letter. A reduced input tuple supported in one factor maps on each side to its corresponding one normalized cobar block in that factor. If several factor words are nonempty, the left projection is zero by the generator rule for \(\rho_A\). On the right, each nonempty factor has at least one output letter before the full shuffle, so the total output has at least two letters and also has zero one-letter projection. Coefficient terms agree by their actual unit relations. Both sides are coalgebra maps. Cofree uniqueness therefore proves the whole first identity, with every higher output and tensor-cut sign.

The second is naturality of the explicit coalgebra unit under the full shuffle coalgebra map, followed by the two actual quotient maps. The unit formula sums the same consecutive coproduct pieces on both sides; cuts of a shuffle are the shuffled factor cuts, as proved in C.75.2 and C.76.2. This gives the whole equation, including ordinary unit outputs.

The middle projection equation is the entire factor naturality of C.76.1. For the last equation, the unit's naturality for \(\bigotimes_iBF_i\) gives \(B(T(F_i))\eta_A=\eta_B(\bigotimes_iBF_i)\). Compose with \(B\zeta_B\) and use the second unit identity. This proves all the stated equations on full bars, not just on generators after forgetting the source-ending maps.

To spell out the native comparison types, the supplied external operator gives a strict dg common-input model \(L=QF_{\rm ext}\,\zeta_A:T(A_i)\to Q_{\otimes_iB_i}\). The independent factor map gives \(P=\zeta_BT(F_i)\) with that same source and target. Their exact restrictions by the two identities are respectively \(B\iota_{\otimes_iB_i}\,BF_{\rm ext}\operatorname{sh}_A\) and \(B\iota_{\otimes_iB_i}\operatorname{sh}_B(\bigotimes_iBF_i)\). Apply full postcomposition by \(\iota_{\otimes_iB_i}\) to the supplied whole native comparison between the original two multi-input maps. It becomes an actual full multi-Nat comparison between \(L\eta_A\) and \(P\eta_A\), including all its higher parameter components.

For a closed homogeneous comparison \(\psi\), choose a graded preimage \(\phi_0\) under Theorem C.78.1.1's restriction. Its defect \(D\phi_0\) is a closed element of the actual restriction kernel. The correction \(\phi=\phi_0-H(D\phi_0)\) has the prescribed restriction and is closed. The bare component is unchanged because the unit is the identity there and the kernel has zero bare component. If the native comparison has pointwise homotopy-equivalence components, these remain its actual bare equivalences. Its full inverse classes and primitives are retained because restriction is a dg mapping quasi-isomorphism. For a whole free coherent parameter diagram use this same fixed-object dg projection in the relative free-generator induction of Theorem C.46.2.1. It lifts the entire diagram, rather than choosing unrelated closed edges. The relative clause retains the already assigned compatible generator faces and their full projection data. Cube boundaries use Theorem C.74.2.1 with this actual kernel.

This construction uses the given native external comparison; it does not infer it from a matching cohomology ring or unrelated endpoint equivalences. It supplies a specific full common-input lift of that comparison. Its simultaneous assembly with the actual native positive common graphs and the prescribed graft/field comparison remains a separate obligation. \(\square\)

C.78.3. Solved full-bar and mapping-sign calculations

Exercise C.78.3.1 (the Nat contraction has the shifted Hom sign; advanced). Take \(A=k1\oplus ka\), \(|a|=0\), \(da=a^2=0\), and \(T=Q^{\mathrm u}(A)\). Let \(F=G:T\to k\) be its augmentation. Write \(x=\mathsf t(sa)\), \(h=\mathsf t(sa|sa)\). At original rank two consider source bar inputs \(u=s h\), \(v=s(x^2)\), \(w=sx|sx\). Find the restriction kernel differential and the primitive of the cochain \(g(u)=-1\), \(g(w)=1\), \(g(v)=0\). Check the sign in Theorem C.78.1.1.

Solution. Here \(|x|=0\), \(|h|=-1\), and \(Dh=x^2\). The actual bar differential and unit values are

\[ \begin{gathered}b(u)=v,\quad b(w)=-v,\\ b(v)=0,\\ \eta(sa|sa)=u+w.\end{gathered} \tag{C.78.9} \]

The input quotient has \(u=-w\), so its contraction can be chosen as \(h_Q(v)=-w\), \(h_Q(w)=0\). A central scalar cochain \(f\) with \(f(v)=1\) and all other values zero has degree one, since \(|v|=-1\). The Nat sign gives \(Df=-f b=g\), of degree two. In particular \(g\eta=0\), and the full augmentation actions are zero on all positive inputs. No higher original-rank components occur in this example. The actual restriction-kernel homotopy satisfies

\[ \begin{gathered}(Hg)(v)\\ \quad=(-1)^3g(-w)=1,\\ Hg=f.\end{gathered} \tag{C.78.10} \]

Thus \(D(Hg)=g\). Using instead the unshifted sign \((-1)^{|g|}\) with this same \(h_Q\) gives \(-f\) and differentiates to \(-g\), not \(g\). This verifies the coefficient \((-1)^{r+1}\) required by the full Nat convention. \(\square\)

Exercise C.78.3.2 (mixed and ordinary-unit outputs of the full tensor unit; advanced). Let \(a,b\) be closed degree-zero mappings in the two factors and write \(X=\mathsf t(sa\otimes1)\), \(Y=\mathsf t(1\otimes sb)\), \(z=\mathsf t(sa\otimes sb)\). Compute \(\eta(sa\otimes sb)\), its full \(B\rho\)-image and its full shuffle comparison. Then specialize \(a\) to the actual coefficient unit of its factor.

Solution. Both original suspended letters have degree minus one. The full tensor coproduct has the two proper cut orientations with opposite signs. The canonical unit is consequently

\[ \begin{gathered}\eta(sa\otimes sb)=sz\\ \qquad+sX|sY-sY|sX.\end{gathered} \tag{C.78.11} \]

The first projection kills the mixed generator \(z\) and keeps the other two terms, exactly the shuffle of \(s x_a\) and \(s x_b\) in their designated tensor slots. This is the first entire unit square, including its two distinct outer-bar words.

For the second square put \(u=a\otimes1\), \(v=1\otimes b\). Its one-output part is \(s\mathsf t(su|sv)-s\mathsf t(sv|su)\); its two-output part is \(s x_u|s x_v-s x_v|s x_u\). Together these are exactly \(B\iota_{A\otimes B}\) of the original full shuffle \(su|sv-sv|su\). Taking only one of these output lengths would lose the entire comparison equation.

If \(a=1\), the normalized relations give \(X=1\), \(z=0\), and kill both higher cobar blocks containing the global unit. The full unit image is still

\[ s1|sY-sY|s1. \tag{C.78.12} \]

These are ordinary coefficient output letters of the full bar. They are retained in the coalgebra identity. A normalized positive Nat cochain evaluates this image to zero because each word contains a unit input; that explains the cochain normalization without deleting either full-bar output word. The full identity and its normalized evaluation are different operations. \(\square\)

Theorem C.78.1.1 gives the full tensor-unit mapping restriction; Theorem C.78.2.1 gives canonical entire tensor squares and the lift of supplied native external comparisons. Exercises C.78.3.1–C.78.3.2 check the shifted Hom sign and the full mixed/unit-output words. Editable SVG source.

C.79. Positive native inputs and fixed covariance

Positive common-input towers retain the full bar unit and every ordered pure-state cut. Their actual projection kernels lift the whole coherent native operator diagram. Changes of presentation must also transport, or preserve, each fixed product and graft map.

C.79.1. One positive common-input tower, with the actual pure maps

Let \(C=B\mathcal M\) be the fixed positive minimal IC bar of C34, \(U=\Omega C\), and \(v:U\to\mathcal G\) the actual strict dg generator quasi-equivalence constructed in Theorem C.68.4.1. Retain its finite additive matrix interpretation. For \(m\geq0\), set \[ \begin{gathered}V_m=\Omega(C^{\otimes m}),\\ P_m=T(U,\ldots,U).\end{gathered} \tag{C.79.1} \] At zero factors these are the coefficient category. Define \[ \begin{gathered}\xi_m:V_m\to P_m,\\ \xi_m=\Omega(\eta_C^{\otimes m}),\\ p_m:P_m\to U^{\otimes m},\\ p_m=(\epsilon_U^{\otimes m})\rho_m.\end{gathered} \tag{C.79.2} \] The first formula uses the augmented identification of \(P_m\) below; the second uses the actual counits and projection of C72 and C76.

Proposition C.79.1.1 (the actual positive state tower). These are strict dg mapping quasi-isomorphisms. The projection \(p_m\) is graded-surjective, and its actual kernel has a finite normalized linear contraction. The entire tower is positive on its reduced pure-state generators and satisfies \[ \begin{gathered}p_m\xi_m=\kappa_m,\\ \kappa_m:V_m\to U^{\otimes m}.\end{gathered} \tag{C.79.3} \] For an ordered root partition \(\pi\), its cut maps satisfy \[ \begin{gathered}\kappa_\pi^P\xi_m\\ \quad=(\bigotimes_j\xi_{I_j})\kappa_\pi^V,\\ (\bigotimes_jp_{I_j})\kappa_\pi^P=p_m.\end{gathered} \tag{C.79.4} \] Thus all pure-state ordered-root input squares agree exactly before any capacity or native full face is selected.

The actual geometric attachment is the strict dg quasi-equivalence \[ \begin{gathered}\chi_m=\zeta_{\mathcal G}T(v,\ldots,v)\xi_m,\\ \chi_m:V_m\to Q^{\mathrm u}(\mathcal G^{\otimes m}).\end{gathered} \tag{C.79.5} \] and its exact projection square is \[ \epsilon_{\mathcal G^{\otimes m}}\chi_m=v^{\otimes m}\kappa_m. \tag{C.79.6} \] All coefficient and zero-fold maps are their actual identities. The structural positive tower is strictly natural under the given pure coalgebra maps and their cobar powers, including the calibrated \(g\) and \(q=\Omega g\) of C48. No strict square for an attaching geometric comparison is asserted when that comparison is given only as a full \(A_\infty\) map; its actual higher comparison is retained separately.

Proof. The augmentation of \(U\) is its actual positive cobar augmentation. Its reduced mappings have degree at least two and are a dg ideal. Consequently the normalized quotient description of C74 is exactly \[ P_m=\Omega((B_{\rm red}U)^{\otimes m}). \tag{C.79.7} \] Indeed its free generators are tuples of nonempty reduced \(U\)-words, with the other factors empty. There are no scalar unary or binary outputs from this dg augmentation ideal. Its tensor bar differential and all proper tensor cuts are therefore precisely that augmented cobar differential. This is an equality of the actual free models, not an identification made only after taking cohomology.

The unit \(\eta_C:C\to B_{\rm red}U\) is a chain coalgebra quasi-isomorphism by Lemma C.39.4.1. Both reduced coalgebras have positive degrees. Its finite tensor powers remain quasi-isomorphisms by the split tensor contractions of C.30.1, and the positive cobar comparison clause of C.39.4.1 applies to them. This proves the assertion for \(\xi_m\). The actual projection \(p_m\) is graded-surjective by its pure one-letter generator values. C76's projection and C72's tensor counits make it a quasi-isomorphism. Its mapping kernel is acyclic; the coefficient-linear splitting argument of C.30.1 provides its normalized linear contraction. Alternatively its original-letter finite kernel contraction follows by the same filtered kernel construction as C75. The pure generators in \(P_m\) have degree at least two, since each reduced suspended \(U\)-letter has degree at least one. The same positive bound holds for \(V_m\) by C34 and C41.

Project \(p_m\xi_m\) on a generator of \(V_m\). If more than one original \(C\)-factor is noncoaugmented, every term has support in those factors and its \(\rho_m\)-projection is zero. If only factor \(i\) is noncoaugmented, the factor unit is the sum of all consecutive cobar blocks. Its actual counit keeps exactly its one-letter projection, the original \(\mathsf tc\) in factor \(i\). This is the defining generator formula for \(\kappa_m\). Coefficients agree. Extending by products proves the first exact square.

The same support calculation with groups proves \(\kappa_\pi^P\xi_m=(\bigotimes_j\xi_{I_j})\kappa_\pi^V\). A generator meeting two groups is killed on both sides. One supported in a single group has that same group's entire tensor unit on both sides. The factor units do not send a noncoaugmented element to a coaugmentation, so this support argument loses no unit term. C76's projection regrouping square, followed by the actual factor counits, proves the second ordered-cut identity. These are generator identities of strict dg functors, so hold on all words and with the actual matrix balancing signs.

For the geometric attachment, C74 gives the actual strict \(T(v,\ldots,v)\), and strict dg factor naturality in C76 gives \[ \begin{gathered}p_{\mathcal G}T(v,\ldots,v)\\ \quad=v^{\otimes m}p_m,\\ p_{\mathcal G}=(\epsilon_{\mathcal G}^{\otimes m})\rho_{\mathcal G}.\end{gathered} \tag{C.79.8} \] The right-hand composite is a mapping quasi-isomorphism, and \(p_{\mathcal G}\) is one by C72 and C76. Thus \(T(v,\ldots,v)\) is one as well. C76's \(\zeta_{\mathcal G}\) and the already proved \(\xi_m\) make \(\chi_m\) a mapping quasi-isomorphism. Its counit square follows by substituting the exact actual shuffle counit square of C76 and then the preceding two strict projection identities. No positivity of the intermediate geometric dg model or its unaugmented normalized resolution was used.

Finally the explicit unit is natural for a pure coalgebra map, its cobar is natural on every generator, and all projections use those same pure-factor twisting values. Thus the positive structural tower and ordered cuts are strictly natural under the actual \(g\) and the powers of \(q=\Omega g\). Its zero-fold instance is the coefficient identity. The finite additive extension uses the full matrix-unit balanced-tensor calculation in C.38.1, independently of any extra geometric comparison. This proves the proposition. \(\square\)

C.79.2. Full native lifting through the positive projection

Write \(A_m=U^{\otimes m}\). First retain the actual native diagram on these coefficient-linear enhanced input models, as in C.48.2, with the complete geometric interpretation supplied by C.68.4. The maps at this stage are full normalized unital \(A_\infty\) functors and full natural transformations. In particular they are not obtained by taking cohomology of the original native operators. Denote an original operator by \(F:A_a\to\operatorname{Add}(A_b)\).

For each such operator choose a lift \(\widetilde F:P_a\to \operatorname{Add}(P_b)\) with its fixed IC-sum object labels. The required projection identity is the equality of entire bar maps \[ Bp_b\,B\widetilde F=BF\,Bp_a. \tag{C.79.9} \] For an entire operator-word family \(\widehat\Theta\), let \(\Theta\) be its original native family. Its corresponding condition is the whole evaluation identity \[ \begin{gathered}Bp_b\operatorname{ev}(\widehat\Theta\otimes1)\\ \quad=\operatorname{ev}(\Theta\otimes Bp_a).\end{gathered} \tag{C.79.10} \] All original operator parameters remain on both sides. Thus this identity also specifies every mixed higher output, not just each separately marked natural transformation.

Proposition C.79.2.1 (the positive lift of the actual coherent native diagram). The supplied whole native diagram of C.47.2 has lifts through the \(p_m\)'s satisfying these identities. They retain its original joint index labels, its formal identities, every higher native composition cell and any already chosen compatible union of full generator faces. The construction applies to the single supplied calibrated two-endpoint comparison as well. On a pure comparison fiber its prescribed map is exactly \[ \begin{gathered}Q_m=T(q,\ldots,q),\\ p'_mQ_m=q^{\otimes m}p_m.\end{gathered} \tag{C.79.11} \] Here the primes denote the target positive models from C48; the second equation is exact strict-dg naturality. The assertion concerns the native operator diagram and its supplied higher comparison. It does not impose unwritten external-product or grafting equations.

Proof. The object map is fixed using the actual finite IC-sum decompositions. Proposition C.79.1.1 gives surjective quasi-isomorphisms on its mapping blocks, including their full relative matrix coefficients. The normalized functor \(Fp_a\) has a strict representative from \(\Omega B_{\rm red}P_a\). Its output is augmented: on \(r\) reduced inputs of degrees at least two, its output has degree at least \(2r+1-r=r+1\), so cannot be a coefficient identity. On the relative coefficient algebra use the actual prescribed identity map.

Lift this strict representative through \(p_b\) by C.46.2. Its free generator complex retains the entire unary differential of \(B_{\rm red}P_a\); its other differential terms use smaller original bar length. The normalized coefficient-linear contraction of \(\ker p_b\) therefore corrects the closed defect on that generator complex. Precomposing by the actual normalized bar-cobar unit gives \(\widetilde F\). The recovery triangle is exact, so its entire projection is \(Fp_a\), as required. The relative clause keeps a previously assigned differential-stable generator family. A formal identity is assigned \(1_{P_a}\), which has the required exact projection without any correction.

For two fixed lifts the full normalized Nat projection is \[ \begin{gathered}(p_b)_*:\\ \operatorname{Nat}_\infty(\widetilde F,\widetilde G)\\ \quad\longrightarrow\\ \operatorname{Nat}_\infty(Fp_a,Gp_a).\end{gathered} \tag{C.79.12} \] It is graded-surjective with acyclic actual kernel by C.66.3. The leading contraction postcomposes every source Taylor value with the mapping-kernel contraction of \(p_b\). It includes the complete source unary differential. Its remaining perturbation consumes a nonempty source piece. Hence its geometric series is finite on every original source word. This is the full Nat kernel; no assertion of acyclicity of the whole Nat space is being used.

Now order the original positive native index words by their number of nonidentity labels. Choose their free resolved parameter generators once, keeping every source Taylor component. Their lower faces are built from shorter original index words and the complete horizontal operation of C69. At a new generator take a graded lift of its supplied native value after source \(p_a\). Subtract its already assigned lower-face expression from its differential. The resulting defect has zero \((p_b)_*\)-image, because the native word satisfies its original equation and the lower words have their exact projections. Its differential is zero: expanding it gives the square-zero source parameter differential, the already established lower equations and the full C69 horizontal chain equation. Applying the Nat-kernel contraction corrects that defect.

This step is legitimate at changing frontier types. To see the essential closure, take two whole lifted families from \(a\) to \(b\) and from \(b\) to \(c\). Evaluate their composite by the nested evaluation formula of C.69.2. First apply \(Bp_c\) to the outer whole output. Its prescribed identity replaces that outer family by its native one evaluated after \(Bp_b\) on the entire inner output. The inner identity replaces the latter by its native evaluation after \(Bp_a\). The nested evaluation identity now gives precisely the native composite after \(Bp_a\).
