This works before projection to a single output, and therefore includes all higher marked and unit-output terms. There is no assumed tensor product of arbitrary \(A_\infty\) functors in this argument.

For a union of previously chosen full generator faces, the new defect vanishes on that union. Regard it as a map from the quotient generator complex and use the same output-kernel contraction. The correction then vanishes there too. In particular shared original block words receive their choice once; their later occurrences are restrictions. This is C.46.2's relative argument applied to the actual full Nat kernel, or equivalently C74's full boundary-kernel induction. It does not claim that arbitrary prescribed homotopy classes on unrelated faces extend.

Formal-identity slots have their normalized values. At an internal such slot the two neighboring source-composition terms are the same shorter positive word with opposite suspended signs. At an end the corresponding source face cancels the ordinary functor identity action. These are all terms meeting the identity slot, so the normalized extension satisfies its full equation. A positive original label whose native operator happens to equal the identity remains a positive parameter letter. It is never deleted or identified with a formal identity.

For the calibrated comparison use the one actual C48 two-endpoint diagram, with the endpoint retained in the type. Give a comparison arrow its additional positive endpoint height. Its positive words have exactly the same induction. On its pure comparison fibers fix \(Q_m\) above. Its projection square follows from Proposition C.79.1.1's strict naturality, so these prescribed free-generator faces already have the correct entire projection. The relative construction retains them. Every later native comparison cell is the lift of the given cell in this same two-endpoint diagram. It is not inferred merely from its bare components.

The native joint indices are locally forward finite by C64. For a fixed original input, source-word length and the number of original parameter letters bound all the perturbation/evaluation sums. Consequently the construction is one global assignment on original words; its finite forward corners and full faces inherit literal restrictions. The zero-frontier input is the coefficient category, while a nullary output still has its full target unit-object mapping module. These conventions also satisfy the same projection and lifting equations. This proves the proposition. \(\square\)

C.79.3. Fixed rational marks under a change of presentation

The following algebraic identity distinguishes a change made to both presentations from a correction made only to a comparison.

Proposition C.79.3.1 (transport every actual marked map). Suppose actual source and target presentations \(L,L'\) over \(k\) have differentials \(D,D'\) and specified maps \(\mu:L^{\otimes r}\supset X\to L^{\otimes s}\), \(\mu':(L')^{\otimes r}\supset X'\to(L')^{\otimes s}\). The domains are the complete specified domains. Let \(N:L\to\overline L\) and \(N':L'\to\overline L'\) be actual invertible presentation maps defined over \(k\), preserving the prescribed labels and windows. Transport every differential, domain and marked map, including all multi-input graft marks, by these same maps. If \(G:L_E\to L'_E\) is a simultaneous comparison over \(E\), then \[ \overline G=N'GN^{-1} \tag{C.79.13} \] is a simultaneous comparison of the transported presentations, which are still defined over \(k\). Its restrictions and leading coordinates are the corresponding transported ones.

In contrast, if \(A\) is only a chain automorphism of the target, then \(AG\) retains the original fixed graft marks precisely when \[ A^{\otimes s}\mu'=\mu'A^{\otimes r} \tag{C.79.14} \] on their actual domains. Chain compatibility alone is insufficient.

Proof. Set \(\overline D=NDN^{-1}\) and \(\overline\mu=N^{\otimes s}\mu(N^{-1})^{\otimes r}\), with domain \(N^{\otimes r}X\), and similarly on the target. The differential equality is \[ \begin{gathered}\overline D'\overline G=N'D'GN^{-1}\\ =N'GDN^{-1}=\overline G\overline D.\end{gathered} \tag{C.79.15} \] On the full transported domain, substitute the same inverse pairs into the marked-map equation. Write \(R=(N')^{\otimes s}\) and \(S=(N^{-1})^{\otimes r}\). This gives \[ \begin{gathered}\overline G^{\otimes s}\overline\mu\\ =R(G^{\otimes s}\mu)S\\ =R(\mu'G^{\otimes r})S\\ =\overline\mu'\overline G^{\otimes r}.\end{gathered} \tag{C.79.16} \] These identities retain every intermediate tensor factor. Degree-zero presentation maps introduce exactly the original graded tensor signs. They prove all marks simultaneously, including nullary marks. Their coefficients and the transported domains are over \(k\), since \(N,N'\) and both original presentations are. Any shared-face or window restriction preserved by these maps restricts the same equations. Leading components are obtained by taking the leading components in the same formula.

For the final assertion use the known equality \(G^{\otimes s}\mu=\mu'G^{\otimes r}\). The equality for \(AG\), followed by \((G^{-1})^{\otimes r}\) on its complete transported domain, is exactly the displayed covariance condition on \(A\). The converse follows by substitution. Thus an extension-field conjugate of the target marks cannot silently replace the fixed rational target marks in a descent problem. \(\square\)

C.79.4. Solved positive-unit, native-path and covariance calculations

Exercise C.79.4.1 (the nonprimitive unit term; intermediate). Let \(C=k1\oplus kc\oplus kd\), with degrees \(0,1,2\), zero differential and \(\overline\Delta d=c\otimes c\). Put \(U=\Omega C=T(x,z)\), where \(|x|=2,|z|=3\) and \(dz=x^2\). In \(P_1=\Omega B_{\rm red}U\), set \[ \begin{gathered}X=\mathsf t(sx),\\ Z=\mathsf t(sz),\\ Y=\mathsf t(s(x^2)),\\ H=\mathsf t(sx|sx).\end{gathered} \tag{C.79.17} \] Compute the unit image of \(z\), its differential and the failure of the formula which keeps just \(Z\).

Solution. The internal unary term of \(Z\) is \(Y\). For \(H\) the bar binary term is \(-Y\), since \(|sx|=1\), and its cobar cut term is \(+X^2\). Thus \[ \begin{gathered}DZ=Y,\\ DH=X^2-Y,\\ D(Z+H)=X^2.\end{gathered} \tag{C.79.18} \] The full coalgebra unit has \(\eta_C(d)=sz+sx|sx\), so \(\xi_1(z)=Z+H\). This is a chain map on the free generator \(z\), and therefore on the whole free dg algebra. The incomplete value \(Z\) has defect \(Y-X^2\), which is nonzero: a single generator with original \(U\)-letter \(x^2\) and a product of two generators are distinct basis words. The actual projection gives \(p_1Z=z,p_1H=0,p_1Y=x^2\), and hence \(p_1\xi_1(z)=z\). It detects neither a license to omit \(H\) nor equality of the two source basis words. \(\square\)

Exercise C.79.4.2 (a nonzero positive native path; advanced). Add a primitive \(e\) of degree three to \(C\). Its cobar generator \(w\) has degree four and zero differential. Let \(W=\mathsf t(sw)\) in the new \(P_1\). Define two functors from \(T(x,z,w)\), with \(dz=x^2\), by \[ \begin{gathered}F_0(x)=X,\\ F_1(x)=X,\\ F_0(z)=Z+H,\\ F_1(z)=Z+H,\\ F_0(w)=W,\\ F_1(w)=W+DH.\end{gathered} \tag{C.79.19} \] Construct their actual path lift and show why its third component cannot be dropped.

Solution. Both assignments are dg functors: the only nonzero generator differential was checked in Exercise C.79.4.1, and \(D(W+DH)=0\). Use the path dg category of C.50.3 on the identity object. Its maps are \((f,g,a)\), with \[ \begin{gathered}D\begin{pmatrix}f\\ g\\ a\end{pmatrix}\\ =\begin{pmatrix}Df\\ Dg\\ -Da+f-g\end{pmatrix}.\end{gathered} \tag{C.79.20} \] Send \(x,z,w\), respectively, to \[ \begin{gathered}(X,X,0),\\ (Z+H,Z+H,0),\\ (W,W+DH,-H).\end{gathered} \tag{C.79.21} \] On the last generator its third differential is \(DH+W-(W+DH)=0\). The image of the \(z\) differential is the square of the image of \(x\). Thus these assignments extend to a strict dg functor on the entire free input algebra. Its product third component, for homogeneous left input of degree \(r\), is \(a_2f_1+(-1)^r g_2a_1\); this determines all longer-word components and includes the actual unit \((1,1,0)\).

Both projections followed by \(p_1\) are exactly the identity input functor; the third component has zero \(p_1\)-image, since \(p_1H=0\). This is therefore an actual positive lift of one projected comparison. Dropping its third component on \(w\) leaves the nonzero third-slot defect \(-DH=Y-X^2\). Equality of the two projected functors alone does not supply that missing term. \(\square\)

Exercise C.79.4.3 (chain and coalgebra equations do not imply covariance; advanced). Let \(T^c(ka\oplus kb)\) have deconcatenation, \(|a|=1,|b|=3\), zero differential and its signed shuffle product. Let \(A\) be the cofree coalgebra map with primitive components \(A_1=1\), \(A_3(a,a,a)=b\), all its other nonlinear primitive values zero. Show that it is a degree-zero chain coalgebra automorphism with identity leading map, but does not preserve this fixed product.

Solution. Its full formula is the sum over consecutive partitions whose blocks are either single letters or the triple \(aaa\), replacing each such triple by \(b\). Cutting an output word is equivalent to cutting between two consecutive input blocks. This proves the coalgebra equation including the coaugmentation. Every nonlinear replacement lowers letter length by two and preserves degree, so the finite geometric inverse exists on every input word. The differential is zero, hence it and its inverse are chain maps. In particular \(A(a)=a,A(a|a)=a|a\) and \(A(a|a|a)=a|a|a+b\).

There are three signed shuffles of \(a\) with \(a|a\), with coefficients \(+1,-1,+1\). Therefore \[ \begin{gathered}a\mathbin{\operatorname{sh}}(a|a)=a|a|a,\\ A(a\mathbin{\operatorname{sh}}(a|a))\\ \quad=a|a|a+b,\\ A(a)\mathbin{\operatorname{sh}}A(a|a)\\ \quad=a|a|a.\end{gathered} \tag{C.79.22} \] Their difference is the nonzero primitive \(b\). Thus even the chain, coalgebra, inverse and leading-component conditions together do not imply the fixed-product equation of Proposition C.79.3.1. \(\square\)

Propositions C.79.1.1–C.79.3.1 prove the positive state tower, the full native projection lift and transport of fixed rational marks. Exercises C.79.4.1–C.79.4.3 compute the nonprimitive unit, a nonzero positive path and a shuffle-covariance counterexample. Editable SVG source.

C.80. Rational native coefficient descent

The full tree presentation, its actual native product and graft comparisons, and the rational coefficient descent are developed in Rational forest coordinates with units and nullary operations. Its Theorems 77–79 use the rational geometric collection and fixed cohomological target of C.48.1, including their actual tensor objects and universal classes.

C.80.1. The rational represented tensor comparison

Let \(\mathcal G_{\mathbf Q}\) be the rational spherical generator enhancement of C.27 and C.48, with finite IC sums as objects and with its specified ordered convolution functors \(F_n^G\). Let \(\mathcal H_{\mathbf Q}\) be its graded cohomology category with zero differential, the fixed rational decomposition maps and the cohomological tensor functors \(F_n^H\). Put \[ P_G(\mathbf x;y)=\operatorname{RHom}_{\mathcal G_{\mathbf Q}}(F_n^G\mathbf x,y), \qquad P_H(\mathbf x;y)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal H_{\mathbf Q}}(F_n^H\mathbf x,y). \tag{C.80.1} \] The arity-zero representing object is \(IC_0\). Its entire mapping complex, including positive-degree maps, belongs to this collection.

Theorem C.80.1.1. There is a normalized full tree comparison \[ F_{\mathbf Q}:P_G\longrightarrow P_H \tag{C.80.2} \] whose first map is a quasi-isomorphism on every represented profile and induces the fixed cohomology identity. It represents an enhanced strong monoidal equivalence between the finite coherent perfect envelopes of \(\mathcal G_{\mathbf Q}\) and \(\mathcal H_{\mathbf Q}\). For the specified symmetric input diagram, this equivalence is strong symmetric monoidal. Its tensor and unit classes are the actual cohomological ones.

Proof. The actual rational collection and all-profile leading calibration are Proposition 8 of the linked chapter. Its Theorem 9 identifies the full represented fan modules, on every original input and output word, and Theorem 17 retains their entire calibrated comparison. The native unary differential, binary graft and normalized three-vertex source package are Theorems 10–12; the prescribed two-vertex coefficient comparison is Theorem 13.

Theorems 71–76 retain the complete original execution indices, source changes, both endpoint maps, joint graft inputs and all labelled source and painted faces. Theorem 77 supplies one strict boundary row with its entire old comparison. The augmentation there acts only on the additional finite geometric parameter. Original bars, proper identity-valued parameters and ordinary identity outputs remain.

Theorem 78 extends through its exact represented-restriction kernel and evaluates every complete fundamental chain. For a tree with \(q\) vertices, the source and coefficient values have degrees \(2-q\) and \(1-q\), respectively. Full matrix products and genuine grafts precede primitive recovery. Stokes' equation gives the entire coderivation and comparison equations, including all source unary terms and all simultaneous target-block products. This constructs the native source over \(\mathbf Q\) and one calibrated full comparison over \(E\), with the source/comparison bounds \(3/2\) and the full fan packages fixed.

Theorem 79 then gives (C.80.2). Explicitly, rational minimal transfer gives \(I:M\to P_G\), \(J:P_G\to M\), with \(JI=1\). The entire field map \(g_E=\Phi I_E\) has first component \(1_H\). The compatible full unipotent windows of Theorems 1–3 give \(g_{\mathbf Q}:M\to P_H\), and \(F_{\mathbf Q}=g_{\mathbf Q}J\). These windows bound every connected-subtree boundary arity and retain nullaries and identity outputs. The field point remains related to this rational comparison by the full target automorphism \(a=g_E(g_{\mathbf Q}\otimes E)^{-1}\) and the comparison prism of Theorem 79. No rationality of its individual chosen higher coefficients is required.

The full represented recovery theorem, Theorem 4, applies to this whole comparison. For every tuple its tensor constraint is represented by the image of \(1_{F_n^G\mathbf x}\). All higher tree components give its naturality, substitution and unit coherence. At the empty tuple this is the actual identity of \(IC_0\). The first mapping map is a quasi-isomorphism and the generator labels agree, so the unary functor is a quasi-equivalence. C.23.5 and C.27 extend it, with its tensor constraints, to finite cones and coherent retracts. The fixed permutation equations give the stated symmetric compatibility. This proves the theorem. \(\square\)

C.80.2. Arbitrary characteristic-zero coefficients

Corollary C.80.2.1. For every characteristic-zero field \(L\), the actual finite-support \(L\)-coefficient spherical generator envelope has the strong cohomological tensor comparison obtained from (C.80.2) by coefficient extension and coherent idempotent completion. It induces the identity on its fixed graded collection. The symmetric compatibility holds for the specified symmetric diagram.

Proof. The prime-field inclusion gives \(\mathbf Q\to L\). The comparison of actual mapping objects with coefficient extension uses the finite pair models of C.26–C.27. At each group-nerve level they are finite perfect rational complexes. Their duals, evaluation and trace therefore commute with field extension. The uniform lower bound \(L_0\) of C.26.3 is independent of the nerve level. In total degree \(d\), levels greater than \(d+1-L_0\) contribute neither the relevant terms nor their incoming differential. Thus the finite-window totalization proof in C.29.4 compares the entire mapping objects after \(\mathbf Q\to L\). It does not commute tensor product with an unrestricted infinite product.

The ordinary and exceptional IC boundary tests in C.27 are the same finite restriction complexes. Exact field extension preserves them and their rank-one open coefficient, so it sends each rational IC generator to the actual \(L\)-coefficient IC generator. Lesson 11, Theorem 8.3, proves semisimplicity over this original characteristic-zero field: every spherical perverse object is a finite sum of those generators with finite-dimensional \(L\)-coefficients. Finite perverse truncations give every bounded finite-support object. Consequently the coherent perfect envelope after extension is the actual one, not just a fully faithful subcategory of it.

The same finite pair and finite-window argument applies to the ordered wall kernels and the moving configurations of C.27–C.29. It compares their actual proper and tensor operations. Their IC strict extension tests identify the actual geometric fusion components. Extend the entire rational functor and its constraints in (C.80.2) through these coefficient functors. Exact extension preserves all full tree equations, every finite cone and every specified coherent retract. The resulting comparison is therefore strong monoidal on the actual \(L\)-envelope, with the stated unit and symmetric compatibility. \(\square\)

11. Scope and free reading

Sections 2–7 establish the unit self-Ext formula,the invariant-polynomial classifying-space ring,the torus tensor model over characteristic-zero fields,the Koszul endomorphism and generated-category calculations,and the distinction between compact and bounded objects. The examples and exercises retain the specified shifts,coefficient fields and support conditions.

Appendix A develops stabilizer cohomology,equivariant Ext purity,minimal-model transfer,Frobenius formality and spherical generator envelopes. Appendix B treats the polynomial Kostant slice,the universal centralizer,equivariant coherent restriction and composition on free dual polynomial generators. Appendix C.1–C.29 develops the geometric generator mapping comparison,finite-jet and constant-group comparisons,the graded tensor cohomology functor,determinant and primitive cup operators,geometric Kostant modules,and the arithmetic enhanced symmetric monoidal finite-envelope equivalence. Its Betti and trait comparisons retain the full action nerves,trace normalizations and ordered convolution data.

Appendix C.30–C.79 develops the relative descent and coherence tools:directed finite coalgebra windows,common tensor cores,full nested functor graphs,bar-cobar and module contractions,formal unit/execution indices,parameter faces and shuffle domains. Relative represented-action recovery keeps the prescribed pure-state functors and their exact core powers. Whole one-cross restrictions have explicit homotopies to chosen product lifts. Coherent parameter families retain all higher components when normalizing selected product edges. Commuting ordered cut projections identify the actual sums and intersections of product-shuffle domains. On the stated chain submodels,a finite perturbation contracts the full relative Taylor kernel and permits closed comparisons and compatible homotopy primitives to extend globally. Compatible product actions extend by finite curvature correction,and ordered output-root induction gives module models with their prescribed product restrictions. The native central tensor retains every unit output and identity strand;an actual finest-domain comparison extends to transport the entire path differential. The exact common projection square and full represented evaluation construct that finest comparison for the specified native rootwise product families,retaining both actions and all higher source components. The full projection-square homotopy retains four correction terms,and one actual finest primitive suffices to normalize all prescribed compatible ordered cuts. The reverse path projection lifts entire coherent families with exact projection-compatible edges;its canonical return formula retains the original raw comparisons and their kernel homotopies. Full bar-unit mapping restriction preserves the entire transformation cohomology and records the prescribed square for one specified native product family. Relative restriction retains genuine full faces when the corresponding relative transformation class is supplied. A supplied compatible entire common path lifts to native modules with the original first family fixed;its identity-cone correction retains assigned faces and every higher generator. Global locally forward finite root indices support one fixed-profile product normalization whose finite-corner and full-face restrictions agree on their intersections. The full joint-execution grafting domain has its original bar map; complete product shuffles lie in it exactly under the outer-final/inner-initial prerequisite condition. Entire coherent diagrams in a specified dg category admit explicit full-string transport and strictly associative staged model contraction, retaining their path comparisons. Typed kernel cotensors preserve their intermediate frontier cores, and the actual canonical-state projection has an acyclic full Nat kernel for relative coherent operator lifting. Canonical cobar sources admit an actual dg retraction to strict operator objects, and full marked postcomposition carries entire higher model-change diagrams. Actual dg model bridges retain geometric object representatives and give relative fixed-outer-type native operator diagrams without requiring source augmentations. Full marked evaluation gives entire associative horizontal substitution, retaining the mixed cochain homotopy and nonlinear model-change terms. A full-differential relative contraction preserves the complete split source image and yields exact unit comparisons for transport across changing intermediate types. The actual native joint diagram has normalized formal units, retains every positive index label, and carries its supplied full comparison through the model bridges. Normalized unital cobar models retain actual scalar constants and give strict dg operator objects with exact composition and full unit naturality. Their full transformation restriction has an exact section, a contracted kernel and an entire projected horizontal comparison. Full tensor-parameter categories and relative coherent cube extensions retain prescribed compatible boundaries and all original unary and unit data. Their actual binary tensor projection has a finite kernel contraction, and the full shuffle gives a common unital tensor input with the exact counit square. Finite ordered families share exact regrouping and multishuffle squares, with one contraction compatible with all ordered tensor cuts. Entire projected evaluation is preserved under composition, yielding compatible strictly unital native sequential operator cubes with their full parameter restrictions. Full tensor-unit mapping restriction retains all transformation classes and primitives, and its exact tensor squares lift supplied native external comparisons. Positive native input towers and whole projection lifts retain the original native higher cells; fixed rational product and graft marks have their separate covariance equations.

Appendix C.80 and its linked chapter establish the full native source and painted-cell evaluations, the calibrated rational strong monoidal comparison and its extension to arbitrary characteristic-zero coefficient fields. Their shared inputs retain the entire profile-changing execution and external grafting diagrams, all unary and nullary data and every simultaneous target partition. The quantum/loop-rotation,renormalized,singular-support and Ran/factorization equivalences of Section 8 require arguments beyond the results established here.
